contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: Matching Support to the Right Stage
contentBlocks.body:
The three programmes IB Gram sees requests for around Vasant Vihar are the Primary Years Programme for ages 3 to 12, the Middle Years Programme for ages 11 to 16, and the Diploma Programme for ages 16 to 19. Each one needs a different kind of tutor, and conflating them is one of the more common mistakes parents make when searching casually online.

A PYP student rarely needs subject drilling. What helps most is gentle reading support, numeracy confidence and someone who can talk through the current unit of inquiry without turning it into a worksheet exercise. Push too hard on content at this stage and a young learner can lose interest in the inquiry approach that PYP is built around.

MYP sits in between. A Grade 8 or Grade 9 student in Vasant Vihar might be capable in class but struggle to turn a broad classroom project into criterion-ready work, because MYP assessment rewards specific things: using command-term language correctly, showing process, meeting the actual rubric rather than just producing a good answer. A tutor who only knows content, not MYP's assessment criteria, misses half the job.

DP is the most demanding stage and the one most families search for directly. Here the tutor needs subject depth at the HL or SL level requested, comfort with IA structure and timing, and enough exam-paper familiarity to run realistic Paper 1, 2 or 3 practice without guessing at format.

For a PYP learner, it is often simpler: more willingness to read independently, or less resistance to a particular subject.

If none of that is visible by week four, it is worth raising directly with IB Gram rather than waiting it out. Tutor fit does not always work on the first try, and that is not a failure on the family's part. A tutor who explains Physics well one-on-one is not automatically the right personality fit for a reserved twelve-year-old, and a switch at that point is a normal part of the process, not an admission of failure.

contentBlocks.heading: Firefighting Before Mocks vs. Building the Whole Year
contentBlocks.body:
Two very different requests land on IB Gram from Chanakyapuri households, and they need different answers. The first is urgent: a Grade 11 student two weeks from a Physics HL mock, parents wanting someone who can walk through past papers immediately. The second is quieter — a family that wants a tutor attached to a subject from the start of the year, checking IA drafts as they're written rather than fixing them after a first low mark. Chanakyapuri's mix of diplomatic postings and international school enrolment means both patterns show up constantly, sometimes in the same household across two children.

Neither approach is wrong, but they call for different tutors. A firefighting engagement works best with someone who already knows the syllabus cold and can diagnose gaps in a single session — useful, but it rarely changes how a student studies day to day. Year-long support costs more in total hours and asks more of the family's calendar, but it catches an EE research question drifting off-topic in October rather than in April. Delhi's cross-city traffic makes this choice practical, not just pedagogical: a tutor coming from across town for one urgent session before finals is realistic; the same tutor committing to a weekly evening slot for eight months needs a route that actually holds up over a full term. IB Gram asks about both the academic gap and the logistics before suggesting a match, because a plan that ignores the commute usually collapses by November.

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Between a Tutor Who Visits and One Who Doesn't
contentBlocks.body:
Delhi families most often land on a hybrid answer rather than picking one mode outright. A younger child working through Middle Years Programme units might do better with someone physically present twice a week, correcting notebook habits and keeping a distractible student on task. A Grade 12 student preparing Math AA HL past papers, on the other hand, usually cares more about whether the tutor genuinely knows the syllabus than whether that tutor lives fifteen minutes away — and the strongest subject specialist for Math AI or Economics HL essay structure may simply not live near Chanakyapuri at all.

Home tutoring works when the commute is honestly workable for both sides — not just possible on paper, but something a tutor will still show up for reliably in month four of a Delhi winter with morning fog delays. When that isn't realistic, online tutoring is not a compromise; for many Delhi families it's the better fit, because it opens up the pool to tutors anywhere who match the exact subject and level needed, rather than only those within a plausible driving radius. Screen sharing handles most IB content well — annotated past papers, IA outlines, TOK presentation slides — though a student who needs constant redirection to stay focused may genuinely do better in the same room as their tutor. That's a real trade-off: online buys subject depth and schedule flexibility; in-person buys presence and structure. Most Chanakyapuri households end up using both at different points in the year.

contentBlocks.heading: What Chanakyapuri Students Actually Ask for Help With
contentBlocks.body:
The subject requests IB Gram receives from Chanakyapuri and its neighbouring areas follow a fairly consistent pattern. Math AA HL comes up constantly, usually from students who managed Grade 10 without much trouble and then find the jump in abstraction hard to place — calculus proofs, vectors, and paper 3 investigation-style questions that reward a different kind of thinking than school tests measured before. Math AI HL requests tend to come from students who want the applied, technology-heavy route done properly rather than as a fallback from AA, and the two need genuinely different teaching approaches even though the topic labels overlap.

Physics and Chemistry HL/SL both bring a mix of concept gaps and lab-report anxiety — IA data analysis is where most of the actual tutoring time goes, more than raw content teaching. Economics is its own category: strong theoretical understanding but essay structure that loses marks on evaluation and diagrams, which is a writing problem as much as an economics one. English A requests are less about vocabulary and more about argument construction under exam time pressure — students who can discuss a text well in class but freeze when asked to build a Paper 2 comparative essay from scratch in forty-five minutes. Across Grade 1 to Grade 12, the earlier grades ask for something different again: steady subject-by-subject confidence building rather than exam technique, because there's no exam yet to aim at.

contentBlocks.heading: From PYP Habits to Diploma Programme Deadlines
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram supports all three programme stages relevant to Chanakyapuri families, and each one needs a different kind of tutor, not a smaller version of the same one. Primary Years Programme support, for ages 3 to 12, is mostly about building study habits and subject confidence early — reading fluency, number sense, curiosity about the units of inquiry — rather than anything that resembles exam coaching. Getting this wrong by hiring someone who teaches like it's already Grade 10 tends to backfire; young PYP students disengage fast from anything that feels like drilling.

Middle Years Programme, ages 11 to 16, is where assignment planning starts to matter more than it did before — MYP personal projects, criterion-based assessment, and the first real experience of structured deadlines a student has to manage somewhat independently. A tutor here needs to understand MYP's assessment criteria specifically, not just the subject content, because a well-written piece of work can still lose marks against criteria it didn't address. Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19, is the stage most Chanakyapuri enquiries are actually about: subject depth at HL or SL, IA supervision that respects what the school's own supervisor already said, EE mentoring that keeps a research question narrow enough to answer well, and TOK support that connects a knowledge question to real subject examples rather than abstract philosophy. Moving between these stages, the constant is that a tutor's job shifts from building foundations to managing deadlines to defending marks against assessment criteria — three different skills housed in one word, tutoring.

contentBlocks.body:
It's worth saying plainly what IB Gram does not promise. No tutor can guarantee a particular grade or a 7, and any platform that says otherwise is telling a Chanakyapuri parent what they want to hear rather than what's true. A tutor can improve how well a student understands Math AA HL calculus, how clearly an Economics essay evaluates a policy, how methodically an EE research question gets narrowed down — but the final outcome still depends on the student's own effort between sessions, the school's own assessment of coursework, and factors outside any tutor's control.

There's a real limitation worth naming here too: a tutor starting six weeks before a May 2026 exam can sharpen technique and close specific gaps, but cannot rebuild two years of missed foundations in that window. Families sometimes ask for exactly that, and the honest response is to say what's realistic in the time available rather than accept the engagement and let it under-deliver quietly. What IB Gram can commit to is process: a tutor matched on actual subject and programme background, a first session that diagnoses rather than assumes, a week-four check to see if the plan is working, and a straightforward path to switching tutors if it isn't. That's a narrower promise than guaranteed results, but it's the one that holds up when a parent asks a hard question on a phone call.

The honest answer for Greater Kailash is that home tutoring is realistic for some pockets and some hours, and online tutoring fills the rest - especially once a family wants a specific subject specialist rather than whoever happens to be available nearby. IB Gram treats that as a starting brief, not a limitation to work around quietly. A student in Grade 9 preparing for MYP assessments needs a different weekly rhythm than a Grade 12 student three months from May 2026 finals, and the matching process below is built to separate those cases rather than offer one generic slot. What follows covers how matching works, which programmes and subjects are supported, and where the honest limits of home tutoring in this part of Delhi actually sit.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Matches a Tutor to Your Child
contentBlocks.body: The process starts with a short conversation, not a form to fill and forget. A parent tells IB Gram the student's grade, programme - PYP, MYP or DP - subject or subjects, and what triggered the search: a mock result, an IA deadline, or simply a new school year. From there, IB Gram checks tutor qualifications, subject depth at the right level (Math AA HL is not the same teaching job as Math AI SL), and whether the tutor has handled a similar case before, such as a student switching boards mid-way or one rebuilding a weak Chemistry foundation before Paper 2. A shortlist is offered, not a single name pushed through. The family picks based on fit - teaching style, schedule, sometimes even language of instruction - and a first session is arranged. That first session is diagnostic: the tutor reviews recent test papers or IA drafts, asks about school pace, and sets a realistic four-week plan rather than promising a fixed outcome. At the four-week mark, the plan is reviewed against what actually happened - did the student start submitting drafts earlier, did confidence in Paper 1 problem-solving improve, is homework getting done without daily reminders. If the match isn't working, IB Gram treats that as information, not failure, and looks for a better fit rather than asking the family to push through a bad pairing out of politeness.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Support, Matched to Age and Stage
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram supports the Primary Years Programme (ages 3 to 12), Middle Years Programme (ages 11 to 16) and Diploma Programme (ages 16 to 19), covering Grade 1 through Grade 12 for Delhi families. The needs at each stage look different enough that treating them the same would be a mistake. A PYP parent usually wants steady support with reading, number sense and the inquiry-based projects the programme is built around - less about exam pressure, more about not falling behind on units of inquiry. MYP families start to feel graded pressure: criteria-based assessment means a Grade 8 or Grade 9 student is being marked against specific descriptors in each subject, and a tutor who can explain those descriptors saves weeks of confused revision. DP is where the stakes visibly change - Math AA or AI at HL or SL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A all carry external exams in May 2026 or November 2026, plus internal assessments, an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge that run alongside regular coursework. A Grade 11 student choosing between Math AA and AI, or deciding HL versus SL load, benefits from a tutor who has actually taught the difference rather than repeating a general rule. IB Gram's matching accounts for this: a PYP tutor and a DP Economics tutor are not interchangeable, and the process treats programme stage as a primary filter, not an afterthought applied after subject.

contentBlocks.heading: Home Sessions, Online Sessions, and the Honest Trade-off
contentBlocks.body: Home tutoring in Greater Kailash and neighbouring pockets like Defence Colony, Hauz Khas and New Friends Colony is possible, but it depends on the tutor's own location and how much South Delhi traffic a session can absorb without eating into study time. A 6 PM slot that looks fine on paper can turn into a tutor arriving fifteen minutes late every week once evening traffic near the surrounding arterial roads builds up. That's not a reason to avoid home tutoring - many Greater Kailash families use it successfully for younger students who benefit from in-person attention - but it is a reason to be realistic about which hours are sustainable, not just which hours look convenient in a schedule. Online tutoring solves a different problem: it removes the commute entirely and opens up subject specialists who may not live anywhere near South Delhi at all, which matters more for something like Math AA HL or a specific Economics essay-writing gap than for general homework supervision. Delhi families increasingly choose a hybrid setup - a home tutor for younger children or subjects needing close supervision, online for DP-level subject depth or when a school mock exposes a gap that needs a specialist fast. IB Gram doesn't push one mode over the other; the honest limitation is that home tutoring availability depends on tutor location and cannot be guaranteed for every pocket or every hour a family wants.

Physics and Chemistry requests usually arrive after a mock exposes a specific weakness - often Paper 2 data analysis in Physics, or organic mechanisms in Chemistry - rather than as a general request for help. Economics tends to be about essay structure and evaluation technique as much as content; students who know the theory still lose marks on Paper 1 and Paper 2 for weak evaluation paragraphs, and that's a teachable, specific skill. English A support in Greater Kailash often comes from families whose child is a confident reader but an inconsistent writer under exam conditions - the gap between a strong practice essay and a rushed Paper 1 commentary. contentBlocks.heading: What Should Be Visible After Four Weeks
contentBlocks.body: Trust in tutoring is built from specifics, not reassurance, so here is what a Greater Kailash parent should reasonably expect to see, not just be told. In week one, the tutor should be able to name what the student is weak in - not generically, but as in 'struggling to structure Paper 2 evaluation paragraphs in Economics' rather than 'needs to work harder.' By week two, homework or practice questions should be specific to that gap, not a generic worksheet pulled from a shared folder. By week four, there should be some visible change: a student attempting a past paper section unprompted, an IA draft that moved from a vague thesis to a checkable one, or simply fewer arguments at home about starting the work. None of this is guaranteed on a fixed timeline - a student rebuilding two years of Math foundation needs longer than four weeks, and IB Gram doesn't pretend otherwise. What is reasonable to expect is transparency: a tutor willing to say plainly if progress is slower than hoped, and why, rather than vague reassurance every week. Parents should also expect to be told when a subject needs more than tutoring can fix alone - occasionally a student needs a school conversation about deadline extensions, or a diagnostic assessment for something unrelated to teaching quality. A tutor who only ever says things are going well, regardless of what the actual work shows, is not a good sign.

Rather than a fixed rate card, IB Gram shares specific tutor pricing once your grade, subject and mode of tutoring are known, because a Math AA HL tutor three months from May 2026 exams and a PYP reading tutor are not comparable services. Ask for a clear breakdown before committing to weekly sessions.

mainEntity.name: What happens if the tutor and my child just don't click?

acceptedAnswer.text: It happens, and it isn't treated as a failure on either side. If a match isn't working after a fair trial - usually a few sessions, enough to judge teaching style and not just a bad day - tell IB Gram directly rather than persisting out of politeness for a full term. A new tutor is proposed based on what didn't work the first time: pace, communication style, or even something as simple as personality fit for a teenager who needs more independence than a younger student would. Changing tutors mid-year is more common than families expect and doesn't restart the process from zero.

mainEntity.name: Does online tutoring actually work for something like Chemistry, which needs practical understanding?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most Chemistry topics at DP level - mechanisms, calculations, exam technique for Paper 1 and Paper 2 - online tutoring works well, since the core challenge is usually conceptual understanding and practice under timed conditions rather than lab access, which the school already provides. Where online is genuinely weaker is hands-on lab technique itself, though that's a small part of the assessed content compared to written papers. Most Greater Kailash families use online tutoring for Chemistry theory and problem-solving, and rely on the school for lab components, which is a reasonable and common split.

mainEntity.name: Are there tutors who work with students from schools in Chanakyapuri or Saket?

acceptedAnswer.text: IB Gram is not affiliated with The British School New Delhi, the American Embassy School or DPS International Saket, but many families searching from Greater Kailash do have children attending IB programmes at schools in that Chanakyapuri-Saket cluster. Where possible, IB Gram proposes tutors who have prior experience with students from a similar school context - comparable pace, comparable homework load - because that familiarity tends to matter more in practice than a general IB credential. Mention your child's school during the first conversation so this can be factored into the shortlist rather than assumed.

mainEntity.name: My child is switching from CBSE to the IB Diploma - can a tutor help with that transition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it's a common enough request that tutors experienced with it are specifically flagged during matching. The main adjustment isn't content difficulty so much as assessment style - IB rewards structured argument, evaluation and process over memorised answers, which catches CBSE-trained students off guard in subjects like Economics and English A especially. A tutor who has handled this transition before will usually spend early sessions on how to answer IB-style questions, not just teaching syllabus content the student may already partly know. Starting this conversation a term before Grade 11 subject choices lock in gives more room to adjust than starting after.

mainEntity.name: How soon before May 2026 exams should we start, if we're only now looking?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends heavily on the gap being addressed - a Grade 12 student needing exam technique and past-paper practice can see meaningful movement in two to three months, while one rebuilding a genuinely weak foundation in Math AA HL needs longer than that and should be told so honestly. Starting now, even a few months out, is still worth doing since focused revision on specific weak areas - IA polish, a particular Paper 2 topic, essay structure in Economics - moves faster than general teaching. What isn't realistic is expecting a full HL subject rebuilt from scratch in six weeks; a tutor should say this plainly rather than promise otherwise.

mainEntity.name: Can one tutor cover both Math AA HL and Physics, or do we need two separate tutors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Occasionally one tutor covers both if their background genuinely supports it, but it's more common and usually better to have separate tutors for Math AA HL and Physics, since strong exam-level teaching in each requires different depth. A tutor stretched across two HL sciences or a science-and-Math combination they haven't specifically taught at that level often ends up weaker in one than the other. IB Gram would rather match two specialists than one generalist stretched thin, even though managing two schedules is slightly more work for a family - it's a trade-off worth knowing about upfront.

mainEntity.name: What does a first session actually cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first session is diagnostic, not a jump straight into teaching. The tutor typically reviews recent test papers, an IA draft if there is one, or simply asks about school pace and where the student feels stuck, then sets a realistic plan for the next few weeks rather than a vague promise of improvement. Parents are usually included briefly at the start and end of this session to align on goals - exam technique, IA structure, general confidence - so everyone is working toward the same specific outcome rather than assuming it's obvious.

mainEntity.name: Is IB Gram affiliated with the IB Organization or with schools like the American Embassy School?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and has no official affiliation with the International Baccalaureate Organization, or with schools such as The British School New Delhi, the American Embassy School or DPS International Saket, unless specifically stated for an individual tutor's own background. The platform matches independent tutors to families based on subject, grade and IB programme familiarity; it does not represent, certify, or act on behalf of the IB Organization or any listed school in any capacity.

finalCta: If you're weighing a home tutor in Greater Kailash against an online specialist for Math AA HL or DP Economics, start with a short conversation about your child's grade, subject and timeline. IB Gram will shortlist tutors based on that, not push a single default option, with availability depending on subject and schedule.

introSummary: If you're searching for IB tutors in Saket Delhi, the honest answer is that the right fit depends on the programme, the subject, and how much travel a family can sustain on a school night. IB Gram works with tutors across PYP, MYP and the Diploma Programme, covering Grade 1 through Grade 12. Some Saket families arrange home sessions; many more use online tutoring for stronger subject depth, especially in Math AA/AI, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A, with IA, EE and TOK support built in rather than bolted on.

contentBlocks.heading: What Changes in a Student's Study Routine Between Grade 6 and Grade 12
contentBlocks.body:
A Grade 6 student in the Middle Years Programme and a Grade 12 student staring down DP mocks are solving different problems, even if both technically need 'a tutor.' The younger student is still building habits — how to keep a subject notebook, how to break a project into stages, how to ask a question in class instead of nodding along. The older one already knows how to study; what she needs is someone who can read an IA draft and say, specifically, where the analysis thins out, or explain why a Paper 2 essay lost marks on structure rather than content.

This difference matters more in a place like Saket than it might elsewhere, because school timings across South Delhi vary enough that a family cannot assume a fixed evening slot will work every week. A tutor who adapts pacing to the week's actual homework load, rather than running a fixed syllabus regardless of what's due, tends to hold a student's attention longer. For MYP students, that often means shorter, more frequent check-ins on unit tasks. For DP students preparing for the May or November 2026 sessions, it means blocking longer sessions around IA deadlines and mock exam weeks.

Choosing a tutor for a Grade 7 student is therefore a different exercise than choosing one for a Grade 12 student, even when both families type the same search term.
items: MYP students (Grade 6-10): habit-building, unit task pacing, subject notebooks
DP students (Grade 11-12): IA feedback, Paper 1/2/3 technique, mock analysis
Saket-area school timings vary, so fixed weekly slots aren't always realistic
Younger students need structure; older students need targeted correction

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB Subjects Saket Families Ask About Most
contentBlocks.body:
Most enquiries from Saket and the surrounding South Delhi pockets cluster around a familiar set: Math AA HL and Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A. The pattern is not surprising. Math AA HL is where the widest range of ability shows up in one classroom — a student comfortable in Grade 10 board maths can suddenly find HL calculus and vectors moving faster than the school can slow down for one child. Math AI HL causes a different kind of trouble: the applications context, finance and statistics modelling, confuses students who are strong at pure computation but weak at translating a word problem into the right approach.

Physics and Chemistry tutoring in Saket is usually requested alongside IA support — a student is fine with the theory but needs someone experienced with the IB's specific data-analysis and evaluation criteria, not just the content. Economics tuition tends to be about essay structure: how to build an evaluative argument for a Paper 2 case study rather than simply defining terms. English A support is less about grammar and more about how to build a comparative literary argument that an IB examiner will actually credit.

None of this is unique to struggling students. Ordinary, capable students hit these exact walls every year, and a subject specialist who has taught the IB syllabus specifically tends to close the gap faster than a generalist tutor working from a general board framework.
items: Math AA HL: calculus, vectors, proof-based reasoning
Math AI HL: applications, statistics, financial modelling
Physics and Chemistry: IA data analysis and evaluation criteria
Economics: Paper 2 evaluative essay structure
English A: comparative literary argument building

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Pairs a Saket Family With the Right Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
The matching process starts with specifics, not a general form. A parent tells IB Gram the student's grade, programme, subject or subjects, current level of difficulty, and roughly how much time is left before the next school deadline or mock exam. That detail matters more than it sounds — a Grade 11 student six weeks from mocks needs a different tutor profile than a Grade 9 student just starting an MYP Individuals and Societies unit.

From there, IB Gram shortlists tutors whose subject background and exam-board familiarity match the request, factoring in whether the family wants home tutoring, subject to a tutor's ability to travel into or near Saket, online tutoring, or a hybrid mix. The shortlist is not the same for every family asking for 'a Math tutor' — it depends on HL versus SL, on whether the concern is content or exam technique, and on schedule constraints the family has already flagged.

A first session is deliberately diagnostic. The tutor reviews recent schoolwork, asks the student to work through a problem or short passage live, and forms a view of where the actual gap sits, which is often different from what the parent assumed on the phone. That first-session finding shapes the plan for the following weeks, and it is reviewed again around the four-week mark to check whether pacing and tutor fit are genuinely working, not just assumed to be.
items: Step 1: share grade, programme, subject and timeline
Step 2: shortlist by subject depth and exam-board familiarity
Step 3: diagnostic first session, not a generic intro class
Step 4: four-week review of pacing and fit

contentBlocks.heading: Saket, South Delhi Pockets and Where Home Tutoring Actually Works
contentBlocks.body:
Saket sits inside a cluster of South Delhi neighbourhoods that IB Gram sees requests from regularly — Defence Colony, Hauz Khas, New Friends Colony, Panchsheel Park, Green Park and Jor Bagh. Families in these pockets often ask the same underlying question in different words: can a tutor realistically reach us on a weeknight without losing half the session to traffic?

The honest answer is that it depends on where exactly, and at what hour. A tutor based near Saket can often manage a 6 or 7 pm slot in Panchsheel Park or Green Park without much trouble. Reaching Chanakyapuri or Vasant Vihar from the same starting point at peak evening traffic is a different proposition, and families in those areas often find online tutoring gets a specialist into the session on time, every time, rather than gambling on Ring Road congestion.

This is also why hybrid arrangements are common in this belt — weekday sessions online for consistency, with an occasional in-person session when a tutor's schedule allows it, particularly ahead of a mock or a submission deadline. For families slightly further out, in Gurugram, Noida or Ghaziabad, online tutoring is usually the default rather than the fallback, simply because a reliable weekly home-tutoring commute across NCR is hard to promise honestly.
items: Nearby: Defence Colony, Hauz Khas, New Friends Colony, Panchsheel Park
Also nearby: Green Park, Jor Bagh
Higher-traffic reach: Chanakyapuri, Vasant Vihar — online often more reliable
NCR families (Gurugram, Noida, Ghaziabad): online is usually the default

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: What Support Looks Like at Each Stage
contentBlocks.body:
Primary Years Programme tutoring for a Saket family with a Grade 1 to Grade 5 child rarely looks like 'tutoring' in the conventional sense. It's more often a steady half-hour of reading fluency, number sense or inquiry-project support, aimed at keeping a young learner curious rather than drilling worksheets. Parents sometimes arrive expecting exam prep and are relieved to hear that isn't what a good PYP session should be.

Middle Years Programme support, roughly Grade 6 to Grade 10, shifts toward subject depth and the MYP's own assessment criteria — command terms, criteria-based rubrics, and the personal project in the upper MYP years. A tutor unfamiliar with how MYP grades against criteria, rather than simple right-or-wrong marking, will misjudge where a student actually stands.

Diploma Programme tutoring, Grade 11 and 12, is the most demanding to get right, because it has to track six subjects, three core components, and two possible exam sessions. A DP tutor working with a Saket student needs to know the difference between HL and SL demands in that subject, understand how the IA is internally assessed and externally moderated, and be comfortable walking through TOK exhibition or essay expectations without treating TOK as an afterthought.

None of these stages benefits from a one-size tutor. The programme changes what good support actually means.
items: PYP (ages 3-12): reading, number sense, inquiry support
MYP (ages 11-16): criteria-based assessment, personal project
DP (ages 16-19): six subjects, IA/EE/TOK, HL vs SL depth
Exam sessions: May 2026 and November 2026

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Is Recommended
contentBlocks.body:
Before a tutor is put forward for a Saket family's request, IB Gram checks a specific set of things: subject qualification and academic background, prior experience teaching the IB curriculum specifically, as opposed to a general board like CBSE or ICSE with an IB label added on, and familiarity with the exact course — Math AA is not Math AI, and a tutor comfortable with one is not automatically comfortable with the other.

This matters because IB assessment language is specific. A tutor who can't explain the difference between a Paper 1 and Paper 3 command term, or who has never actually read an IA rubric, will teach content correctly but miss where marks are lost. That gap shows up in mock results, not in a first impression.

Verification is not a one-time badge. If a subject match turns out weaker than expected once actual sessions begin, which does happen because tutoring is not a perfect science, IB Gram treats that as a signal to review the pairing, not something the family has to quietly live with. A parent who feels a session isn't landing should say so early rather than after three months, because the fix is usually a subject or pacing adjustment, not a bigger problem.

None of this guarantees a particular grade. It's a filter for competence and fit, not a promise of outcome.
items: Subject qualification and academic background reviewed
IB-specific teaching experience checked, not just general tutoring history
Exact course match verified (for example AA vs AI, HL vs SL)
Ongoing review if a pairing isn't working, not a one-time check

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or a Mix: Deciding What Actually Suits Saket
contentBlocks.body:
Three modes come up in almost every Saket enquiry: home tutoring, online tutoring, and a hybrid of the two. Each has a genuine trade-off, not just a marketing angle.

Home tutoring works best when a student needs someone physically present to catch handwriting habits, keep a younger child on task, or when a family simply prefers in-person structure. Its limitation in this belt is honest and practical: it depends entirely on whether a suitably matched tutor can reach the specific pocket at the specific time slot the family needs, and Delhi's evening traffic doesn't cooperate with every request.

Online tutoring removes the travel constraint entirely, which is exactly why it tends to win for subject specialists — a strong Math AA HL or Economics tutor based across town, or even outside Delhi, becomes available the moment travel isn't the deciding factor. It also holds up better for short, intensive revision cycles before a mock, when a family needs a session booked within days, not weeks.

Hybrid support is what many Saket families settle into by the second month: weekly online sessions for consistency and subject depth, with home sessions reserved for occasions where in-person genuinely adds value, such as before a major internal assessment deadline. There is no universally correct choice here. It depends on the subject, the student's age, and how firm the family's evening schedule actually is.
items: Home tutoring: in-person structure, limited by travel and traffic
Online tutoring: wider access to subject specialists, faster to schedule
Hybrid: online for consistency, home sessions around key deadlines
Choice depends on subject, student age and schedule firmness

contentBlocks.heading: Schools Around Saket and Chanakyapuri, and Where IB Gram Stands
contentBlocks.body:
Saket itself is home to DPS International Saket, and families in the wider South Delhi and Chanakyapuri belt often reference The British School New Delhi and the American Embassy School when describing their child's curriculum and cohort. These references are useful shorthand — they tell a tutor roughly what pace, assessment style and cohort expectations the student is working within — but IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any of these schools unless specifically stated for a particular arrangement.

What this means in practice: a tutor matched to a DPS International Saket student isn't drawing on privileged access to that school's internal papers or teachers. They're drawing on general IB curriculum experience, familiarity with how that kind of school typically paces the syllabus, and the ability to adapt to whatever specific assignment or mock the student brings to a session.

Parents sometimes ask whether IB Gram can guarantee a tutor who has taught at their exact school before. Usually, no, and it would be dishonest to promise that as standard. What can be arranged is a tutor experienced with the same programme, similar subject combinations, and comparable assessment expectations, which in nearly all cases matters more than school-specific familiarity.

The British School New Delhi — Chanakyapuri

contentBlocks.heading: What a Parent Should See by Week Four
contentBlocks.body:
Trust in a tutoring arrangement shouldn't rest on a sales pitch. It should rest on what's visible after a month of actual sessions. By week four, a parent in Saket should be able to point to something concrete: a student who now attempts a Physics IA draft without freezing, a Math AI HL worksheet completed with fewer careless errors, or an English A paragraph that finally makes a defensible comparative point instead of just describing two texts side by side.

If that concrete change isn't visible by then, that's information, not failure. It usually means one of three things: the subject match needs adjusting, the pacing is wrong for the student's current school workload, or the gap is bigger than a weekly session alone can close before the next deadline. IB Gram treats a stalled month as a prompt to review the pairing, not a reason to keep going unchanged and hope.

One honest limitation worth stating plainly: tutoring cannot compensate for a student starting IA work six weeks before a May 2026 submission with almost nothing drafted. A tutor can help structure what's left, but there is a ceiling on what any tutor can rebuild that late. Starting the conversation earlier, even a term earlier, changes what's realistically possible far more than switching tutors mid-crisis ever will.
items: Concrete week-4 signals: fewer errors, a completed IA draft, better structured essays
No visible change by week 4 means reviewing pairing, subject match or pacing
Late starts, weeks before a submission, limit what any tutor can fix
Earlier conversations matter more than switching tutors under pressure

contentBlocks.heading: Starting With a Saket Tutor Search This Term
contentBlocks.body:
Starting is simpler than most families expect. It begins with a short conversation about the student's grade, current programme, the specific subject or subjects causing concern, and how much time is left before the next school deadline, mock exam, or the May or November 2026 session. That single conversation shapes everything that follows — the shortlist, the mode (home, online or hybrid), and how the first session is structured.

For a Grade 12 student six weeks from mocks, that first conversation might lead straight into an IA review and a Paper 2 practice plan. For a Grade 3 student who has lost confidence in reading, it might lead to something much gentler: twenty minutes of paired reading, three times a week, with no pressure attached.

Fees and scheduling are discussed upfront and depend on the subject, the grade level, and whether the arrangement is home-based or online; nothing is fixed without the family seeing the specifics first. A tutor being suggested doesn't mean the family is locked in — the first session works as much as a check for the family as it does a diagnostic for the tutor, and either side can flag early if the fit feels wrong.

The practical next step is telling IB Gram what's actually needed: not a general enquiry, but the grade, the subject and the timeline.
items: Share grade, programme, subject and timeline to start
Fees and mode discussed upfront, nothing fixed in advance
First session works as a two-way check, not a lock-in
Arrangements are subject to tutor availability and schedule fit

faqs.question: How much does an IB tutor in Saket cost?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the subject, grade level, HL versus SL, and whether sessions are home-based or online — there's no single number that applies across Math AA HL, English A and PYP reading support alike. Home tutoring in South Delhi typically costs more than online sessions once a tutor's travel time is factored in. IB Gram shares specific fee ranges once the grade, subject and preferred mode are known, rather than quoting a flat rate upfront that wouldn't reflect what the family actually needs.

faqs.question: Can a tutor really travel to Saket for home sessions given Delhi traffic?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and sometimes not — it depends on where the tutor is based relative to Saket and what time slot the family needs. A 5 pm weekday slot is far more workable than a 7:30 pm one after peak traffic sets in across South Delhi. IB Gram checks travel feasibility as part of matching rather than assuming it will work; if home tutoring isn't realistic for a given slot, online tutoring is suggested instead, without treating it as a downgrade.

faqs.question: Is online IB tutoring actually as effective as home tutoring?
faqs.answer: For subject-heavy work like IA feedback, Paper 2 essay structure or Math AA HL problem sets, online tutoring often works better, because it opens access to a stronger subject specialist regardless of where they are based. It's less ideal for a young PYP learner who needs more hands-on redirection. Most Saket families land on a mix: online for older, subject-focused students, and home or hybrid sessions for younger children who need someone physically present to hold attention.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor isn't the right fit for my child?
faqs.answer: It happens, and it isn't treated as a failure on either side. IB Gram reviews the pairing — sometimes the subject match was right but the teaching pace wasn't, sometimes the personality fit was off. A different tutor is proposed based on what the first session actually revealed, rather than starting the matching process over from scratch. Families are encouraged to flag a mismatch within the first two or three sessions rather than waiting months and hoping it improves on its own.

faqs.question: Do you offer tutors specifically for Math AA HL and Math AI HL in Saket?
faqs.answer: Yes — but they aren't interchangeable, so it helps to know which course your child is actually enrolled in before requesting a tutor. Math AA HL leans toward pure calculus, proof and abstract reasoning, while Math AI HL is built around applications, statistics and modelling. A tutor strong in one isn't automatically strong in the other. IB Gram matches based on the specific course, not just 'IB Maths' as a general label, since that distinction changes what a session actually needs to cover.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP, not DP yet — is tutoring worth starting this early?
faqs.answer: It can be, particularly if MYP unit tasks or the personal project are already causing stress, because MYP habits carry directly into DP demands two or three years later. It isn't necessary for every MYP student, though — a child coping fine with school pace doesn't need weekly tutoring just because DP is coming eventually. IB Gram would rather have that honest conversation upfront than sign a family into sessions the student doesn't actually need at this stage. A first conversation about actual difficulty level costs nothing to have.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover multiple subjects for my child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, especially at the PYP or early MYP stage where a generalist tutor can competently handle overall academic support across several subjects. By DP level, this gets harder — Physics HL and Economics HL, for instance, need genuinely different subject specialists, and a single tutor claiming deep expertise in both is worth questioning. IB Gram usually recommends one subject specialist per DP subject rather than stretching a generalist across a Grade 12 student's full course load.

faqs.question: How does IB Gram handle IA and EE support without doing the work for the student?
faqs.answer: The line is enforced deliberately. A tutor reviews structure, argument, referencing and how well a draft matches IB assessment criteria — pointing out exactly where analysis is thin or a claim isn't supported — but the writing and thinking stay the student's own. This matters for both academic integrity and for what the student actually learns. A tutor who simply rewrites a paragraph for a student produces a better paragraph and a weaker student, which isn't the goal of an IA or EE mentoring session.

faqs.question: What if my child needs help right before May 2026 mocks with very little time left?
faqs.answer: Short, intensive revision cycles are common in the weeks before mocks, and IB Gram can arrange focused sessions around a specific weak paper or topic rather than a full-syllabus restart. What's honest to say upfront: a tutor starting two weeks before mocks can sharpen technique and close specific gaps, but can't rebuild a subject from zero in that window. Families closer to the November 2026 session, with more runway, generally see more room for a broader revision plan.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram affiliated with DPS International Saket or the schools nearby?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform, not affiliated with DPS International Saket, The British School New Delhi, the American Embassy School or any other school referenced on this page, unless a specific arrangement states otherwise. Tutors are matched based on programme and subject experience relevant to a school's typical curriculum pace, not on any privileged relationship with that school. Parents comparing schools for context should verify current details directly with each school rather than relying on general tutoring platforms.

contentBlocks.heading: What Vasant Vihar Families Actually Ask For
contentBlocks.body: Vasant Vihar is one of the pockets in Delhi where IB tutoring demand runs high, largely because of the embassy community nearby in Chanakyapuri and the concentration of international-school families across South Delhi. When parents here start looking for IB tutors, the first real question is not who is available, but which format suits the situation. Online tutoring genuinely does more than most families expect: it opens access to a specialist Physics or Economics tutor who may live in Gurugram or Noida but can still run a focused evening session without anyone sitting in traffic. It also makes short, intense revision blocks before school mocks far easier to schedule. Where online falls short is with younger children, roughly Grade 1 to Grade 6, who often need a tutor physically present to hold attention and build habits, and with subjects where a shared notebook and real-time diagram work faster face to face. Home tutoring in Vasant Vihar and nearby South Delhi pockets can be reviewed depending on a tutor's own location and travel radius; it is not guaranteed for every request, and families should expect this discussed honestly during matching rather than promised upfront. Grades run 1 to 12 here, with support available for both the May 2026 and November 2026 exam sessions. IB Gram treats home and online as two different tools, not one wrapped inside the other, and works out which one, or which mix, actually fits before assigning anyone.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or a Mix: How Vasant Vihar Families Choose
contentBlocks.body: Delhi families often default to assuming home tutoring is the serious option and online is the fallback. That is not how it plays out in practice. A family in Vasant Vihar with a Grade 11 student on Math AI HL might do better with an online specialist who teaches that syllabus every week, rather than a generalist who can reach the house in twenty minutes. Conversely, a Grade 4 student building reading stamina under the Primary Years Programme usually benefits more from someone sitting beside them at the table, correcting pacing in real time, than from a screen. Home tutoring may be possible in select South Delhi, central Delhi and nearby residential pockets, subject to a tutor's own travel radius and schedule; it is reviewed case by case rather than guaranteed, because Delhi traffic between Vasant Vihar and further-out parts of the city can eat an hour each way that neither the tutor nor the family wants to lose. Online tutoring is available across Delhi for every supported IB programme and subject, which matters when a family needs a specific specialist rather than whoever happens to be nearby. Many Vasant Vihar households end up on a hybrid plan: a home session on weekends when schedules allow, and an online slot midweek for a subject where consistency matters more than presence. Neither format is inherently better; the right one depends on the student's age, the subject, and how much the family's week can actually bend.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Depth: Math AA, Math AI, Sciences and Beyond
contentBlocks.body: The subjects Vasant Vihar families ask about most are Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A, and each pulls a slightly different kind of tutor. Math AA HL needs someone comfortable with proof-based reasoning and harder calculus and functions content, not just someone who can run through past papers. Math AI HL leans more applied, and a tutor who teaches it well usually structures sessions around modelling and technology use rather than pure algebra drills. Physics and Chemistry at HL or SL both hinge on how comfortable a student is translating a word problem into the right equation before calculating anything, which is where a lot of Grade 11 and 12 students quietly lose marks. Economics tutoring in Delhi tends to focus heavily on essay structure and diagram accuracy for Paper 1 and Paper 2, since IB examiners reward argument structure as much as content knowledge. English A support usually splits between the literary analysis expected in written tasks and the oral commentary skills tested separately. A tutor who is strong in one of these is not automatically strong in all of them, so IB Gram treats subject matching as its own step rather than assuming a generalist can cover the full list. For a Vasant Vihar family, naming the exact subject and level up front, HL or SL, shortens the matching process considerably and avoids a mismatch further down the line.

English A: written tasks plus oral commentary preparation

contentBlocks.heading: From PYP to the Diploma: What Changes at Each Stage
contentBlocks.body: The Primary Years Programme, roughly ages 3 to 12, is less about subject mastery and more about building the inquiry habits and written fluency that later IB work assumes are already in place; a tutor at this stage is often doing as much work on attention span and curiosity as on any specific topic. The Middle Years Programme, ages 11 to 16, is where subject-specific gaps start to matter, and where a student moving between schools or curricula mid-year can genuinely fall behind without anyone noticing until a report card says so. The Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19, is the stage most Vasant Vihar families are searching for tutors about, and it carries its own vocabulary: Internal Assessments, an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, and externally set Paper 1, 2 and sometimes Paper 3 exams sat in May or November. A Grade 11 student starting DP subjects fresh has different needs from a Grade 12 student six weeks from mock exams, and a tutor who is good with one is not automatically good with the other. IB Gram's grade range for this area runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12, and a family should expect the intake conversation to start with which of these three stages the student is actually in, since that decides almost everything else about pacing, tone and what a first session should cover.

contentBlocks.heading: What Actually Breaks When a Tutor Handover Goes Wrong
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor leaving mid-year is more disruptive in the IB than in most other systems, and Green Fields families feel this early. A CBSE tutor change mostly costs a few weeks of syllabus revision. An IB change costs more: a Math AA HL student loses the specific way a tutor was building command-term fluency, an IA draft sits half-annotated, and a TOK essay loses whoever understood the earlier drafts. The new tutor has to reconstruct not just what was taught, but how the student was taught to think about criteria.

This matters because Green Fields, sitting near Surajkund and close to the Badarpur border, draws families comparing local home support against the deeper DP specialist pool across Delhi and Gurugram. A parent switching from a local generalist to an online HL specialist mid-course needs the handover done properly, not just a new name added to a WhatsApp group. IB Gram treats a tutor change as a structured event: the new tutor reviews the student's actual IA drafts, recent mock scripts and school feedback before the first paid session, not after three sessions of guessing.

The honest limitation: a mid-year switch during exam season rarely produces the same result as starting the relationship a full term earlier. Families should expect a short adjustment period, not instant continuity, however good the new match is.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP to Diploma: How the Tutoring Need Changes
contentBlocks.body:
The Primary Years Programme, running roughly from age 3 to 12, asks for a different kind of tutoring support than most parents expect from the word 'tuition'. A PYP tutor in Green Fields is usually helping with reading fluency, numeracy or a unit-of-inquiry project, not drilling a syllabus — the programme is built around concepts and inquiry rather than content coverage, and a tutor who does not respect that will fight the school's own method.

The Middle Years Programme, for ages 11 to 16, is where criterion-related assessment starts to matter directly. An MYP student does not just need to know content; they need to turn a broad classroom topic into work that visibly meets specific criteria, using the command-term language the school actually grades against. A tutor unfamiliar with MYP criteria will coach the wrong thing well.

The Diploma Programme, for ages 16 to 19, is where subject-level choice (HL or SL), IA structure, EE mentoring and TOK become the daily reality. IB Gram treats this as a hard boundary in every match it makes for Green Fields families, not a soft suggestion.

contentBlocks.heading: The Assessment Calendar Behind the Tutoring Decision
contentBlocks.body: Most tuition searches start with a subject name. In the IB system, the assessment calendar should come first. A Diploma Programme student working toward the May 2026 or November 2026 session is not simply revising a syllabus; they are building an Internal Assessment, refining an Extended Essay draft, keeping a Theory of Knowledge exhibition or essay on schedule, and practising Paper 1, 2 and sometimes Paper 3 formats that reward specific command terms like 'evaluate' or 'discuss' differently. A tutor who ignores that structure and simply re-teaches the textbook ends up misaligned with what the school and the IB Organization actually grade. For Grade 1 to Grade 12 students in Neharpar and Greater Faridabad, this matters at every level, not only in the Diploma years. A Primary Years Programme child is assessed against units of inquiry, not test scores in the traditional sense. A Middle Years Programme student is marked against published criteria bands, so a tutor's real value is teaching a student to read a criterion rubric and produce work that satisfies it honestly. Academic honesty is not a side note here; command-term literacy and independent work are part of what the IB checks. In practice, the families we see in Neharpar want Math AA or AI, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English writing support most often, and the tutoring plan usually gets built backward from the next IA deadline or mock date.

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Between a Home Tutor and an Online DP Specialist
contentBlocks.body: Neharpar sits within Greater Faridabad, close to Sector 86, and it is still a growing residential corridor rather than an established, easy-to-navigate part of the city. That matters when you are deciding between a home tutor and an online specialist. A home tutor can work well for a younger PYP or early MYP student who needs someone physically present to build reading habits, keep a workbook routine and hold a fixed session time. But travel here is not always simple. Traffic patterns around Greater Faridabad and connecting roads can make a strict weekly home schedule harder to sustain than it looks on paper, and a tutor's realistic travel radius often does not stretch evenly across every pocket of a growing sector. This is where online tutoring earns its place, not as a fallback but as the stronger option for specific needs. A Diploma student working at HL in Math or Physics, needing IA structure feedback at short notice, or wanting a doubt cleared before a Sunday mock, is usually better served by an online specialist who does not depend on road conditions to show up on time. Hybrid plans are common in Neharpar for exactly this reason: a home tutor handles routine and accountability, while an online subject specialist covers HL depth, IA review and exam-season continuity. Which mix makes sense depends on the student's age, subject level, and how firm the family's weekly schedule actually is.

contentBlocks.heading: The Subjects Neharpar Families Ask About Most
contentBlocks.body: Ask ten Neharpar parents what their child needs and Math usually comes up first, but the specifics matter. Math AA HL and Math AI HL are different subjects in practice, not just different labels; a tutor comfortable teaching calculus proofs for AA may not be the right fit for AI's applied, technology-based problem sets, and matching the wrong one wastes months. Physics and Chemistry bring their own pressure points, particularly around the Internal Assessment: a lab-based IA needs a tutor who can question a student's method and variables without writing the report for them, since that crosses into academic honesty territory. Economics IA work leans on real-world commentary tied to syllabus concepts, which is a different skill from solving a diagram-based Paper 1 question. Biology students often need help connecting content across topics for Paper 3's data-based questions. English A support usually centres on close reading and building an argument that survives a marker checking against assessment criteria, not on grammar drilling. Beyond subjects, the recurring requests we see from this area are structural: IA planning from first draft to final wording, Extended Essay mentoring on research question framing, TOK exhibition and essay support, review of school-set assignments before submission, timed past-paper practice, and mock exam preparation. Parents also ask for visibility, not just results, which is why a workable plan includes parent-visible weekly goals rather than a vague promise that a student is 'doing fine.'

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: What Changes at Each Stage
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram covers the Primary Years Programme (ages 3 to 12), the Middle Years Programme (ages 11 to 16), and the Diploma Programme (ages 16 to 19), and the tutoring approach changes meaningfully at each stage. A PYP tutor in Neharpar is mostly supporting a unit of inquiry: helping a seven-year-old ask better questions, build reading stamina, and connect a home reading habit to whatever transdisciplinary theme the school is running that term. There is no exam pressure here, so the job is confidence and curiosity, not test drilling. MYP shifts the target toward criteria. A Grade 8 or Grade 9 student is now marked against published achievement level descriptors in each subject, and a tutor's job is to teach the student to read those descriptors and produce work that visibly satisfies them, across subjects from Math to Individuals and Societies to Sciences. This is also the stage where independent work habits get built before DP arrives. DP is where the stakes and the structure both jump. Subject levels split into Higher Level and Standard Level, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay become compulsory components alongside six subjects, and the Internal Assessment in each subject carries real weight toward the final grade. A family choosing a DP tutor in Neharpar for the May 2026 or November 2026 session needs someone who has taught that subject at HL or SL before, not a confident generalist unfamiliar with how IB actually grades it.
items: PYP (3-12): inquiry, reading habits, no exam pressure
MYP (11-16): criteria-based marking across subjects
DP (16-19): HL/SL split, TOK, EE and IA all compulsory

contentBlocks.heading: Steps From Enquiry to First Session
contentBlocks.body: When a Neharpar family submits a request, IB Gram first looks at four things: the programme level, the exact subject and level (HL or SL where relevant), the preferred mode of home, online or hybrid, and the realistic weekly schedule around school timings. That combination narrows the pool to tutors whose subject background and exam-board familiarity actually fit, rather than sending every request to whoever is available first. A suggested tutor is shared with the family along with relevant background, and the family decides whether to proceed to a first session, not the platform. The first session itself is not a sales pitch. A competent tutor uses it to check the student's current level against the syllabus, look at any past assessment or IA feedback already available, and agree on what the first few weeks will focus on. This gets written down in plain terms so the parent knows what 'progress' should look like, rather than hearing a vague reassurance. Around the four-week mark, IB Gram expects a parent to see something concrete: a completed diagnostic, an IA outline or draft in progress, a clearer sense of where the student's command-term weaknesses are, or at minimum a specific, named plan for the weeks ahead. If none of that has happened, that is a signal worth raising, not something to sit on quietly. If the fit turns out to be wrong, IB Gram can review a change of tutor. Switching is not treated as a failure on the family's part; a mismatch caught early costs far less time than one carried through an entire term.

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before Any Match Is Suggested
contentBlocks.body: Trust here should not rest on a badge or a star rating; IB Gram does not publish tutor counts or manufactured ratings, and it will not promise a specific grade or a guaranteed 7. What it can do is describe the checks plainly. Before a tutor is suggested for a Neharpar family, their subject background is reviewed against the specific level requested, whether that is MYP Individuals and Societies or DP Physics HL, because subject-adjacent is not the same as subject-qualified. Familiarity with IB's own language matters as much as subject knowledge: command terms, criterion-related assessment, and the IB Organization's academic honesty policy are not optional extras a tutor picks up later. A tutor who does not understand the difference between guiding a student's IA and writing sections of it is a liability, however strong their subject knowledge looks on paper. IB Gram also asks tutors to work within that boundary explicitly, and expects parents to raise it if a tutor's approach ever feels like it is crossing into doing the work rather than teaching the student to do it. Here is an honest limitation: no vetting process can fully predict classroom chemistry between a specific tutor and a specific teenager, and the first session exists precisely because paperwork cannot substitute for watching someone teach. Availability for any given subject or level is real but not fixed; it depends on tutor schedules at the time of the request, which is why matches are reviewed and subject to availability rather than promised in advance.

Subject background checked against the specific level, not just 'IB experience'
Command terms and academic honesty policy treated as core knowledge
IA guidance stops at teaching, never at writing the assessed work
Availability is reviewed per request, not promised in advance

contentBlocks.heading: How a Parent Can Verify Things Independently
contentBlocks.body: A sensible parent does not take a match on faith, and IB Gram does not expect anyone to. Before committing, it is reasonable to ask a suggested tutor directly which specific level they have taught before, ask for an example of how they would structure a first month for the subject in question, and ask how they distinguish IA guidance from IA writing in practice. A tutor who cannot answer that last question clearly is worth reconsidering, regardless of how confident they sound about content. IB Gram supports this by keeping contact and scheduling details visible to the family so a first session can be arranged directly and confirmed before it happens, rather than through a black box. During the trial period, a parent's own observation is the real verification step: does the tutor reference the actual syllabus and command terms the student's school uses, or generic content pulled from any board's textbook? Does a written plan from week one match what the student experiences in week three, or has it quietly drifted? For younger PYP and MYP students in Neharpar, a parent sitting in on part of an early session, even online, is a reasonable and normal request, not an overstep. For DP students who want more independence, a fortnightly summary of what was covered and what the next IA or paper-practice milestone is works better than sitting in. If a tutor resists any form of visibility into what a session actually covered, treat that as information, not paranoia.

contentBlocks.heading: Getting Started From Neharpar
contentBlocks.body: Starting is meant to be simple, even though the decision behind it is not always simple. A Neharpar family typically starts by being specific rather than general: not 'we need an IB tutor' but 'Grade 11 DP Physics HL, IA due in eight weeks, prefer online with one home session a fortnight if possible.' That level of detail is what lets IB Gram narrow the match quickly instead of sending a generic subject teacher who happens to be free. From there, expect a suggested tutor with relevant background, a conversation before anything is confirmed, and a first session that produces a written starting point rather than a vague good first impression. If the student is younger, PYP or early MYP, it is fine to start broader, since the early sessions themselves will surface exactly where support is needed. Timing matters more than families sometimes realise: starting DP IA support in the final month before a deadline limits what any tutor can do, however good they are, because an IA needs drafting and revision time built in, not a rescue attempt at the end. Starting three to four months before a mock session or an IA deadline gives a tutor room to actually improve the work rather than just polish it. For Neharpar specifically, deciding on mode early, home, online or hybrid, saves a few weeks of back-and-forth later, since it changes which tutors are realistically available to match against.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor even practical for Neharpar, or should we just go online?
faqs.answer: It depends on the exact pocket and the student's age. Compact areas near Sector 86 with reasonable road access can work for a home tutor, particularly for a younger PYP or MYP student who benefits from a fixed in-person routine. Further into Greater Faridabad, or where traffic on connecting roads is unpredictable, a strict weekly home slot becomes harder to sustain, and a DP student needing HL depth or IA support is usually better matched with an online specialist anyway. Many Neharpar families end up on a hybrid plan rather than choosing one mode outright.

faqs.question: What does IB tutoring actually cost, and does it change by subject?
faqs.answer: Fees are not fixed here; they depend on the tutor's experience, whether the subject is HL or SL, whether sessions are home, online or hybrid, and how many hours a week are needed. A DP HL specialist subject typically costs more per hour than a PYP inquiry-support session, and home tutoring in Neharpar can carry a premium tied to travel. Rather than quoting a flat number that would not hold true for every case, IB Gram shares specific tutor rates once your grade, subject and mode are known, so you are comparing an actual quote, not a generic estimate.

faqs.question: My child is starting IB a term late compared to classmates in Neharpar schools. Can a tutor fix that?
faqs.answer: A tutor can close a real gap, but timelines depend on the size of it and how many months remain before the next assessment window. A term behind in MYP is very fixable with a focused eight-to-ten-week plan. A term behind in DP, especially close to IA submission or mock exams, limits how much ground can be covered safely without sacrificing depth for speed. Be wary of anyone who promises to fully close a large DP gap in a few weeks; the honest answer is usually a prioritised plan covering what will actually be assessed first.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for something like a Physics or Chemistry IA that needs lab work?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the parts that matter most, which are the thinking and the write-up, not the physical apparatus itself. A student typically runs the practical component at school, and the tutor's real value is in the IA design conversation beforehand, the data analysis and evaluation afterward, and making sure the write-up reflects the student's own reasoning. Online works well for this because it is largely a screen-and-document conversation. Where online genuinely struggles is hands-on lab troubleshooting in the moment, which is why some families prefer a hybrid setup for science subjects specifically.

faqs.question: What if we start with a tutor and it just isn't working after a few sessions?
faqs.answer: Say so early rather than waiting out the term hoping it improves on its own. IB Gram can review a change of tutor if the subject fit, teaching style or scheduling genuinely is not working, and switching early costs far less than persisting with a mismatch through mocks or an IA deadline. Before switching, it helps to be specific about what is not working: is it subject depth, communication style, punctuality, or pace? That detail lets the next match actually correct the problem instead of repeating it with a different name attached.

faqs.question: Is there a real difference between an IB tutor and a normal CBSE or ICSE tutor for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and it is not about intelligence or teaching skill in general. IB assessment runs on command terms, criterion bands and internally assessed components like the IA and TOK, which most CBSE or ICSE tutors have simply never had to teach against. A Physics tutor who is excellent at solving numericals for a board exam may not know how an IB Physics IA is actually marked, or what 'evaluate' requires versus 'explain.' It is worth asking directly whether a prospective tutor has taught IB specifically, and for which subject levels.

faqs.question: How much weekly time should we realistically budget for a DP subject like Math AA HL?
faqs.answer: There is no single right number, since it depends on the student's current level and how close the next assessment is, but two structured hours a week per HL subject is a reasonable baseline outside intensive periods. Around IA deadlines or the months before May or November exam sessions, that often needs to increase temporarily, sometimes to three or four hours for a subject the student is struggling with. What matters more than the raw hour count is consistency: two hours every week beats six hours crammed into one session before an assessment.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover multiple DP subjects, or do we need a different specialist for each?
faqs.answer: Usually a different specialist per subject at HL, and possibly at SL too, because genuine depth in, say, Physics HL and Economics HL rarely lives in the same person. Some tutors comfortably cover two related SL subjects, such as Biology and Chemistry, but claims of covering four or five DP subjects at a strong level are worth questioning closely. For a Neharpar family managing multiple tutors, hybrid or online scheduling usually makes coordination easier than fitting several home visits into one evening.

faqs.question: Do you only work with specific schools in Faridabad, or can any student join?
faqs.answer: Any student pursuing PYP, MYP or DP, Grade 1 through Grade 12, can request a match, regardless of which school they attend. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not officially affiliated with any particular school in Sector 15, Green Fields, Neharpar or elsewhere in Faridabad unless that is explicitly stated. References to school clusters describe the local student population a tutor is likely to have worked with already, which can shorten the settling-in period, but it is not a partnership claim.

faqs.question: What actually happens in that first session, and is it a real class or just an assessment?
faqs.answer: It is a working session, not a sales conversation, though it does double as an assessment of fit. Expect the tutor to check where the student currently stands against the syllabus, look at recent school feedback or IA drafts if any exist, and agree on specific goals for the first few weeks in writing. You should walk away from it knowing what will be covered next, not just whether the student 'liked' the tutor. If that clarity is missing, it is reasonable to ask for it directly before committing.

introSummary: If you're searching for IB tutors in Sector 15, Faridabad, you're probably choosing between a home tutor who can visit after school and an online specialist for a tricky DP subject. IB Gram is an independent platform that reviews each request — grade, programme, subject, timings — before suggesting a match, rather than assigning whoever is free. Sector 15 sits close to Sector 16 and Ajronda, both within easy reach for home visits, while online tutoring stays useful for HL subjects, IA support and the run-up to May and November exam sessions. This page explains how that decision actually gets made.

contentBlocks.heading: What a First Session in Sector 15 Actually Covers
contentBlocks.body: A first session for a Sector 15 family should feel less like a sales pitch and more like a diagnostic. Before anything is scheduled, IB Gram asks for the student's grade, programme — PYP, MYP or DP — subject, current school assessment pattern and what's actually going wrong: exam technique, conceptual gaps, or falling behind on IA deadlines. That information shapes who gets suggested, not the other way round. When the first session happens, whether at home in Sector 15 or over a video call, the tutor should spend the opening twenty minutes listening rather than teaching: reviewing recent school work, asking the student to explain a concept in their own words, and checking command-term literacy, because a DP student who cannot distinguish 'evaluate' from 'discuss' will lose marks regardless of subject knowledge. By the end of that first hour, a parent should have three things: a plain-language note on where the student actually stands, a realistic view of what four weeks of consistent sessions can achieve, and a session plan that names specific topics rather than vague revision. If a tutor cannot produce that after a first session, treat it as a signal to ask for a different match rather than push through. Families in Sector 15 comparing IB Gram against a walk-in coaching centre should notice this difference immediately: there's no fixed timetable to fit into, and the plan is built around what the student's school and exam session actually require.

Command-term check within the first session

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Pairs a Tutor to Your Sector 15 Request
contentBlocks.body: Matching starts with the request itself, not a list of names to browse. A parent in Sector 15 tells IB Gram the grade — anywhere from Grade 1 to Grade 12 — the programme level, the subject, and whether the concern is conceptual (a Grade 8 MYP student who understands the topic in class but freezes on assessed criteria) or exam-specific (a Grade 12 DP student six weeks from a May or November paper). That request is checked against tutor subject background, DP experience at HL or SL, and realistic travel or availability before any name is suggested. This matters more for IB than for a board syllabus, because IB tutoring depends on understanding concept-based learning and criterion-related assessment, not just subject content — a tutor strong in CBSE maths will not automatically know how MYP criterion D or a DP IA is actually graded. Once a match is proposed, the family gets a short profile: subject background, which programme levels the tutor has handled, and suggested mode — home, online or hybrid — based on the request. Nothing is locked in before a first session. If the fit is wrong after that session, IB Gram treats it as normal and revises the match rather than asking the family to persist through a bad pairing. For Sector 15 specifically, home-tutor matching also weighs how far a tutor can reasonably travel; a tutor based near Ballabhgarh may prefer online sessions with a Sector 15 family purely on travel time, and that trade-off is disclosed upfront rather than discovered after two sessions.
