Name the exact course when you enquire. A request that only says maths tutor will produce a shortlist that has to be rebuilt once the level becomes clear, which costs a week.

mainEntity.name: What does IB tutoring near DLF Phase 4 cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fees vary by level, subject and format rather than sitting at one fixed rate. Diploma Higher Level subjects and internal assessment mentoring cost more per hour than Middle Years support, because fewer tutors can do that work well. Home sessions usually carry a premium over online ones, since the tutor is giving up travel time. An advisor can share indicative ranges for your specific combination before any session is arranged, and you should ask about cancellation terms and session length at the same time.

mainEntity.name: How soon can sessions start if my child's internal assessment is due in three weeks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often within a few days, though it depends entirely on subject and tutor availability. Be honest about the deadline in the first message, because a three-week IA brief goes to a different tutor from year-long support and needs someone with a free slot immediately. Expect the first session to be spent reading the draft and the criteria rather than teaching content. The tutor will question the research focus and flag criteria the draft has skipped. Writing remains the student's own work throughout.

mainEntity.name: My child is in MYP and school grades look fine. Is a tutor premature?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily, though the reason for starting should be clearer than a vague worry. Middle Years grades can look comfortable while the underlying habits stay weak, particularly around criterion-related tasks where a student describes rather than analyses. If reports repeatedly praise effort while marking down one criterion, that is a real gap worth addressing before Diploma content arrives. If everything is genuinely solid, occasional sessions in the term before DP subject choices may serve you better than weekly tutoring now.

mainEntity.name: Does IB Gram have any connection with Lancers International or Scottish High?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with any school named on this page unless specifically stated. Schools are mentioned because families around Phase 4 attend them and the commute affects which session times are realistic. Some tutors have worked with students from these schools and understand their assignment patterns, which is useful context. It does not amount to endorsement, partnership or any arrangement with the schools, their staff or their management.

mainEntity.name: What if we see no change after a month?

acceptedAnswer.text: Say so early instead of waiting out the term. At roughly four weeks there should be something specific to point at: cleaner structure in written answers, fewer method slips, work handed in before the deadline rather than on the night. If none of that is visible, the likely causes are a mismatch of teaching manner, a wrong reading of the gap, or sessions scheduled when the student is already exhausted. Any of the three can be corrected, and a different tutor can be shortlisted.

mainEntity.name: Can the same tutor take both Physics and Chemistry?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but do not treat it as the default. Plenty of science tutors are genuinely strong in one subject and merely adequate in the other, especially at Higher Level where the assessment demands diverge sharply. If both subjects need real work, two specialists usually produce better results than one generalist. If one subject only needs occasional doubt-solving while the other needs sustained teaching, a single tutor covering both makes the weekly schedule far easier to protect.

mainEntity.name: Is online tutoring genuinely useful for a Grade 9 student, or only for seniors?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can work at Grade 9, with conditions. Younger students drift more easily on a screen, so sessions need to be shorter, more interactive and built around a visible shared workspace rather than a lecture. A tablet with a stylus helps enormously in mathematics and sciences, because watching working appear line by line is most of the teaching. If a student has attention difficulties or resists the subject, home sessions are usually the better starting point, moving online later once habits settle.

contentBlocks.heading: The Week a DLF Phase 5 Student Actually Has
contentBlocks.body:
Look at how the week is spent before looking at tutors. In the towers around The Crest and DLF Park Place, an evening usually has three claimants: school work due tomorrow, a sport or activity running four days a week, and some external test preparation sitting quietly in the background. The IB workload does not shrink to accommodate any of them.

So the habit question comes first. Does the student open the assignment brief before starting, or only after finishing a draft? Is revision spread across the term or compressed into the fortnight before mocks? Are past papers attempted under time, or read through with the answers open alongside? Those answers reveal more about the kind of tutor needed than any grade on a report card.

A student with sound habits and a genuine content gap needs a subject specialist and perhaps six weeks. A student with solid content knowledge and disorganised habits needs someone willing to sit with a planner and a deadline sheet in session one, which is a different skill and not every excellent mathematician has it.

Getting that diagnosis wrong is the most common reason tutoring stalls by week five. Sessions are pleasant, the student likes the tutor, and nothing measurable moves. Say what the real problem is when you enquire, even when it is unflattering. Families comparing IB tutors in DLF Phase 5 Gurugram get further by describing the routine than by listing subjects.

contentBlocks.heading: How Study Habits Change From PYP to DP in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Habits are not one thing across the three programmes. They change shape completely.

In the Primary Years Programme, ages 3 to 12, the habit worth building is asking questions aloud and staying with a problem past the first wrong answer. Very little of it resembles studying. A tutor working with a Grade 3 student should be reading alongside them, playing with number, and resisting the pull towards a worksheet pack that keeps everyone busy and teaches nothing.

In the Middle Years Programme, ages 11 to 16, the habit shifts towards reading the task properly. Criterion-related assessment punishes students who write what they know instead of what was asked. The useful drill here is unglamorous: highlight the criterion, list what it demands, check the draft against that list before submitting. Students who build this at Grade 8 find Grade 11 considerably less brutal.

The Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19, adds calendar management on top of everything else. Internal assessments land across six subjects, the Extended Essay needs supervisor meetings, Theory of Knowledge carries its own deadlines, and the May 2026 or November 2026 papers wait at the end. Nobody holds that in their head. The habit is a written term plan with real dates, reviewed weekly, which is what a good first month of tutoring should produce.
items: PYP: curiosity and persistence, not worksheets
MYP: read the criterion before writing the answer
DP: a written term plan beats memory every time
Extended Essay and TOK need their own dates
May 2026 and November 2026 sessions planned backwards

contentBlocks.heading: DLF Phase 5, Golf Course Road and the Tutor Routes Around Them
contentBlocks.body:
Phase 5 sits on Golf Course Road in the premium residential pocket, high-rise rather than low-rise, with The Crest and DLF Park Place among the towers families name when giving directions. That position has a practical effect on tutoring, because the road is the main artery and everything gets measured in minutes along it.

Sector 53 and Sector 54 lie immediately north along the Rapid Metro corridor. Sector 57 and Sushant Lok 3 sit east near Golf Course Extension Road. DLF Phase 4, DLF Phase 1 and South City 1 are west, Nirvana Country and Sector 50 lie towards Sohna Road and Vatika Chowk, and Sector 65 is further out on the Extension.

Tutors living anywhere along that spine reach Phase 5 without much trouble between four and eight in the evening. After eight the traffic thins but tutors are tired and usually finishing a last session elsewhere. Before four, students are still in school.

There is a real squeeze in the middle. Everyone wants half past five, and IB tuition near DLF Phase 5 at that hour is the most requested slot in the area. Families willing to take seven o'clock, or to move one weekly session online, end up with noticeably more choice of tutor.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Requests That Come From DLF Phase 5 Homes
contentBlocks.body:
Requests from these towers skew Diploma-heavy, partly because families here often begin looking in Grade 11 rather than earlier.

Mathematics splits along the usual line, though the reasons differ. Students taking Math AA HL alongside two sciences are generally short of time rather than short of ability, and their sessions become triage: which topics carry the most marks, which can be left thin. Math AI HL students more often need help turning a vague idea into a modelling investigation with data they can defend under questioning.

Physics and Chemistry sessions here tend to circle the internal assessment. A student with a demanding training schedule will happily spend three weeks polishing a lab write-up and leave Paper 2 technique untouched until February. A tutor should notice that imbalance and name it early.

Economics attracts students who read widely and write loosely. The correction is mechanical: one accurate definition, one correctly labelled diagram, one evaluation that names a genuine limitation rather than gesturing at one.

English A requests are frequently about pace under exam conditions. Plenty of capable readers cannot produce a structured Paper 1 response within the time allowed, and that is a rehearsal problem before it is a comprehension problem. Any IB science tutor DLF Phase 5 parents consider should be equally willing to say which of these is really happening.

Physics and Chemistry: IA polish versus Paper 2 technique
Economics: definition, diagram, one real limitation
English A: timed rehearsal for Paper 1

The school run out of Phase 5 shapes the evening more than parents expect when they first ask for a six o'clock session.

Lancers International School is on Golf Course Road, the shortest of the common journeys, which often means a student is home and settled by half past four. GD Goenka World School out towards the Sohna Road region is the longest of the four, and students on that route frequently reach home after five with training still ahead of them.

Ask when your child last ate before booking a slot. A session starting fifteen minutes after a long bus journey loses its first twenty minutes, and you pay for those twenty minutes.

Tutors are matched on IB assessment experience rather than on school names. Knowing a school's assignment rhythm is helpful context and nothing more than that.

contentBlocks.heading: Turning a Habit Problem Into a Tutor Brief in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
A useful brief describes behaviour, not only subjects. The conversation tends to run like this.

You describe the pattern. Not she is weak in chemistry, but she understands it in class, scores well on tests she has revised for, and loses marks on anything requiring planning ahead. That single sentence reshapes the shortlist.

The advisor separates content gaps from habit gaps, because they call for different tutors and often different session lengths. Content work runs well in ninety-minute blocks. Habit work needs shorter and more frequent contact, sometimes three brief sessions a week through the first month.

Levels, school and available slots come next, along with any sport or test preparation that already owns part of the week. Tutor availability is then checked directly with the tutor and remains subject to their schedule.

Two or three profiles follow, with the reasoning stated openly, including who is stronger on structure and who is stronger on content depth.

The first session is diagnostic. Expect the tutor to look at a marked assignment, a recent test paper, and the student's planner if one exists. It should end with a rough plan carrying dates rather than a promise of regular practice.

Four weeks on, the test is simple. Has something changed that you can point at without squinting?

contentBlocks.heading: Why Hybrid Suits DLF Phase 5 Better Than Pure Home Tutoring
contentBlocks.body:
Hybrid is the format most often preferred here, and the reason is scheduling rather than fashion.

A typical week already holds a fixed sport or activity, school assignments with rolling deadlines, and sometimes external test preparation. Two fixed home sessions rarely survive that intact past October. One home session for teaching and one online session for review moves with the week instead of fighting it, and the online slot can shift to a Sunday morning or a late Thursday without anyone driving anywhere.

Pure home tutoring still suits some students, particularly younger ones and anyone who genuinely cannot concentrate on a screen. Tutors reach the Golf Course Road towers without much difficulty in the early evening, so an IB home tutor DLF Phase 5 request is usually placeable, subject to availability.

Pure online works best for Diploma students grinding through past papers, for rarer subject combinations, and for weeks when the family is travelling. It is also the honest answer for late doubt-solving before an internal deadline, because no tutor is driving to a tower at ten at night.

The weakness of hybrid is administrative. Two formats mean two sets of arrangements, and the whole thing falls apart when nobody writes the week down. Agree the pattern within the first fortnight and then hold it.

contentBlocks.heading: What a Tutor in Gurugram Cannot Fix
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor cannot buy back time. If sport occupies five evenings and the Diploma occupies the other two, something has to give, and no quantity of tutoring resolves that arithmetic. Families sometimes have to make a choice they have been avoiding, and an honest advisor will say so rather than sell more sessions.

A tutor cannot manufacture interest in a subject chosen for university admissions rather than for enjoyment. The subject can be made tolerable and it can be made passable. Enthusiasm is not on the price list.

A tutor cannot write the Extended Essay, draft the internal assessment, or edit a student's sentences into somebody else's voice. Real support means asking why the research question is worded that way, whether the evidence supports the claim, and which criterion the draft has quietly skipped. The writing stays the student's responsibility, and the school's academic honesty rules apply regardless of who is helping.

And a tutor cannot promise a grade. Any promise of a specific score, a guaranteed improvement or a fixed result should end the conversation there. What can be offered instead is a described process, stated matching criteria, and a clear four-week checkpoint where you decide whether to continue.

That is a smaller claim than most advertising makes. It is also one that can be kept.

EE and IA support means questions, never redrafting

contentBlocks.heading: Checks Behind Every Gurugram Shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Every tutor considered for a family here passes through the same checks, and none of them involve marketing copy.

Documents come first. Identity and academic qualifications are collected and verified before a profile is shared. Where a tutor claims IB teaching experience, that claim is examined rather than accepted, because there is a wide gap between having taught a syllabus and having once read one.

Then level-specific competence. A tutor may be strong at Middle Years mathematics and unconvincing at Analysis and Approaches Higher Level. Each level is assessed separately, and Higher Level subjects are treated as their own qualification rather than an extension of Standard Level.

Assessment literacy matters most for Diploma work. Can this tutor read a criterion and explain in ordinary language what separates a mid-band response from a top one? Can they mark a past-paper answer and defend the marks they awarded? Those two questions filter out a surprising number of otherwise capable subject experts.

Manner and reliability are tracked afterwards. Feedback from families in live matches is reviewed, and tutors who cancel frequently, arrive unprepared or drift from the agreed plan stop appearing in shortlists.

Verification is a filter and not a warranty. It improves the odds considerably. It does not remove your own judgement from the decision.

Higher Level treated as a separate competence

contentBlocks.heading: Booking Around Sport, Travel and Test Dates
contentBlocks.body:
Before enquiring, map the week honestly on paper. Sport, school commitments, travel plans for the term, and any external test dates already booked. Most tutoring schedules fail because the family described the week they wished they had rather than the one they live in.

Then decide what you are actually buying. Six weeks of intensive help before mocks is a different arrangement from a year of steady support, and the tutor profile differs accordingly. Say which one you want, because asking for both produces neither.

List subjects with levels, name the school, and mention the sport if fixtures move week to week. A tutor who can flex a Wednesday is worth more to you than one who cannot, and that preference can be built into the shortlist from the start.

Send all of that and an advisor reviews it against tutor availability around Phase 5. You receive two or three suggestions with reasoning attached, and a first session arranged as a diagnostic rather than a trial lesson. Everything stays subject to tutor schedules and can be reviewed as the term changes shape.

If the fit is wrong, say so in week two. Nobody gains from a polite term in which very little happens.

faqs.question: My son trains four evenings a week. Can tutoring realistically fit around that?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, though it will not look like two neat fixed slots. Most families in this situation run one longer teaching session on a free evening and one shorter online review at a movable time, often a weekend morning. Tell the advisor which evenings are genuinely blocked and whether fixtures shift week to week, because a tutor who can flex is a different person from one with a rigid calendar. Availability for flexible arrangements is checked with the tutor before anything is confirmed.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether the problem is the subject or the study routine?
faqs.answer: Look at where marks are lost. A student who performs well on revised tests but poorly on coursework and planned tasks has a routine problem, not a knowledge problem. A student who struggles even with topics revised twice has a content gap. Mixed patterns are common, and the first session is designed to separate them by working through a marked assignment and a recent test side by side. The plan that follows should name which one is being treated first.

faqs.question: Can a tutor reach the towers on Golf Course Road easily in the evening?
faqs.answer: Between four and eight, generally yes, since tutors working along the Sector 53, Sector 54 and Sushant Lok stretch pass close by. The difficulty is concentration of demand rather than distance. Half past five is the single most requested time in this pocket, so a family able to take seven o'clock will see a wider set of profiles. Tower entry needs visitor registration, so leaving a name at reception in advance keeps the session starting on time.

faqs.question: We travel often during term. Do sessions have to stop while we are away?
faqs.answer: No, and this is one of the clearer arguments for keeping at least one online session in the weekly pattern from the beginning. A student who has already worked with a tutor on screen loses nothing when the family is out of the country, whereas switching format mid-crisis rarely goes smoothly. Time zones matter for longer trips, so mention planned travel when you enquire and the schedule can be shaped around it in advance.

faqs.question: How are fees worked out when we mix home and online sessions?
faqs.answer: Rates generally differ by format, because home sessions include the tutor's travel time and online sessions do not. They also vary by level and subject, with Higher Level Diploma work and internal assessment mentoring priced above Middle Years support. A hybrid week is therefore quoted as a combination rather than a single number. Ask for the breakdown before starting, along with the notice period for cancelling or rescheduling a session at short notice.

faqs.question: Should we start Diploma tutoring in Grade 11 or wait until Grade 12?
faqs.answer: Grade 11 is easier to work with, and cheaper in total, because internal assessments can be planned rather than rescued. Starting in Grade 12 is still worthwhile, but the work becomes more selective: topic triage, exam technique and deadline management rather than building understanding from the base. A student joining in October of Grade 12 should expect an honest conversation about what can realistically be covered before the May session.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay without crossing academic honesty lines?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is clear enough to state. A tutor may discuss whether the research question is answerable, whether the sources support the argument, and which assessment criteria the draft is neglecting. A tutor may not write passages, restructure paragraphs into their own phrasing, or supply the analysis. Your school's own academic honesty policy governs the essay and the student signs for the work. Any tutor unclear about that distinction is the wrong choice.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor and my daughter simply do not get on?
faqs.answer: Raise it quickly rather than hoping it settles. Personality mismatch is common and rarely anyone's fault: a tutor who suits an anxious student can grate on a confident one who prefers to be challenged hard. Tell the advisor what specifically is not working, since a vague complaint produces a similar replacement. A different profile can be shortlisted, subject to availability, and the diagnostic already completed usually carries over so you are not starting from scratch.

faqs.question: Do you arrange support for Theory of Knowledge, or only for the main subjects?
faqs.answer: TOK support can be arranged, though the tutor pool is smaller than for mathematics or the sciences and availability varies by term. Most requests concern the essay rather than the exhibition, and they arrive late, which is a shame because the thinking benefits from time. Useful TOK help looks like discussion and challenge rather than content delivery, so expect sessions to feel more like an argument than a lesson. Ask early if this matters to you.

The Expressway sits at the northern edge of the city, away from the DLF and Golf Course Road pocket where most experienced IB tutors already teach. contentBlocks.heading: What Online Tutoring Does Better for Dwarka Expressway Families
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the honest comparison, because along this corridor it decides everything else.

Online tutoring does four things better than a home visit. It removes travel, which here is not a minor saving: a tutor driving up from Golf Course Road surrenders ninety minutes of an evening in order to teach for sixty. It widens the pool, so a Math AA HL specialist or someone who has recently marked Economics commentaries becomes reachable despite living nowhere near the Expressway sectors. It allows short sessions, and a focused thirty-minute doubt-clearing call two days before a test often beats an extra ninety-minute block. It also makes late slots possible, which matters for a student who reaches home at six and eats at eight.

Online tutoring does three things worse. Younger children drift. Handwritten working is harder to supervise unless the tutor uses a tablet and stylus and insists the student does the same. And a tutor in the room notices a student pretending to follow, where a tutor on a screen sees only a nodding thumbnail.

So the sensible default here is online for Diploma and upper Middle Years work, home visits where a younger child or a genuine concentration problem justifies the travel, and a mixture where the schedule permits. That recommendation is made family by family, not as blanket policy.
items: No travel cost buried in the tutor's evening
Specialist subjects reachable regardless of address
Short thirty-minute sessions before a test
Late-evening slots that a driving tutor cannot offer
Weaker for young children and unsupervised handwriting

contentBlocks.heading: Dwarka Expressway Sits at the Edge of Gurugram's Tutor Belt
contentBlocks.body:
The Expressway runs along the northern Gurugram corridor, closer to Delhi and Dwarka than to the older DLF phases, through newer sectors built around developments such as Sobha City, Puri Diplomatic Greens, ATS Triumph and Godrej Summit. Most of the housing here is recent, most residents moved in within the last decade, and the tutoring supply has not caught up with the housing supply.

That is the central fact for anyone searching from this address. Experienced IB tutors in the city are concentrated well to the south, around Golf Course Road, Sector 53 and Sector 54, DLF Phase 4 and DLF Phase 5, Sushant Lok, Sector 57 and down Sohna Road towards Vatika Chowk and Sector 50. Someone teaching in South City 1 or Nirvana Country on a Tuesday is not adding an Expressway session to that same day.

Proximity to Delhi cuts both ways. A few tutors based in West Delhi and Dwarka are genuinely closer to you than tutors in Sector 65, and home visits can sometimes be built on that. Others have already filled their weeks in Noida or Faridabad.

So IB tuition near Dwarka Expressway is arranged online more often than anywhere else in the city. That follows from geography, not from any shortcoming of the corridor itself.
items: Northern corridor, closer to Delhi and Dwarka
Newer sectors, recent residents, thin local tutor supply
Tutor concentration lies south around Golf Course Road

Online share is higher here than elsewhere in the city

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tutoring on Dwarka Expressway: When It Is Worth the Drive
contentBlocks.body:
Most enquiries about IB tutors in Dwarka Expressway Gurugram settle online, but home visits here are possible and they are conditional. Three factors make them realistic.

Frequency comes first. A tutor will consider a two-session-a-week commitment on the Expressway far more readily than a single hour, because the travel spreads across more teaching. Families asking for one weekly visit tend to receive a shorter list of names.

Timing comes second. Sessions between five and seven work. Anything needing the tutor to arrive by four means fighting traffic in both directions, and anything ending after nine leaves a long drive home. An IB home tutor Dwarka Expressway request is easiest to place when the window is generous rather than exact to the minute.

Grouping comes third. Where two families in the same development need the same subject at the same level, the route problem shrinks and both households gain. Worth asking about within your society, though it only works when the students are genuinely at a similar stage.

Hybrid is where most families land after a term. One visit for teaching new material and supervised written work, one online session for revision, past papers and doubt-solving.

The honest position: home tutoring here costs more, offers fewer names, and cancels more often in bad weather. It is still the right call for a Grade 4 student, or a teenager who cannot work on a screen.
items: Two visits a week place more easily than one
Five to seven is the workable arrival window
Same-society, same-level pairs shorten tutor routes
Hybrid settles most families by the second term
Fewer names, higher fees, more weather cancellations

contentBlocks.heading: Subjects Where a Screen Helps and Subjects Where It Gets in the Way
contentBlocks.body:
Subject choice affects format more than most parents realise when they first enquire.

Mathematics transfers to a screen well, on one condition: both people need a tablet and a stylus. Watching a Math AA HL derivation appear line by line is the teaching itself. Typing equations into a chat box is not. Math AI HL sits even more comfortably online, since the modelling investigation involves spreadsheets and calculator work that are easier to share on screen than to squint at across a table.

Physics survives the move with good diagrams and a willing annotator. Chemistry is harder, particularly organic mechanisms and anything involving apparatus, and a tutor who can mark up a shared document will always beat one narrating a static slide.

Economics is close to format-neutral. Reading an article together, drawing the diagram, arguing over the evaluation: all of that works remotely without loss.

English A is the surprise. Discussion-heavy work on unseen extracts often goes better online, because the text sits on both screens and nobody is craning over one shared copy. Timed writing under supervision is the exception and is better done in a room.

Ask any IB science tutor Dwarka Expressway parents are considering what they physically write with during a session. The answer reveals whether they have taught online seriously or simply moved a lecture onto video.
items: Tablet and stylus required for maths and sciences
Math AI HL: spreadsheets and GDC share well on screen
Chemistry mechanisms need live annotation, not slides
Economics is close to format-neutral
English A unseen work often improves online; timed writing does not

contentBlocks.heading: From Enquiry to First Session for a Dwarka Expressway Request
contentBlocks.body:
The sequence for a request from this corridor differs in one respect from the rest of the city. Format is settled early rather than last.

You send grade, subjects with levels, the school, the development you live in, and your realistic weekly slots. State immediately whether online only is acceptable, because that single answer roughly doubles or halves the pool available to you.

An advisor then separates what needs a specialist from what needs a capable all-rounder. A Grade 7 student needing help across three subjects can work well with one generalist. A Grade 12 student sitting Math AA HL and Physics HL needs two people, and at least one of them will almost certainly be online.

Availability is confirmed with each tutor individually, including their willingness to travel out here if home sessions are wanted. Nothing gets promised before that check, and it stays subject to their schedule.

You receive two or three profiles with reasoning written out, marked clearly for which are online only.

The first session runs as a diagnostic on recent school work and a past-paper question. For an online match it doubles as a technology test. If the setup fails during that hour, fix it before continuing instead of tolerating it for a term.

Review at four weeks against something specific you can name.

Specialist versus all-rounder decided by grade and level
Travel willingness confirmed with each tutor

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Support Across Northern Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The same three programmes are supported here, Grade 1 to Grade 12, but the format advice changes with age.

Primary Years Programme students, ages 3 to 12, are the group for whom online tutoring is weakest. A six-year-old on a video call needs an adult sitting alongside for most of the hour, which cancels much of the convenience. Where a home tutor cannot be arranged, shorter and more frequent online sessions of twenty-five or thirty minutes work considerably better than one long block that ends in tears.

Middle Years Programme students, ages 11 to 16, sit in between. From around Grade 8, most can hold a focused online session provided the tutor keeps them writing rather than listening. This is also the stage where criterion-related tasks begin to carry weight, and reviewing a marked assignment on a shared screen is genuinely easier than passing paper back and forth across a table.

Diploma Programme students, ages 16 to 19, adapt to online work most readily of all. Internal assessments, Extended Essay planning, Theory of Knowledge discussion and past-paper revision for the May 2026 or November 2026 sessions all run well remotely. Drafts are annotated live, and the student keeps a written record of every comment, which is more than most sessions in a room leave behind.
items: PYP: short frequent sessions, or a home tutor if possible
MYP from Grade 8: online works if the student keeps writing
Marked assignments review better on a shared screen
DP: IA, EE, TOK and past papers all suit remote work
Annotated drafts leave a record the student can revisit

contentBlocks.heading: IB School Commutes From Sobha City and Diplomatic Greens
contentBlocks.body:
Children living along this corridor attend IB schools that are, without exception, a drive away. Pathways World School serves the wider Gurugram region. Lancers International School is on Golf Course Road. Scottish High International School sits in Sector 57. GD Goenka World School lies out in the Sohna Road region. All four involve crossing a good part of the city, and some families here choose schools in Delhi or Dwarka instead for precisely that reason.

The consequence is a late start to the working evening. A student leaving school at three and reaching home at half past four is not ready to begin again straight away. Booking a session at five and then wondering why the first half hour drags is a scheduling error rather than a tutoring failure.

Long commutes also make online sessions more attractive to the students themselves. A child who has already spent two hours on a bus has limited appetite for another adult arriving at the door.

Tutors are matched on IB syllabus and assessment experience rather than on school familiarity. contentBlocks.heading: How Gurugram Tutors Are Screened Before You Meet Them
contentBlocks.body:
Screening does not relax because a session happens on a screen. If anything it needs one extra layer.

Identity and academic qualifications are collected and verified for every tutor before a profile reaches a family. Claimed IB experience is checked rather than assumed, with attention to whether the tutor has taught the current syllabus, supervised internal assessments, or marked work against published criteria.

Subject competence is assessed at the exact level requested. Higher Level and Standard Level are treated as distinct, and confidence with Analysis and Approaches is not accepted as evidence of comfort with Applications and Interpretation.

For online matches, teaching setup forms part of the assessment. Does this tutor have a stable connection, a tablet or other writing surface, and a working method for sharing and annotating documents? A brilliant physicist with a bad camera angle and a habit of talking over slides will lose a Grade 10 student inside three weeks.

Reliability is monitored once a match is running. Families report on punctuality, preparation and whether the agreed plan is being followed, and tutors who fall short stop appearing in shortlists.

This process reduces risk rather than removing it. It makes no claim at all about the grade any particular student will go on to achieve.
items: Documents and qualifications verified before sharing profiles
IB experience examined, level by level
Online setup assessed: connection, stylus, annotation method
Punctuality and preparation tracked from family feedback
Risk reduced, outcomes never guaranteed

contentBlocks.heading: Honest Limits of Remote Teaching in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Some limits worth stating before you commit money to this.

Remote teaching depends on a working connection. Power cuts, patchy bandwidth through monsoon weeks and a shared home line all interrupt sessions, and any tutor promising you an uninterrupted term is overpromising. Agree in advance what happens to a session that dies at the twenty-minute mark, so nobody argues about it later.

Remote teaching also depends on the student being present in more than the technical sense. A muted teenager with a second window open is a problem no platform solves. Sessions taken in a shared room rather than behind a closed bedroom door help far more than any monitoring software.

Beyond format, the usual boundaries hold. No tutor writes an internal assessment, restructures an Extended Essay, or supplies analysis that the student then submits as their own. Support means questions, criteria and honest feedback on a draft the student has written.

And nobody here promises a grade, a band, or an improvement figure. Those promises are unverifiable and the people making them know it. What is offered instead is a stated process, described checks on tutors, availability confirmed rather than implied, and a first month after which you should be able to point at something concrete.

If that sounds modest, it is meant to.
items: Bandwidth and power cuts interrupt sessions; plan for it
Agree upfront what happens to a session cut short
Shared room beats a closed door for concentration
No IA writing, no EE restructuring, no supplied analysis
No promised grades, bands or improvement figures

contentBlocks.heading: Set Up the Desk Before the First Session
contentBlocks.body:
Ten minutes of setup separates a good first online session from a wasted one.

Put the student at a desk in a shared part of the house, not on a bed. Use a laptop or a large screen, because working from a phone fails within a fortnight and the student will not tell you it is failing. Buy an inexpensive tablet and stylus if the subject involves mathematics or science, since handwriting is the substance of those sessions. Test the connection at the hour the session will actually run, when everyone else in the house is online too.

Then gather the academic material. Subjects with exact levels. A recent marked assignment. The school's assessment calendar if you have one, because deadlines shape the plan more than syllabus order ever does.

Send all of that with your development name on the Expressway and the slots you can protect, and say plainly whether home visits should be considered or online only.

An advisor reviews availability with tutors before suggesting anyone. You get a small shortlist with reasons attached and a diagnostic first session that also proves the setup works. Everything stays subject to tutor schedules and can be reviewed once the term settles into shape.
items: Desk in a shared room, laptop not phone
Tablet and stylus for any maths or science subject
Test the connection at the real session hour
Marked assignment plus the school assessment calendar
State clearly: home visits considered, or online only

faqs.question: Is it hard to find a home tutor willing to travel to Dwarka Expressway?
faqs.answer: Harder than in the DLF phases, and worth knowing before you plan around it. Most experienced IB tutors work south of here, so a visit means a long drive in both directions. Requests for two sessions a week place more easily than a single hour, and a five to seven arrival window helps considerably. Home visits are reviewed case by case and remain subject to tutor availability. Many families here start online and add a home session later if one becomes practical.

faqs.question: What equipment does my child actually need for online IB sessions?
faqs.answer: A laptop or desktop with a decent screen, a stable connection, and headphones so household noise does not derail the hour. For mathematics, physics or chemistry, add an inexpensive drawing tablet with a stylus. Watching working appear stroke by stroke is most of what a tutor does in those subjects, and typed equations are a poor substitute. A phone is not adequate beyond an occasional quick doubt-clearing call, however tempting it looks in the first week.

faqs.question: Our internet drops during the monsoon. How is that handled?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before it happens rather than during an argument. Most tutors will reschedule or extend when a session is lost early, and a written understanding about the cut-off point avoids awkwardness later. A mobile hotspot as backup covers most short outages. If interruptions are frequent, that is a genuine argument for prioritising a home tutor even at higher cost, because repeated broken sessions damage a student's willingness to engage more than the lost hours themselves do.

faqs.question: Can two families in the same society share a tutor?
faqs.answer: It can work and it is worth exploring in these developments, where several households often need the same subject. The condition is that the students are genuinely at a similar stage, not merely in the same grade. A Grade 11 pair working through the same Math AI SL syllabus can share productively. Pairing a student needing foundations with one needing exam polish helps neither. Arrangements depend on tutor willingness and availability, so raise the idea when you first enquire.

faqs.question: My daughter's school is in Delhi, not Gurugram. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: It changes the timetable rather than the tutoring. Term dates, internal deadlines and mock schedules will follow her school, so share its assessment calendar rather than assuming a common city pattern. It may also change the commute in your favour, since a Delhi school run can be shorter from this corridor than a journey to the Sohna Road region. Tutors are matched on IB syllabus and assessment experience, which does not depend on which side of the border the school sits.

faqs.question: How do fees compare between online and home sessions here?
faqs.answer: Home sessions on the Expressway usually cost more than online ones, and the gap tends to be wider here than in central areas because the travel is longer. Level and subject matter too, with Higher Level Diploma work and internal assessment mentoring priced above Middle Years support. Ask for indicative ranges for your exact combination before committing, and clarify the notice period for cancellation, since a cancelled home visit costs the tutor an evening they cannot recover.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring workable for a Grade 5 child?
faqs.answer: It can be, with adjustments that most people skip. Keep sessions to twenty-five or thirty minutes and run them more often rather than booking a single long block. Have an adult within earshot for the first few weeks. Insist the tutor keeps the child writing, drawing or speaking throughout instead of explaining at length. If none of that is feasible, a home tutor is the better option for this age, even though it takes longer to arrange in this area.

faqs.question: Can a tutor supervise a chemistry internal assessment remotely?
faqs.answer: The written and analytical parts, yes. Choosing a workable research question, checking the method genuinely tests it, reviewing data processing and uncertainty treatment, and reading the evaluation against the criteria all work perfectly well on a shared screen. The practical work itself belongs in the school laboratory under the teacher's supervision, and no tutor should be involved in it. The student writes every word of the report, and the school's academic honesty policy governs the whole process.

faqs.question: How quickly can we start if mocks are six weeks away?
faqs.answer: Online matches usually move fastest, often within a few days, because no travel arrangement has to be solved first. Say clearly in the enquiry that the timeline is six weeks, since a short intensive block suits a different tutor from a year-long arrangement. Expect the first session to identify which topics carry the most marks and which can be left thin. Six weeks is enough to change exam technique meaningfully. It is not enough to rebuild two years of content.

contentBlocks.heading: Three Timelines: This Week, This Month, This Term
contentBlocks.body:
Most parents searching for IB tutors in Golf Course Extension Road Gurugram are working inside one of three timeframes, and the right tutor looks different in each.

This week. Something has already gone wrong. A Physics test came back thin, an IA draft was returned with comments the student cannot decode, or a Math AA HL topic has quietly become a wall. The request is urgent and narrow, and the match has to be someone genuinely free at a fixed slot within days.

This month. A report card has landed, or mocks are visible on the school calendar. There is room to diagnose before acting, which usually produces a better match, because tutor selection is not being driven by whoever happens to be free on Thursday.

This term. A parent is looking two or three months ahead, often for a Grade 9 or Grade 10 student who will enter the Diploma Programme soon. This is the calmest conversation to have and the one where a tutor's teaching style matters more than raw availability.

Say which of the three you are in when you send a request. It shapes the shortlist more than the subject does. It also changes what an honest answer sounds like: with eight weeks left before the May 2026 session, nobody should be offering a full syllabus rebuild, and a tutor who offers one is worth doubting.
items: This week: urgent, narrow, slot-driven
This month: diagnose first, then match
This term: style and fit over raw availability
Grade 9 and 10 planning ahead of DP
Eight weeks out means triage, not a rebuild

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Tutors Are Matched to Golf Course Extension Road Requests
contentBlocks.body:
The request form is short on purpose, but four fields do most of the work: programme and year, subject with its level, the pocket you live in, and the two or three time windows that survive a school night.

An advisor reads it rather than letting a filter run. Level matters more than subject name. A tutor comfortable with MYP Sciences is not automatically right for Chemistry HL Paper 3, and Math AI HL and Math AA HL are different enough to be treated as separate requests. Where a brief mentions an internal assessment, the match narrows again, because IA supervision turns on criterion language and research question scope rather than content revision.

Location is the third filter and the one parents underestimate. A tutor living near Sector 65 can reach M3M Merlin or Emaar DigiHomes on a weekday evening without much drama. The same tutor asked to reach DLF Phase 1 for a six o'clock start will either arrive late or quietly stop taking the slot after a month. contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Support Across Gurugram's Golf Course Extension Road Belt
contentBlocks.body:
Support runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12, and the three programmes ask genuinely different things of a tutor.

Primary Years Programme families on this stretch usually want reading fluency, number sense and enough structure that a six-year-old will sit down without a fight. What they do not want is a worksheet factory. Inquiry-led early learning falls apart if a tutor converts it into drills, so the match here leans towards patience rather than subject depth.

Middle Years Programme requests are the most common from the newer towers. A Grade 8 or Grade 9 student can understand a concept perfectly in class and still lose marks because the response never addressed the criterion. Tutors at this level spend a surprising share of their time on command terms: what "evaluate" expects that "describe" does not, why a conclusion with no limitations rarely reaches the top band.

Diploma Programme requests are the most specialist. Two years, six subjects, an extended essay, TOK, and internal assessments in almost everything. A DP tutor is part subject teacher and part deadline manager, because a student who is fine in Economics and drowning in Math AA HL usually has a scheduling problem as well as a content one. Planning that begins in Grade 11 is far easier than planning that begins in January of Grade 12.
items: PYP: reading, number sense, short sessions
MYP: criteria and command-term translation
DP: six subjects, EE, TOK, IA deadlines
Grade 1 to Grade 12 coverage
A Grade 11 start beats a Grade 12 scramble

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Both on the Extension Road Corridor
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and the communities around them, depending on which tutors have that pocket open. Online tutoring is available across Gurugram for every supported IB subject.

The honest version: home tutoring on this corridor works when the timing is realistic, and stops working when it is not. A 5.30 pm start at Ireo Grand Arch is usually fine. A 7.15 pm start for a tutor coming from the far side of Vatika Chowk on a Friday is a promise that traffic will eventually break.

Online has one clear advantage here, and it is not convenience. It is access to specialists. Higher-level Physics, Math AA HL and less commonly requested subject combinations have thin local supply, and insisting on home visits can mean accepting a weaker subject match in order to save travel. For late-evening slots and for revision blocks close to an exam session, online is often the better trade.

Hybrid suits many families along Golf Course Extension Road: one longer in-person session at the weekend for teaching, one shorter online session midweek for doubt-solving and marked-work review. It also survives the weeks when school activities eat the calendar, because a thirty-minute check-in is easier to protect than a two-hour visit.
items: Home visits subject to tutor schedules
Online across Gurugram for all supported subjects
Late slots usually work better online
Hybrid: weekend teaching, midweek doubts
Vatika Chowk is the evening pressure point

contentBlocks.heading: Subjects Golf Course Extension Road Students Ask About Most in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Requests from this belt cluster predictably. Math AA HL and Math AI HL lead, followed by Physics and Chemistry, then Economics, then English A.

Math AA HL requests usually arrive after the first proof-heavy unit, when a student who was comfortable through MYP suddenly is not. Math AI HL requests look different. The algebra is lighter, but the modelling and the technology-assisted work catch people out, and the exploration carries real weight.

Physics and Chemistry requests often turn out to be data-handling requests in disguise. The student understands the concept and loses marks in the practical write-up: on uncertainty, on graph interpretation, on the evaluation section of an internal assessment. A tutor who only teaches theory does not fix that.

Economics support is usually about diagram discipline and the gap between explaining and evaluating. English A requests are the least about content and the most about structure: how a commentary is built, how a passage is read closely, how a Paper 1 response earns marks beyond summary.

Standard level and higher level are not the same request, and a tutor is matched to the level rather than to the subject label. Where a student needs help with an extended essay or TOK instead of a taught subject, that is handled as a separate kind of match, because supervision and teaching are different skills.
items: Math AA HL: proof and justification marks
Math AI HL: modelling and the exploration
Physics and Chemistry: IA data handling
Economics: evaluation beyond the diagram
English A: commentary structure, not more reading
SL and HL matched separately

contentBlocks.heading: What Four Weeks of Tutoring Should Actually Look Like
contentBlocks.body:
Nobody can promise a grade, and a tutor who does is telling you about their sales approach rather than their teaching. What can be described is what a working arrangement looks like by the end of the first month.

Week one is diagnostic. The tutor should be asking for recent tests, marked work and the school's assessment calendar, and should finish that session able to name two or three specific gaps rather than a general sense that the subject is hard.

Weeks two and three should feel narrower, not broader. If sessions are still ranging across the whole syllabus, the diagnosis did not land. You should be able to say in one sentence what is being worked on.

By week four, three things should be visible. The student attempts a question type that was avoided a month ago. Homework arguments have reduced, even slightly. And the tutor can tell you what comes next without being asked.

If none of that is true after four sessions, the match is wrong. That is not a disaster and it is not unusual. Say what specifically is not working and a different tutor can be reviewed, subject to availability. Changing early costs a fortnight. Changing in March, with an exam session close, costs far more than that.
items: Week 1: marked work, school calendar, named gaps
Weeks 2-3: focus narrows rather than widens
Week 4: new question types attempted
Fewer homework arguments is a real signal
Change early; changing in March is expensive

contentBlocks.heading: Checks Before a Tutor Is Suggested to a Gurugram Family
contentBlocks.body:
Screening happens before a name reaches you, and it is deliberately unglamorous.

Identity and qualifications are checked against documents rather than against a claim on a profile. Teaching history is reviewed next, with attention to which programmes and levels a tutor has actually taught. Someone who has taught MYP Sciences for years and never taken a student through Chemistry HL is recorded as exactly that, because the difference surfaces in the second week of a DP engagement.

IB-specific familiarity is its own check: assessment objectives, criterion-based marking, internal assessment structure, extended essay supervision, TOK, command-term language. A strong graduate tutor who has never marked against IB criteria can still be useful for foundation work in Grade 8, and is not the right person to guide a Grade 12 IA.

Mode and coverage are confirmed rather than assumed. A tutor listed for home sessions on Golf Course Extension Road is asked which evenings they can realistically hold across a term, not whether they are willing in principle.

Feedback from ongoing engagements feeds into later matches. Tutors who cancel often, who do not reply to parents, or whose sessions drift into unstructured chat stop being recommended. None of this promises a perfect fit at the first attempt, which is why the review-and-change route exists at all.

Programme and level recorded honestly
IA, EE, TOK and criterion familiarity tested
Evening coverage confirmed across a full term
Ongoing feedback removes unreliable tutors

faqs.question: Can a tutor reach M3M Golf Estate or Ireo Grand Arch for a weekday evening session?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it depends almost entirely on where the tutor is based. Tutors living around Sector 57, Sector 65 or Sushant Lok 3 can usually hold regular evening slots on this stretch. Tutors coming from DLF Phase 1, Delhi or Noida are more realistic as weekend options. When you send a request, name the tower and the two time windows you can actually keep, and availability for those specific slots is checked before any name is shared with you.

faqs.question: We are at the Sohna Road end of the Extension Road. Does that change availability?
faqs.answer: It does. The corridor is not one travel zone, and a tutor comfortable near M3M Merlin may find the Vatika Chowk side a different proposition at six in the evening. Families closer to Sector 50 and Sohna Road are usually better served by tutors based on that side, or by online sessions during the week with an in-person session at the weekend. Say which end you live at in the request rather than only naming the road, because it changes the shortlist meaningfully.

faqs.question: What do IB tutors on Golf Course Extension Road usually charge?
faqs.answer: Fees vary by level, subject, mode and travel. Higher-level Diploma Programme subjects sit above MYP support, in-person visits cost more than online, and a tutor crossing the city for a single session prices that time in. Indicative ranges are shared alongside the shortlist so the number is never a surprise after the first session. Compare on value rather than on rate alone: a cheaper hour that stays unfocused for a whole term is the more expensive choice in the end.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely as effective for Math AA HL?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma Programme students, yes, and sometimes better. Higher-level Maths depends on written working, and a shared screen or tablet shows that working as clearly as a table does. The real gain is subject fit, because the pool of Math AA HL specialists in any one part of Gurugram is small, so insisting on home visits can mean trading a strong subject match for a shorter journey. Younger students are the exception, since attention usually holds better with someone physically present.

faqs.question: My daughter has eight weeks before mocks. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: Not too late to make a difference, but the plan has to change shape. Eight weeks is enough to fix exam technique, drill two or three high-yield topics and stop marks leaking on presentation and command terms. It is not enough to rebuild a full higher-level syllabus, and any tutor suggesting otherwise is not being straight with you. Send the recent marked work along with the request so the diagnosis happens before session one rather than during it.

faqs.question: How quickly can we change tutors if the fit is wrong?
faqs.answer: Raise it as soon as you see it, ideally by the third or fourth session. Say specifically what is not working: pace, communication, preparation, or that the level is above or below where the student actually is. A different tutor can then be reviewed, subject to availability at your time slot. Asking for a change is treated as ordinary feedback, not a complaint. Switching early costs a fortnight; switching close to an exam session costs a great deal more.

faqs.question: Do you arrange help with the extended essay and TOK, or only taught subjects?
faqs.answer: Both, but they are matched differently. Extended essay work is supervision rather than teaching: scoping a research question, structuring an argument, holding to a word count, and managing supervisor deadlines set by the school. TOK support focuses on the exhibition and essay, and on the habit of examining knowledge claims properly. A tutor excellent at Physics content is not automatically the right guide for an extended essay, so say clearly in your request which kind of help you want.

faqs.question: Which grades are covered, and is Grade 6 too early for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Coverage runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12. Grade 6 is not too early where there is a specific gap, such as fractions, reading stamina or written expression, but the format should stay light: shorter sessions, fewer per week, and a clear finishing point once the gap closes. Long-running tutoring at that age can create dependence rather than confidence. For Middle Years Programme students, the most useful early work is usually understanding how criterion-based marking differs from a simple right answer.

faqs.question: Are you connected to Scottish High or Lancers, since students here attend them?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with Scottish High International School, Lancers International School, GD Goenka World School, Pathways World School or any other school. Those names appear on this page because families living around Golf Course Extension Road send children to them, which affects travel time and internal deadlines. contentBlocks.heading: The Seven O'Clock Problem on a Wednesday in Sector 53
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the situation behind most enquiries about IB tutors in Golf Course Road Gurugram. School finishes around three. The bus or the car gets home somewhere between four and half past. There is a snack, then a football session or a music class that cannot be moved, then dinner at eight. That leaves one usable hour, and it lands between six and half past seven on a Wednesday.

Every family on this corridor is bidding for the same hour. So is every tutor's other student.

Which is why the first useful question is not who is the strongest Physics tutor available, but who is genuinely free at the only time this particular student can concentrate. A brilliant tutor at nine at night is worse than a good one at six, because a Grade 11 student who has already done seven hours of school does not absorb much at nine.

From there the picture widens. Once the slot is fixed, subject and level set the shortlist, mode decides how much travel sits in the way, and the school's own deadlines decide what the early sessions cover. Golf Course Road has an advantage many parts of the city do not. It is dense and well connected, so a tutor can reach several buildings without crossing town, and that widens the pool for exactly the hour everyone wants.
items: One usable hour, roughly 6.00 to 7.30 pm
Slot first, then subject and level
Late sessions rarely repay the effort
Dense corridor means a wider tutor pool per hour

contentBlocks.heading: DP Maths, Sciences and Economics on Golf Course Road
contentBlocks.body:
Demand along Sector 53, Sector 54 and DLF Phase 5 skews heavily towards Diploma Programme subjects, and within that towards a short list: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A.

Math AA HL is the single most requested. The usual trigger is calculus or the shift into proof, where marks depend on justification rather than on landing an answer. Math AI HL requests tend to arrive later in the year and are more often about the exploration than about class content.

Physics splits into two very different requests. One is mechanics and electricity, where the fix is timed problem practice. The other is the internal assessment, where the fix is experimental design, uncertainty and a discussion that engages honestly with error. Chemistry follows a similar split, with organic mechanisms as the recurring pressure point.

Economics is usually asked for closer to exams than the sciences are, generally once a student realises that a well-drawn diagram without evaluation stalls around the middle bands. English A support tends to be about close reading and structure rather than about reading more widely.

Standard level and higher level are matched separately. A tutor may be excellent at SL Physics and honest enough to say that HL Paper 3 is not their strength, and that answer is far more useful to you than a confident yes.

Physics: timed problems or IA design, rarely both

Economics: evaluation paragraphs, not more diagrams

contentBlocks.heading: From Enquiry to Shortlist for a Golf Course Road Family in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Matching is done by a person reading the request, not by a keyword filter, so the quality of the shortlist depends on how specific the request is.

Four things carry the most weight. The programme and year, because Grade 9 MYP and Grade 12 DP are unrelated jobs. The subject with its level written out, since maths alone is four different requests. The mode you want and the mode you would accept. And the exact time windows that survive contact with a school night.

An advisor then works through availability on this corridor rather than across Gurugram as a whole. A tutor already teaching in Sector 54 or DLF Park Place is a stronger candidate for a 6.30 start than a tutor who is technically willing to travel from much further out. Where a request involves an internal assessment or an extended essay, supervision experience is weighted above general subject knowledge.

You receive a shortlist showing the level each tutor teaches, their mode, the windows they can hold and an indicative fee range. Nothing is booked before you have spoken to at least one of them.

Sometimes the honest answer is that nothing suitable is free at 6.30 on a Tuesday. You will be told that, with the alternatives: a different day, an online tutor with a stronger subject fit, or a wait.

Subject plus level, since maths is four requests
Windows that survive a real school night

A straight no when the slot is unavailable

contentBlocks.heading: Golf Course Road, DLF Phase 5 and the Rapid Metro Corridor in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Golf Course Road runs through Sector 53 and Sector 54 with the Rapid Metro line alongside it, and that line quietly changes tutoring logistics. A tutor without a car can reach The Crest or DLF Park Place reliably at a fixed time, which is rarely true of corridors served only by road.

DLF Phase 5 sits immediately off the road. Sushant Lok, DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4 lie behind it towards the older city. Sector 57 and Golf Course Extension Road continue south-east, while Sohna Road, Sector 50 and Nirvana Country sit further out again. South City 1 and Sector 65 round out the pockets a tutor working this corridor typically covers.

The practical effect is a wider tutor pool per hour than most parts of the city, because a tutor can hold two consecutive sessions in different buildings without a long drive between them. That matters a great deal for the six-to-eight window every family wants.

The trade-off is time lost at school pickup hours and on Friday evenings, when the corridor slows badly. If your only workable slot is seven on a Friday, ask about online for that day and keep the in-person session for a weekend morning instead.

contentBlocks.heading: Grade 1 to Grade 12: What Changes as Students Move Through IB
contentBlocks.body:
Support covers Grade 1 through Grade 12, and the interesting part is the transitions rather than the programmes themselves.

Primary Years Programme work is about habits. Reading stamina, number confidence, and the ability to sit with a problem for ten minutes without abandoning it. Tutoring at this stage should be short, frequent and light, and a parent is right to be suspicious of anything that looks like exam preparation.

The move from PYP into the Middle Years Programme catches families out because the workload does not jump but the expectations do. A student is suddenly assessed against criteria, and a perfectly sensible answer can lose marks for not doing what the criterion asked. Most MYP requests on this corridor are really requests for help with that translation.

The jump from MYP Year 5 into the Diploma Programme is the sharp one. Six subjects, three at higher level, plus TOK, the extended essay and internal assessments that run alongside teaching rather than after it. Students who coasted through MYP on ability often struggle in the first DP term, not because the content is impossible but because nothing has previously demanded that they plan.

Grade 11 is the right moment to fix that. Grade 12, with the May 2026 or November 2026 session in view, is late but not hopeless, provided everyone accepts that the plan becomes triage.

PYP to MYP: expectations jump before workload does
MYP to DP: planning is the real gap
Grade 11 fixes what Grade 12 can only triage
May 2026 and November 2026 sessions as fixed end points

contentBlocks.heading: What Is Checked Before a Name Reaches You
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is a filter, not a certificate, and it is worth knowing what it does and does not cover.

Documents are verified: identity, degree and teaching credentials, checked against records rather than accepted from a profile page. Teaching background is reviewed with a specific eye on programme and level, because the phrase IB experience hides a great deal. Two years of MYP Individuals and Societies and two years of DP Economics HL are both IB experience, and only one of them is relevant to a Grade 12 Economics request.

Subject familiarity is checked against assessment: criterion-based marking for MYP, internal assessment structure and command terms for DP, extended essay supervision where relevant, TOK where a student needs it.

Availability is confirmed against real evenings before a tutor is listed for a pocket. This is the check that prevents the common failure where an enthusiastic yes in June becomes a pattern of cancellations by October.

What screening cannot do is predict chemistry between a tutor and a particular teenager. That is why the first session is treated as a trial and why asking for a change is a normal request rather than a complaint. Ask the tutor directly, in that first session, which levels they have taught and how recently. A straight answer tells you a great deal.

Programme and level, not the phrase IB experience

First session treated as a trial

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Between Home Visits and Online Sessions in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and neighbouring communities, subject to which evenings a tutor has open. Online covers all supported IB subjects across the city.

Home sessions earn their premium with younger students and with anyone who needs supervision as much as instruction. A Grade 6 student will work steadily for an hour with someone sitting across the table and will drift within fifteen minutes on a screen. Presence is the product.

Online earns its place in two situations here. The first is specialist supply, since Math AA HL, higher-level Physics and less common subject combinations have a small local pool, and restricting yourself to home visits can mean choosing a shorter journey over a better subject fit. The second is the final six weeks before an exam session, when short frequent past-paper sessions beat one long weekly visit and nobody wants to add travel to four sessions a week.

Hybrid works well on this corridor: an in-person session at the weekend, an online one midweek for doubts and marked-work review.

One honest limitation. Online is poor for a student who has stopped doing the work. If the real problem is avoidance rather than understanding, a screen makes it easier to hide, and an in-person tutor is the better intervention.

Online: specialist subjects and late slots

contentBlocks.heading: Fees, Value and the Questions Worth Asking a Tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Fees vary by level, subject, mode and how far a tutor travels. Higher-level DP subjects cost more than MYP support, in-person costs more than online, and a tutor crossing the city for one session will price that in. Ranges are shared before a booking, so the number is not discovered after the first session.

Value is harder than price. The cheapest option that produces a comfortable, unfocused hour every week becomes expensive across a term. The most expensive option is not automatically better either, and a very senior tutor is sometimes a poor fit for a student who mainly needs confidence rebuilt.

Three questions separate a good tutor from a plausible one. What exactly will we work on in the first three sessions, and why those? What will you want to see from the school before we start? And what would make you tell us this is not working?

No honest tutor will promise a grade, and a promised score should end the conversation rather than close the sale. What can reasonably be expected is a clear diagnosis in week one and a visible narrowing of focus by week three.

If that does not happen, say so early. Changing a tutor in week three is routine. Changing in the term of the exam is not.

faqs.question: We can only manage 6.30 pm on weekdays. Is that realistic on Golf Course Road?
faqs.answer: It is the most contested hour on the corridor, so it is realistic but not guaranteed. Tutors living in Sector 53, Sector 54, DLF Phase 5 or along the Rapid Metro line can often hold it, since they are not driving across the city between students. faqs.question: Does the Rapid Metro actually make a difference to tutor availability?
faqs.answer: More than parents expect. Tutors without cars are a real part of the pool, particularly younger subject specialists, and a metro-served corridor means they can commit to a fixed weekday time instead of guessing at traffic. It also makes back-to-back sessions in different buildings workable, which keeps rates sane and reduces cancellations. faqs.question: How much does an IB Maths higher level tutor cost around here?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate. Higher-level Diploma Programme Maths sits at the upper end because the pool of tutors comfortable with AA HL proof work and AI HL modelling is small, and in-person sessions carry a travel component on top. Online usually costs less for the same level of expertise. faqs.question: Our son is in Grade 11 and already behind in two subjects. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: Start with one subject, not two. Splitting a tired student across two new tutors in the same month usually produces two half-hearted efforts. Pick the subject where the gap is widest or where an internal assessment is closest, fix the pattern there, then add the second once the first is steady. Send recent marked work with the request so the tutor arrives with a diagnosis in progress. Grade 11 is genuinely the right year for this, and it gets harder after it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Physics and Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on the level. At MYP Sciences, a single tutor covering both is common and often sensible. At higher level in the Diploma Programme, the two diverge enough that a genuine specialist in one is frequently only competent in the other. If both are needed at HL, two tutors usually produces a better result than one. Where a single tutor is preferred for scheduling reasons, ask which of the two they have actually taught to HL and how recently.

faqs.question: What happens in the first session?
faqs.answer: It should look more like an assessment than a lesson. A good tutor spends the hour finding out where the marks are actually being lost: reading recent tests, watching the student attempt a question unaided, asking about the school calendar and upcoming deadlines. By the end there should be two or three named gaps and a plan for the next three sessions. If the first session is a standard lecture on the current chapter, that is a signal worth acting on early.

faqs.question: Is weekend-only tutoring enough for a Diploma Programme student?
faqs.answer: It can work in Grade 11, particularly for one subject with steady weekly progress. It works less well in Grade 12 near an exam session, when short and frequent contact beats one long block, because feedback on a past paper is most useful within a day or two of attempting it. A common compromise on this corridor is one longer weekend session in person plus a shorter online session midweek. That keeps travel down without letting a week pass unmarked.

faqs.question: My child attends Lancers. Do you work with the school directly?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform with no affiliation to Lancers International School or any other school named on this page. Tutors are engaged by families directly and have no access to school systems, teachers or internal records. What a tutor can do is work from what you share: the school calendar, marked assignments, draft feedback and deadline dates. That information is what allows sessions to be planned around school requirements instead of running parallel to them.

faqs.question: What if we need to pause during school holidays or family travel?
faqs.answer: Pauses are normal and should be discussed with the tutor in advance rather than announced the day before. Most tutors hold a regular slot on the understanding that it will be used, so a fortnight of notice protects the arrangement. Long breaks carry a real risk: a slot released in December may be filled by January, particularly the popular early-evening ones. If the pause is unavoidable, ask whether a reduced schedule of one short online session a week would hold the place.

contentBlocks.heading: What Parents Search For, and What Actually Moves the Grade
contentBlocks.body:
Search terms are blunt instruments. Parents looking for IB tutors in MG Road Gurugram almost always type a subject and a place: maths tutor near me, physics tuition MG Road. Reasonable searches. But the thing being searched for is rarely the thing that shifts the grade.

Look at what actually goes wrong. A Grade 11 student loses marks in Physics because the working is not justified, not because the concept is unknown. A Chemistry internal assessment drops a band because the evaluation lists errors without discussing their effect on the result. An Economics answer describes at length when the command term asked for evaluation. None of these are subject-knowledge failures. They are assessment failures, and a tutor who only re-teaches content will not touch them.

So the more useful search, if it could be typed, would be something like: a tutor who marks against IB criteria, at my child's level, free on the one evening we actually have.

That is the request this page is built to answer. What follows covers what is realistic around MG Road specifically, how home, online and hybrid compare in an older and well-connected part of the city, which subjects come up most, and what happens between an enquiry and a first session.

One practical detail that parking and lift access do affect: session length. If a tutor loses twenty minutes at either end of a visit, a sixty-minute booking stops being worth the evening, and ninety-minute sessions tend to survive longer.
