contentBlocks.heading: Signals Worth Watching in October, January and March
contentBlocks.body:
Judging tutoring by the next report card is slow and unreliable. Judging it by what the student does differently is faster.

In October, the signal is language. A student receiving good support starts describing their work in the terms the assessment uses. They talk about what a criterion is asking for instead of whether the teacher liked it. That shift usually appears within five or six sessions.

In January, the signal is behaviour around mocks. Less last-night cramming. A revision order chosen for a reason. Timed practice attempted voluntarily, badly at first, which is fine.

In March, the signal is calm. Not confidence exactly, more that the student knows which topics are secure and which are not, and is spending time accordingly.

If none of those changes has appeared after a month of regular sessions, something is wrong with the match and it should be raised rather than tolerated. Tutors will also tell you when the issue is not academic at all. Sleep, screen habits and an overloaded activity schedule account for more stalled progress than weak teaching does, and a tutor who says so is being useful rather than evasive.
items: October: student adopts assessment language
January: revision planned rather than improvised
March: informed calm about what is secure
One month with no change means the match needs revisiting
Sometimes the blocker is schedule and sleep, not teaching

contentBlocks.heading: Tell Us Where the Year Has Started Going Wrong
contentBlocks.body:
Whatever month you are reading this in, the useful first message is the same shape. Grade and programme, subjects and levels, the mode you would prefer, and the evenings that are genuinely open.

Then add the evidence. A marked assignment with the criterion breakdown visible. A mock script. A line from a teacher that worried you. That single attachment will do more for the quality of the match than a paragraph of description.

An advisor will confirm availability with suitable tutors before sending names, and will be direct about what is realistic given the calendar. faqs.question: When in the academic year should we start tutoring if nothing is obviously wrong yet?
faqs.answer: August or September, if you can manage it. Starting before there is a problem means a tutor can spend three or four sessions working out where the student is genuinely weak while the pressure is low, then build a slow plan around the school's units. Starting after mock results means the same diagnosis has to happen in a week and the plan has to skip things. The earlier start also costs fewer total hours, which surprises most parents who assume early support means more sessions overall.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring easier to arrange in the HUDA sectors than elsewhere in Gurugram?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, for a practical reason. The sectors sit close together, roads inside the colonies move reasonably, and parking is straightforward, so a tutor can run consecutive sessions in Mayfield Garden and Malibu Towne without losing an hour in between. That makes them more willing to take an evening slot here. It does not guarantee a particular tutor is free on a particular evening, and for scarce Higher Level subjects the deciding factor remains who teaches the level well rather than who lives nearby.

faqs.question: Our child is in the Personal Project year and has done almost nothing. What can a tutor do?
faqs.answer: Mostly project management, and that is not a criticism of the student. The Personal Project has no weekly deadline, so it slides for perfectly organised children too. A tutor can break the remaining work into dated chunks, hold a short weekly check on progress, and make sure the process journal actually records decisions rather than being written retrospectively. The academic content is rarely the barrier. What fails is the sequencing, and that is fixable with a fortnight of structure if the deadline has not already passed.

faqs.question: How are fees worked out, and do they change during exam months?
faqs.answer: Rates follow the level and the scarcity of the subject, so Diploma Higher Level sciences and mathematics sit higher than Middle Years or Primary Years support. Mode matters too, since home sessions carry travel time and online does not. Extra sessions taken during a mock or exam month are charged at the same hourly rate rather than at a premium. Everything is agreed before booking, and you are told the rate for a specific tutor rather than a range, so there are no adjustments after the fact.

faqs.question: Can a tutor coordinate with our child's school teacher?
faqs.answer: Not directly, and not without you. IB Gram is an independent platform, so any contact with a school happens through the parent. What works well is passing on the school's written feedback: a marked criterion sheet, a report comment, a returned draft with annotations. A tutor reading the actual teacher's marking will align with it far better than one working from a general syllabus. Most families find that sharing two or three documents removes the need for any direct contact at all.

faqs.question: My child says online sessions are boring. Is that a real problem or just resistance?
faqs.answer: Usually it is a signal about the teaching rather than the medium. Online sessions go flat when the tutor talks for long stretches and the student watches. They work when the student is writing, solving or annotating on a shared screen and the tutor is interrupting. Ask to observe fifteen minutes of a session. If your child is passive for most of it, the problem is method and can be raised. If they are working throughout and still complaining, the objection is usually about the hour, not the format.

faqs.question: We may relocate within Gurugram mid-year. Does the tutoring arrangement survive that?
faqs.answer: Online arrangements survive a move entirely, which is one reason some families in this belt choose them despite preferring in-person teaching. Home arrangements depend on where you land. A move within the sector network or towards Sector 50, Nirvana Country or South City 1 is usually fine. A move across to the DLF phases or the Sohna Road side may put you outside a particular tutor's practical range, in which case either the mode changes to online or a different tutor is matched.

faqs.question: What if we need help in three subjects at once during Grade 12?
faqs.answer: You will almost certainly need more than one tutor, and the honest advice is to stagger rather than run all three at once. Three weekly subject sessions on top of school, internal assessments and the extended essay produces a student with no unallocated time, which is when things start being done badly. A common approach is to take the weakest two subjects first for six to eight weeks, then rotate. Advisors will say so rather than arranging three simultaneous engagements because it is easier to book.

faqs.question: Does the tutor follow the school's teaching order or the published syllabus order?
faqs.answer: The school's order, wherever possible, because a student being taught two topics at once tends to master neither. This is why the school name and the current unit are asked for at the start. Where the school has moved past a topic the student never absorbed, the tutor will run a parallel repair thread, usually the last fifteen minutes of each session, so the gap closes without derailing the current work. That balance is agreed with you, not decided silently.

introSummary: Parents comparing IB tutors in Sohna Road Gurugram almost always start with the hourly rate, which is the wrong number to start with. The figure that matters is what a single hour contains: how much of it is diagnosis, how much is teaching into the specific gap, and how much is a student silently copying worked examples. IB Gram screens qualifications and IB-specific experience, then matches on subject level, programme and mode, so the hour you pay for is spent on the thing that is actually broken.

contentBlocks.heading: What an Hour of IB Tutoring on Sohna Road, Gurugram Should Actually Buy
contentBlocks.body:
Take two sessions costing the same. In the first, the tutor works through a chapter, the student nods, both leave satisfied and nothing measurable has moved. In the second, the tutor spends fifteen minutes making the student attempt something unaided, discovers the actual failure point, and spends the remaining time there. Same rate. Very different purchase.

The distinction is not effort or qualification. It is whether the hour is spent teaching what the student cannot do or covering what the syllabus says comes next.

So a useful way to judge value is by output rather than by input. After a month, can the student attempt a question type they previously avoided. Has the number of unfinished timed papers dropped. Do they know which criterion they lose marks on.

There is a second cost most families ignore, which is total hours rather than hourly rate. A cheaper tutor who takes twelve sessions to fix what a stronger one fixes in six is more expensive, and the difference is worse than financial because those six extra weeks were spent in the school year, not outside it.

That is the frame this page uses throughout.

contentBlocks.heading: Where the Hours Go, Subject by Subject on Sohna Road, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Some subjects need more hours than parents expect and some need fewer, and knowing which is which protects the budget.

Math AA HL is the expensive one, honestly. Weakness there is usually structural rather than topical, sitting in algebraic manipulation two years back, and repairing it takes sustained weekly work rather than a burst before a test. Math AI HL is often cheaper to fix because the failure is frequently procedural: calculator fluency, choosing the right statistical test, presenting a model clearly.

Physics and Chemistry split into two distinct purchases. Internal assessment support is short and intense, perhaps six to eight sessions concentrated around the investigation and write-up. Ongoing subject teaching is a longer commitment, particularly where a school has moved quickly through organic chemistry or through the fields topics in physics.

Economics tends to need fewer total hours than families fear. Most of the loss is in diagram precision and in the quantitative work of Paper 3 at Higher Level, both of which respond quickly to drilling.

English A is the least predictable. Argument construction improves in visible steps, then plateaus, then jumps again after several weeks with nothing apparently happening. Budget for patience rather than for volume.
items: Math AA HL: sustained weekly work, structural repair
Math AI HL: often procedural, faster to correct
Physics and Chemistry IA: short intense block around the investigation
Economics HL: diagram accuracy and Paper 3 drills
English A: uneven progress, plan for weeks not sessions

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP Cost Different Amounts of Time
contentBlocks.body:
Rates differ across the three programmes, and so does the shape of what you are buying.

Primary Years support, ages three to twelve, is the least expensive per hour and the easiest to over-purchase. Two short sessions weekly usually beats one long one, and a child of eight will get very little from ninety minutes at the end of a school day. Parents sometimes buy more than the child can absorb because the rate feels low.

Middle Years support, ages eleven to sixteen, sits in the middle. It is often the best value in the whole range, because fixing criterion-based writing at this stage prevents a much more expensive Diploma problem later. A student who learns to interpret a task instruction properly in Grade 9 does not need to be taught it in Grade 12 while also revising for exams.

Diploma support, ages sixteen to nineteen, costs most, particularly at Higher Level and particularly in the sciences and mathematics. Extended essay supervision and theory of knowledge help are usually charged as separate engagements, since they are advisory work spread across months rather than weekly teaching.

Buy early where you can. Late Diploma support is the most expensive way to solve a problem that was cheaper in Grade 9.
items: PYP: lower rate, shorter sessions, easy to overbuy
MYP: usually the best value across the range
DP HL sciences and mathematics: the top of the range
EE and TOK: separate advisory engagements
Grade 1 to Grade 12 covered, priced by level not by age

contentBlocks.heading: Vatika Chowk at Seven: The Real Price of a Home Session
contentBlocks.body:
A home session on Sohna Road carries a cost that never appears on an invoice, which is the tutor's travel. Someone coming down from Golf Course Road or across from DLF Phase 5 in the evening is spending an hour on the road for an hour of teaching, and that shows up either as a higher rate, a narrower set of available slots, or a tutor who arrives at 7:20pm for a seven o'clock start.

Around Vatika Chowk the traffic is worst precisely when families want sessions. That is the trade-off to weigh, not an argument against home tutoring.

Home tutoring earns its premium with younger students, with anyone who needs their notebook physically inspected, and with students who will quietly do something else if not watched.

Online is cheaper for the same teaching quality and widens the pool of Higher Level specialists across Gurugram. During exam months it also allows sessions to be added at short notice, which travelling tutors cannot do.

Hybrid usually gives the best value here: one weekend session in person, midweek work online. Home tutoring may be available across the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57, Sohna Road and nearby communities depending on tutor schedules, and online support runs across the city for every supported subject.

contentBlocks.heading: Booking a Tutor Without Wasting the First Month
contentBlocks.body:
Most wasted money in tutoring is spent in weeks one to four, on a tutor who was never going to fit. The intake is designed to compress that.

Step one, you give the grade, programme, subjects and levels, the mode you want, and the evening slots that genuinely exist after school transport and activities.

Step two, an advisor asks what evidence you have. A marked internal assessment draft, a mock paper, a criterion sheet. This is the step families skip and the one that saves the most money, because a tutor working from a real script starts teaching in session one instead of session three.

Step three, a shortlist is prepared on subject depth at the correct level, programme experience, and whether the tutor can realistically reach Sector 49 or Sector 50 at the hour you need. Availability is confirmed before any name reaches you.

Step four, a diagnostic first session, after which you should receive a specific statement of what is wrong. Not a reassurance.

Step five, you decide whether to continue. Declining after one session is normal and costs one session.

Send a marked script: it removes two sessions of guesswork
Shortlist filtered by level, programme and reachability
Diagnostic first session with a specific written outcome

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 49, Sector 50 and the Sohna Road Corridor in South Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The corridor runs long and thin, which affects who can teach you. Vatika Chowk sits roughly at the centre, with Sector 49 and Sector 50 on the northern side and Nirvana Country just beyond. South City 1 links back towards the older sector network, and Sector 57 and Sector 65 sit across on the Golf Course Extension side.

A tutor based near Sector 50 can cover most of this without difficulty. A tutor based in DLF Phase 1 or DLF Phase 4 is making a longer trip and will typically offer fewer slots or a slightly higher rate to make the journey worthwhile.

The newer communities further down the road are where the mode decision tends to flip. Distance from the established tutor clusters means fewer people willing to travel, and families there often find that an online specialist is both cheaper and better than the nearest available person willing to drive out.

Delhi, Noida and Faridabad appear in searches because families relocate from them. For home tutoring they are not realistic. Online makes the distinction irrelevant, which is worth knowing before you narrow your search by postcode.

contentBlocks.heading: What You Are Paying to Have Checked
contentBlocks.body:
Part of the fee covers screening you would otherwise do yourself, badly, over several phone calls.

Academic qualifications are verified against documents rather than accepted from a written profile. IB teaching experience is examined separately from general teaching experience, because criterion-related assessment and command-term precision are not picked up automatically by someone who has taught the same subject on a national board for a decade. Identity is confirmed before a tutor visits a home. Subject knowledge is tested at the level claimed, so a tutor offering Chemistry HL is questioned on Chemistry HL.

What the fee does not buy is a prediction. There are no success percentages quoted on this page and no testimonials, because neither could be substantiated and a parent deciding on real money deserves better than decoration.

You can ask what was checked for the particular tutor you are considering, and the answer will be specific. You can also ask what was not checked, and that answer will be given too. Screening reduces risk. It does not eliminate the need for you to judge the first session yourself.

School assessment calendars also cluster demand. When three schools run mocks in the same fortnight, the tutors who teach those subjects are fully booked, and a family calling that week has fewer choices at any price.

contentBlocks.heading: Four Weeks In: Deciding Whether the Money Is Working
contentBlocks.body:
Set a review point at four weeks and actually use it. Six to eight sessions is enough to see whether the method suits the student and not enough for a report card to move, so judge the process instead.

Three things should be visible. The student can state what they are weak at in specific terms rather than saying they are bad at the subject. They attempt questions unaided that they previously skipped, even if the attempts are wrong. Preparation before a test has become slightly more organised.

If those have not appeared, the honest conclusion is that you are paying for company rather than teaching, and the arrangement should change.

Some caution about what four weeks cannot show. A student starting from a genuine two-year gap in mathematics will not have closed it, and expecting that will make you cancel something that is working. Ask the tutor at the outset how long they think the repair takes and hold them to their own estimate rather than to yours.

Nobody can guarantee a grade at the end of it, and any tutor who does should be treated with suspicion rather than relief.

Families targeting May 2026 or November 2026 should allow more runway than the calendar suggests, and younger Diploma cohorts gain the most from starting while there is still slack in the year.

faqs.question: Why do two IB tutors quote such different rates for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Level and scarcity account for most of it. A tutor who can teach Math AA HL or Chemistry HL to Diploma standard is drawn from a much smaller pool than one teaching Middle Years mathematics, and that scarcity shows in the rate. Travel is the second factor, since a home session on Sohna Road for a tutor coming from Golf Course Road includes an hour of unpaid driving. Experience with internal assessment supervision raises rates too, because that work is advisory and spread over weeks rather than taught in an hour.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor ever the better financial decision?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on what is broken. For content catch-up after an absence, or for straightforward practice and doubt-solving at Standard Level, a less expensive tutor is perfectly adequate and the outcome will be the same. Where it goes wrong is with structural weakness, particularly in mathematics, where a tutor who cannot quickly locate the underlying gap will spend eight sessions circling it. Count the total hours to a fix rather than the rate. The cheaper hour is frequently the more expensive term.

faqs.question: Can we start with just one session to see how it goes?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the recommended way to begin. The first session is deliberately weighted towards assessment, so the tutor spends most of it working out where the student actually fails rather than delivering content. Afterwards you should get a plain account of what was found and an estimate of how long correcting it takes. If you decide not to continue, you have paid for one session and learned something useful about the problem. No package or minimum commitment is required before that point.

faqs.question: We live near Vatika Chowk and evenings are chaotic. What time slot actually works?
faqs.answer: Later than you want and earlier than you fear. Traffic through this stretch is heaviest between roughly half past six and eight, which is exactly when most families want sessions, so a seven o'clock home session frequently starts at twenty past. Where the school bus returns early enough, a 5:30pm or 6pm slot is far more reliable. Where it does not, an online session at eight avoids the problem entirely and tends to start on time. Weekend mornings are the most dependable in-person option.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have any tie-up with GD Goenka World School or other schools nearby?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with GD Goenka World School, Pathways World School, Lancers International School, Scottish High International School or any other institution mentioned here. Schools are referenced because their timetables and assessment calendars affect when tutoring can be scheduled and when tutors are in short supply. Any contact with a teacher is handled by you as the parent. Tutors work with your family under a direct arrangement, not through the school.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week is sensible without overloading the student?
faqs.answer: For one subject, two hours weekly is the usual ceiling before returns start dropping, and a single well-run session plus independent practice often beats two rushed ones. Across multiple subjects, count the total evening commitment rather than per-subject frequency. A Grade 12 student with three tutoring sessions, school homework, an internal assessment and the extended essay has no unallocated time, which is when work quality collapses. Staggering subjects across the term generally produces better results than running everything simultaneously.

faqs.question: What happens to fees if we pause during school holidays?
faqs.answer: Sessions are arranged as they are booked rather than sold in long packages, so pausing is straightforward and costs nothing beyond notice to the tutor. mainEntity.name: Is a cheaper tutor ever the better financial decision?

introSummary: IB tutors in South City 1 Gurugram are available for home sessions, online sessions or a mix of both, covering Grade 1 to Grade 12 across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes. Subject to tutor availability, sessions can be set inside the South City 1 and Unitech Heritage City pocket itself. contentBlocks.heading: What breaks when an IB student in South City 1 changes tutors mid-course
contentBlocks.body:
Ask a parent in South City 1 what went wrong with the last tutor and the answer is rarely about subject knowledge. It is about the handover. A Diploma Programme student who switches tutors in October arrives at the new session carrying an internal assessment draft that a school supervisor has already commented on once, a set of topics the previous tutor decided to skip, and a working habit that took two months to build. None of that is written down anywhere.

So the first four sessions go on rediscovering it. The student re-explains the order their school teaches units in. The tutor re-tests ground that was already solid. By the time the real gaps surface, a term has gone.

This page exists because that is the most expensive failure in IB tutoring, and it is avoidable. IB tutors in South City 1 Gurugram can be matched with the previous work in view: the units already taught, the IA stage reached, the command terms the student keeps misreading, the papers already attempted and where marks were lost on them. IB Gram is an independent platform, so a tutor change is a change of person rather than a change of provider, and the record of what has been covered stays with the family.

Past papers attempted and where the marks went

The school deadline calendar, not a generic one

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP support across South City 1, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The three IB programmes fail in different ways, and a tutor who is good at one is not automatically useful in another.

In the Primary Years Programme, ages three to twelve, the risk is turning inquiry into worksheets. A PYP child in South City 1 who is struggling with reading fluency or number sense needs short, frequent sessions that stay close to the unit of inquiry the class is running, not a parallel syllabus of drill sheets sent home every week.

The Middle Years Programme, ages eleven to sixteen, is where most Gurugram parents first ask for help. The subject content is manageable; the criterion-related assessment is not. A student can understand the science perfectly well and still score poorly on Criterion C because they described a result instead of analysing it. That is a writing and framing problem, and it responds to a tutor who marks against the published descriptors rather than against a general sense of quality.

The Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, brings the timetable pressure: six subjects, an HL and SL split, internal assessments in each, plus the extended essay and theory of knowledge running underneath all of it. Support here is triage as much as teaching. Which two subjects are genuinely at risk, and which two are merely uncomfortable.
items: PYP: inquiry-linked reading, writing and number confidence
MYP: criterion descriptors, personal project, subject command terms
DP: HL and SL subject depth, IA milestones, EE and TOK
Grade 1 to Grade 12 across all three programmes

contentBlocks.heading: Where South City 1 sits in Gurugram, and why that changes the timetable
contentBlocks.body:
South City 1 is a central Gurugram residential pocket, and its position is unusually convenient by local standards. Unitech Heritage City and The Close sit inside the same stretch. DLF Phase 1 is a short run north, Sector 50 and the Sohna Road spine lie to the south east, and Nirvana Country and Sector 65 sit further out along the Golf Course Extension side.

In practice that means a tutor living anywhere along the Sohna Road to DLF Phase 4 band can usually reach a South City 1 home without the trip eating the session. The same is not true from Sector 65 or the far end of Golf Course Extension Road at half past six in the evening, when that road slows badly.

Home tutoring may also be arranged across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok and Sector 57, depending on tutor schedules. But the honest version is this: the further a tutor travels, the fewer slots they can offer you, and the more likely a rescheduled session becomes in exam month. Families who want a fixed weekday slot at seven in the evening usually do better with someone already inside the central band. Families who want a rare specialist at nine usually do better online.
items: Inside the pocket: Unitech Heritage City, The Close
Short runs: DLF Phase 1, Sector 50, South City 2
Slower in the evening: Sector 65, Golf Course Extension Road
Online covers all of Gurugram, including Delhi-based specialists

contentBlocks.heading: Subject by subject, from Math AA HL to English A around South City 1
contentBlocks.body:
Math Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the single most requested subject from South City 1 families, and the most common reason for a mid-year tutor change. Paper 3 rewards a student who can follow an unfamiliar extended investigation across several linked parts, and that is a different skill from finishing a textbook exercise set. Math Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level asks for something else again: statistical reasoning, modelling choices, and a willingness to justify an approximation in words.

Physics and Chemistry usually arrive as two problems wearing one coat. The content is behind, and the internal assessment has stalled. Those need separating. A tutor can rebuild kinematics or organic mechanisms in a fixed number of sessions. An IA with no measurable independent variable needs a redesign conversation instead, and more content teaching will not touch it.

Economics rewards diagram accuracy and evaluation more than memory. Students lose marks less often for drawing the wrong diagram than for an unlabelled axis and an evaluation paragraph that lists two sides without deciding anything.

English A sits apart from all of them. Paper 1 unseen analysis, the individual oral and the higher level essay reward reading habits built over months, so late help is possible but its ceiling is lower.
items: Math AA HL: Paper 3 investigations, proof, calculus depth
Math AI HL: statistics, modelling, interpretation in words
Physics and Chemistry: content repair separated from IA design
Economics: labelled diagrams, evaluation that reaches a judgement
English A: Paper 1 unseen, individual oral, HL essay

contentBlocks.heading: The school mix South City 1 families in Gurugram draw from
contentBlocks.body:
Children living around South City 1 are spread across several IB schools rather than concentrated in one, and the practical consequence is that no two neighbours are working to the same internal calendar. Lancers International School on Golf Course Road and Scottish High International School in Sector 57 are both realistic daily commutes from here. Pathways World School in the wider Gurugram region and GD Goenka World School towards Sohna Road draw families from this pocket too, usually with a longer bus run at either end of the day.

That longer bus run is the detail parents underestimate. A student leaving at half past six in the morning and returning at four will not absorb a demanding two-hour session at five. Splitting into two shorter weekday sessions, or moving the heavy subject to a weekend morning, tends to work better than pushing through.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. Naming them here is about matching rather than endorsement: a tutor who already knows how a particular school sequences its Diploma units, and when it sets internal draft deadlines, wastes less of the first month working it out from scratch.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram builds a shortlist for a South City 1 family in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The sequence is deliberately short, because a family that has already lost a term does not want a four-week onboarding.

First, a call that establishes the real state of things: programme and year, subjects and levels, what the last two report cards or mock results actually said, and which deadlines are near. Second, the constraint list, meaning the days that are free, the latest workable start time, and whether home sessions are wanted at all. Third, a shortlist of tutors whose subject depth and IB assessment experience fit, filtered by whichever of home, online or hybrid you chose. Fourth, a trial session, after which the tutor writes down what they found rather than only saying it went well.

Fifth, and this is the part that protects continuity: a short written plan naming the units to be covered, the IA milestones, and what should be visibly different in four weeks.

Availability depends on level and schedule. A Standard Level Economics slot on a Saturday morning is easier to fill than Math AA HL at eight on a weekday evening, and any honest advisor will tell you that before you rearrange your week around it.
items: Call: programme, levels, recent results, near deadlines
Constraints: free days, latest start time, format
Shortlist filtered by level experience and travel
Trial session with written findings, not a verdict
Four-week review point agreed at the start

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online and hybrid sessions that survive Gurugram traffic
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring is the default request from South City 1, and for younger students it is usually right. A PYP or early MYP child works better with someone physically at the table, and a parent can hear how the session is going without hovering over it.

For Diploma Programme students the calculation changes. The specialist you want for Math AA HL or Physics may live nowhere near the central sectors, and insisting on home sessions narrows the pool to whoever can drive here on a Tuesday. Online removes that constraint completely, and for late evening slots after eight it is often the only realistic option.

Hybrid tends to be the compromise families settle on without planning it: one home session a week for the subject that needs supervision, one online session for the specialist subject or for doubt-solving before a class test.

Here is the honest limitation. Online works badly for a student who will not keep the camera on, will not write on a shared document, or is sitting through it against their will. Nothing in the format fixes that, and a home tutor will not fix it either. That is a conversation to have before booking anything, because both formats assume a student who has agreed to be there.
items: Home: younger students, habit building, parent within earshot
Online: HL specialists, IA document work, post-eight slots
Hybrid: one supervised session, one specialist session
Travel premium and cancellation risk rise with distance

contentBlocks.heading: What a parent in South City 1 should expect to see in four weeks
contentBlocks.body:
Four weeks is roughly eight sessions. That is enough to change some things and not others, and knowing which is which prevents a lot of unnecessary tutor changes.

Things that should be visible by week four: the student can explain what a question is asking before attempting it, homework is being attempted rather than avoided, the tutor can name specific gaps instead of saying the basics are weak, and an internal assessment that was stuck has moved to a next stage.

Things that will not be visible by week four: a transformed grade. Predicted grades move slowly, and in the Diploma Programme they move mainly at mocks and major assessment points. No tutor can promise a particular score or a 7, and anyone offering a number in a first conversation is telling you about their sales process rather than their teaching.

If none of the week-four signs appear, silence is the wrong response. Ask the tutor to write out what they think the blocker is. Sometimes it is a genuine mismatch of style. Sometimes it turns out the student is sleeping five hours a night because of a co-curricular commitment nobody mentioned, and no amount of tuition is the fix for that.
items: Week four: gaps named specifically, not generally
Week four: a stalled IA has moved a stage
Not week four: a changed predicted grade
Written blocker note if nothing has shifted

contentBlocks.heading: The checks run before a tutor is recommended to a Gurugram family
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is about evidence, not adjectives. The checks are ordinary and worth stating plainly, because most disappointments trace back to one of them being skipped.

Identity and background are confirmed first. Then teaching history: which IB programmes, which subjects, at which levels, and for how long. A tutor who has taught Chemistry at Standard Level for years is not automatically ready for Higher Level option topics, and that difference should be established before a family discovers it during a session.

Assessment familiarity is checked separately from subject knowledge. Can the tutor talk about criterion-related marking, command terms, the internal assessment rubric for their subject, and how an examiner actually reads an evaluation. A subject expert without this can teach a topic beautifully and still leave a student writing answers that score poorly.

Then a practical screen: how they explain something a student has already misunderstood once, which is the real job.

References are asked for where available. There is a limit to what any screening catches, and personality fit is not something a check can predict. That is what the trial session is for, and it is why a first session should be treated as information rather than a commitment.
items: Identity and background verified before home sessions
Subject and level experience recorded separately
Assessment literacy tested apart from content knowledge
Demonstration built on a real misconception
References collected where available

contentBlocks.heading: Starting with an IB tutor near South City 1
contentBlocks.body:
Getting started takes one conversation rather than a form-filling exercise. Tell the advisor the programme, the year, the two subjects that worry you most, and the two evenings that are genuinely free. If there has been a previous tutor, say what worked and what did not: that single piece of information shortens the search more than anything else you can offer.

From there a shortlist can be reviewed, usually within a few days and subject to tutor availability. Home sessions inside the central Gurugram band are checked against real travel times rather than map distance, and if the timing does not work you will be told, rather than sold a slot that quietly collapses three weeks later.

The trial session is where the decision gets made. Sit in for the first ten minutes if you want to. Ask the tutor afterwards what they would work on first and why, and whether the deadline you are worried about is realistic. A tutor who answers that honestly, including when the answer is that it will be tight, is usually the one worth continuing with.
items: Have ready: programme, year, subjects with levels, free evenings
Say what the previous tutor did and did not fix
Shortlist reviewed subject to tutor availability
Trial session judged on diagnosis, not delivery

faqs.question: Can an IB tutor come home in South City 1, or is online the realistic option?
faqs.answer: Home sessions in South City 1 are often workable, because the pocket sits centrally and a tutor coming from Sohna Road, DLF Phase 1 or Sector 50 has a short run. Availability still depends on the subject and the slot you want. For Higher Level Physics or Math AA at eight in the evening, the pool of tutors willing to travel shrinks sharply, and online usually gives you a stronger specialist. Many families settle on one home session and one online session each week rather than choosing between them.

faqs.question: My child is halfway through DP1 and the current tutor is not working. Is it too late to change?
faqs.answer: Changing during DP1 is common and rarely a disaster, provided the handover is done properly. What matters is capturing where things stand before the new tutor starts: units covered, internal assessment stage, mock results, and the topics the previous tutor quietly avoided. Without that, the first month goes on rediscovery. With it, a new tutor can start from the real gaps by the second session. Changing in DP2 close to final exams is harder, and worth weighing against the cost of staying with a poor fit.

faqs.question: How much do IB tutors around South City 1 charge?
faqs.answer: Fees vary with programme, level, subject and format, so a single number printed on a webpage would mislead you. Higher Level Diploma subjects and internal assessment mentoring cost more per hour than MYP support. Home sessions carry a travel premium; online sessions usually do not. What you should ask for is the whole picture before starting: rate per session, session length, how many sessions a week are being suggested, and what happens to fees if you pause during school exams or a holiday.

faqs.question: Do you cover the extended essay and TOK, or only subjects?
faqs.answer: Extended essay mentoring, theory of knowledge support and internal assessment guidance can all be arranged, though they work differently from subject teaching. An extended essay needs a small number of well-timed sessions around research question framing, source handling and the first full draft, not a weekly slot running for a year. TOK support tends to cluster around the exhibition and the prescribed title essay. Your school supervisor remains the primary authority on both, and a tutor should complement that rather than compete with it.

faqs.question: Which subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in this part of Gurugram?
faqs.answer: Math Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Physics at Higher Level, and the less common option topics within Chemistry are consistently the hardest to fill for home sessions anywhere around the central sectors. There are fewer such tutors, and the ones who exist tend to have full evening schedules by August. English A at Higher Level is easier to find but harder to match well, because writing style matters more. For all of these, accepting online sessions widens the shortlist considerably.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor and my child do not get along?
faqs.answer: Say so early rather than waiting for the term to end. A mismatch of style shows up in the first three or four sessions: the student goes quiet, homework stops, or every session overruns because nothing is landing. A replacement can be arranged, and the handover notes from the first tutor pass to the second, so you are not starting from zero again. Describing what specifically was not working helps more than a general complaint, because that detail is what changes the next match.

faqs.question: Is a tutor from my child's own school a better choice?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and sometimes it is the worst available option. A tutor from the same school knows the internal deadlines and the order units are taught in, which saves setup time. But there are obvious complications where the same person also teaches or assesses your child, and most schools have policies covering this. An independent tutor who knows the programme well and asks for the school calendar in the first session usually reaches the same place without the awkwardness. IB Gram is not affiliated with any school, so matches rest on subject and assessment fit.

faqs.question: We are starting in January with the May session ahead. What can realistically be done?
faqs.answer: A January start before the May session is tight but not pointless, provided the goal is chosen honestly. Four months is enough to secure marks that are still in reach: paper technique, the topics carrying the most weight, past-paper timing under real conditions, and finishing an internal assessment that is still open. It is not enough to rebuild two years of a Higher Level subject from the beginning. A tutor who tells you otherwise in January is not being straight with you about what remains possible.

faqs.question: Do you work with PYP children, or is this mainly for Diploma students?
faqs.answer: Both. Support runs from Grade 1 through Grade 12, covering the Primary Years Programme, the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma Programme. What changes is the shape of the help. Younger children need shorter, more frequent sessions tied to the current unit of inquiry, with a parent nearby. MYP students usually need help converting understanding into criterion-based written work. Diploma students need subject specialists and deadline management. The tutor profile that suits a seven-year-old is rarely the right one for DP2.

What you should ask for is the whole picture before starting: rate per session, session length, how many sessions a week are being suggested, and what happens to fees if you pause during school exams or a holiday.

mainEntity.name: Do you cover the extended essay and TOK, or only subjects?

acceptedAnswer.text: Extended essay mentoring, theory of knowledge support and internal assessment guidance can all be arranged, though they work differently from subject teaching. An extended essay needs a small number of well-timed sessions around research question framing, source handling and the first full draft, not a weekly slot running for a year. TOK support tends to cluster around the exhibition and the prescribed title essay. Your school supervisor remains the primary authority on both, and a tutor should complement that rather than compete with it.

mainEntity.name: Which subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in this part of Gurugram?

acceptedAnswer.text: Math Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Physics at Higher Level, and the less common option topics within Chemistry are consistently the hardest to fill for home sessions anywhere around the central sectors. There are fewer such tutors, and the ones who exist tend to have full evening schedules by August. English A at Higher Level is easier to find but harder to match well, because writing style matters more. For all of these, accepting online sessions widens the shortlist considerably.

mainEntity.name: What happens if the tutor and my child do not get along?

acceptedAnswer.text: Say so early rather than waiting for the term to end. A mismatch of style shows up in the first three or four sessions: the student goes quiet, homework stops, or every session overruns because nothing is landing. A replacement can be arranged, and the handover notes from the first tutor pass to the second, so you are not starting from zero again. Describing what specifically was not working helps more than a general complaint, because that detail is what changes the next match.

mainEntity.name: Is a tutor from my child's own school a better choice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, and sometimes it is the worst available option. A tutor from the same school knows the internal deadlines and the order units are taught in, which saves setup time. But there are obvious complications where the same person also teaches or assesses your child, and most schools have policies covering this. An independent tutor who knows the programme well and asks for the school calendar in the first session usually reaches the same place without the awkwardness. IB Gram is not affiliated with any school, so matches rest on subject and assessment fit.

mainEntity.name: We are starting in January with the May session ahead. What can realistically be done?

acceptedAnswer.text: A January start before the May session is tight but not pointless, provided the goal is chosen honestly. Four months is enough to secure marks that are still in reach: paper technique, the topics carrying the most weight, past-paper timing under real conditions, and finishing an internal assessment that is still open. It is not enough to rebuild two years of a Higher Level subject from the beginning. A tutor who tells you otherwise in January is not being straight with you about what remains possible.

mainEntity.name: Do you work with PYP children, or is this mainly for Diploma students?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. Support runs from Grade 1 through Grade 12, covering the Primary Years Programme, the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma Programme. MYP students usually need help converting understanding into criterion-based written work. Diploma students need subject specialists and deadline management. introSummary: IB tutors in South City 2 Gurugram can be arranged for home or online sessions across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes, Grade 1 to Grade 12, subject to tutor availability. The useful difference on this page is timing. IB work is driven by fixed dates: internal assessment drafts, the extended essay checkpoints, mock exams in the new year, and the written papers in the May 2026 or November 2026 session. Sessions planned against those dates achieve more than the same number of hours spread evenly.

contentBlocks.heading: The IB calendar decides the tutoring timetable in South City 2
contentBlocks.body:
Most tutoring around South City 2 gets planned around the school week. It should be planned around the assessment calendar, because that is what actually generates the pressure.

In the Diploma Programme the fixed points are these: internal assessment drafts falling across DP1 and early DP2, an extended essay with supervisor checkpoints running from the middle of DP1, the theory of knowledge exhibition and then the prescribed title essay, mock exams somewhere around January and February, and the written papers themselves in the May 2026 or November 2026 session. Every one of those has a preparation window, and the windows overlap.

The Middle Years Programme has its own version. Criterion-assessed tasks arrive in clusters near the end of each unit, and the personal project sits over the final year. Even in the Primary Years Programme there is a rhythm set by the units of inquiry and, in the last year, the exhibition.

Once those dates sit on a single sheet, the question stops being how many hours a week and becomes which weeks. Tutoring for a South City 2 family can be booked that way: heavier before a draft deadline, lighter through a settled stretch, intensive in the four weeks before mocks.

contentBlocks.heading: South City 2, Nirvana Country and the Sohna Road side of Gurugram

Which is why the first question in a call is often not who is the strongest tutor, but who can reliably be here at the hour you actually want.

Home tutoring may also be arranged towards Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok and Sector 57, depending on schedules. contentBlocks.heading: Choosing home, online or hybrid sessions in South City 2, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The three formats are not interchangeable, and the right one usually changes as the year moves.

Home sessions are strongest for building a habit. A fixed slot, a tutor at the table, a parent within earshot: for MYP students, and for anyone who has been quietly avoiding a subject for a term, that physical presence does most of the work.

Online sessions are strongest for depth and for timing. A Higher Level specialist can be matched without reference to where they live, screens can be shared for past paper walkthroughs, and a session fits into a gap no travelling tutor could reach. For internal assessment work in particular, where tutor and student need the same document and the same data set open, online often beats sitting side by side.

Hybrid is what the assessment calendar pushes families towards anyway. Weekly home sessions through the settled part of a term, then a switch to shorter and more frequent online sessions in the fortnight before a draft or a mock.

The trade-off is real. Hybrid asks the tutor to hold one plan across two formats, and a tutor who treats the online session as a lesser version of the home one will lose the thread within a month.
items: Home: routine, supervision, younger students
Online: HL specialists, shared documents, late slots
Hybrid: settled weeks at home, deadline weeks online
Ask how notes carry across formats before you commit

contentBlocks.heading: Which South City 2 subjects need a specialist and which need a fixer
contentBlocks.body:
Requests from this pocket fall into two categories, and confusing them wastes both money and time.

The first is a specialist need. Math Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Math Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, and Physics at Higher Level want someone who has taught that exact level, because the distance between Standard and Higher Level in those subjects is not a matter of extra questions at the end of the chapter. Paper 3 in the Mathematics courses is an extended investigation, and preparing a student for it looks nothing like drilling exercises.

The second is a fixer need. Chemistry where the content is fine but the internal assessment has no workable research question. Economics where the diagrams are accurate and the evaluation paragraphs decide nothing. English A where the individual oral is three weeks away and the student has not chosen a global issue that can carry ten minutes of analysis. These are short engagements, sometimes four sessions in total, and a long weekly booking is the wrong instrument.

Ask which one you are buying. A specialist hired for a fixer problem will teach content agreeably for two months and never touch the thing that was stuck.
items: Specialist: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics HL
Fixer: stalled Chemistry IA, weak Economics evaluation
Fixer: English A individual oral, global issue selection
Short engagements exist and are often the cheaper answer

contentBlocks.heading: From first call to trial session for a South City 2 family
contentBlocks.body:
The process runs in five steps and none of them take long.

One, a call covering programme, year group, the subject list with levels marked, and the assessment dates that are closest. Two, the practical constraints, meaning which evenings are open, the latest start time that works after school buses and activities, and whether home sessions are wanted or online is acceptable. Three, a shortlist drawn from tutors whose subject and level experience match, filtered by format and by realistic travel from your side of Sohna Road. Four, a trial session treated as a diagnostic rather than a sample lesson, after which the tutor states what they found. Five, a plan naming the units, the milestones and the review point.

Nothing there is complicated, but each step is a place where matches go wrong. Skip step one and you get a tutor for the wrong level. Skip step two and you get a tutor who cancels. Skip step four and you get three months of pleasant sessions that never address the thing you were worried about in the first place.

Availability depends on level and schedule, and evening slots in the run-up to mock exams fill early.

contentBlocks.heading: How PYP, MYP and DP assessment differs for South City 2 students in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The assessment logic changes three times as a child moves through the IB, and each change catches families out.

In the Primary Years Programme, ages three to twelve, there is no external assessment at all. Progress is judged through the units of inquiry and teacher observation, so tutoring should feed back into class work: reading fluency, written expression, number confidence. Importing a workbook syllabus from another board here creates a second, competing curriculum and usually makes the child slower rather than faster.

In the Middle Years Programme, ages eleven to sixteen, assessment becomes criterion-related. Each subject carries four criteria marked against published descriptors, and work is judged on best fit rather than a running total of marks. This is the stage where capable students first start losing marks for reasons they cannot name.

In the Diploma Programme, ages sixteen to nineteen, internal assessment and external papers combine into a grade out of seven per subject, with the core adding points on top. Tutoring here has to hold both halves at once, because the coursework clock and the examination clock run at different speeds and only one of them is visible on the school timetable.
items: PYP: no external exams, inquiry-linked support only
MYP: four criteria per subject, best-fit judgement
DP: IA plus external papers, graded out of seven
Core points from the extended essay and TOK

A tutor who assumes a standard sequence will be teaching the wrong topic at the wrong time for at least one of them.

So the first thing a good tutor asks for is the school assessment calendar, not the textbook.

contentBlocks.heading: What is checked before a tutor reaches your door in South City 2
contentBlocks.body:
Four checks, in order, and each one exists because of a specific failure it prevents.

Identity and background verification comes first and is not negotiable for anyone entering a home.

Teaching record comes next: which IB programmes, which subjects, and crucially which levels, recorded separately. Standard Level and Higher Level are different jobs in Mathematics and the sciences, and a profile that blurs them is a profile that will disappoint someone.

Assessment literacy is treated as its own check rather than assumed from subject knowledge. A tutor is asked how they would take an internal assessment from research question to evaluation, what a given command term actually demands in their subject, and how criterion descriptors change what a strong answer looks like. Plenty of capable graduates fail this part.

A teaching demonstration follows, built around explaining something a student has already got wrong once. Re-explaining is a harder skill than explaining, and it is the skill you are paying for.

References are collected where available. None of this predicts whether a particular tutor and a particular fifteen-year-old will work well together, and no screening process should be described as if it did.
items: Identity and background verified before home visits
Levels recorded separately from subjects
Assessment literacy tested on IA, command terms, descriptors
Demonstration on a real student error
Fit still decided at the trial, not by screening

contentBlocks.heading: Warning signs and honest limits in IB tuition near South City 2
contentBlocks.body:
Some things are worth being sceptical about, and they come up often enough to name plainly.

A tutor who offers a specific grade before meeting the student is describing a sales position, not a teaching plan. Predicted grades are set by schools on evidence, and final grades are decided by external examiners on work produced under exam conditions. A number offered in a first phone call is worth nothing.

A tutor who insists on teaching their own sequence rather than the school's is building a second syllabus for a student who is already short of time.

A tutor who will not put anything in writing after four weeks is difficult to hold to account, and by the time that becomes obvious a term has usually gone.

And the limit that applies to everybody: tutoring cannot fix a sleep problem, an attendance problem, or a subject combination that was wrong from the start. A student carrying three Higher Level sciences they did not want is not short of tuition. Sometimes the honest recommendation is a conversation with the school about subject choices, and a good advisor will say so even though it means fewer sessions booked.
items: Grades promised before a first meeting
A parallel syllabus that ignores the school's order
Nothing written down after four weeks
Tuition cannot repair sleep, attendance or wrong subject choices

contentBlocks.heading: Booking a first IB session near South City 2
contentBlocks.body:
Starting is a phone call, and the useful version of that call has four things ready: programme and year, subjects with levels, the next two assessment dates you know about, and the evenings that are genuinely free.

With those, a shortlist can be prepared and reviewed, subject to tutor availability. Home options around South City 2, Nirvana Country and the Sohna Road sectors are checked against real travel at the hour you want rather than at midday. If a slot cannot be covered reliably, you will hear that instead of being booked into something fragile that quietly falls apart in week five.

Then a trial session. Ask the tutor afterwards for three things: what they believe the main gap is, what they would do in the first month, and whether the deadline worrying you is achievable. Those answers tell you more than any profile ever will.

If the fit is wrong, say so early. A different match can be arranged without running the whole process again, and the notes from the first tutor go with it.
items: Bring: programme, levels, next two deadlines, free evenings
Travel checked at your hour, not an average
Trial questions: main gap, first month, deadline realism
Tutor changes keep the existing notes

faqs.question: When in the IB year is the best time to start tutoring?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do. The two strongest starting points are the beginning of DP1, when the internal assessment sequence has not yet built up, and the eight weeks before mock exams, when there is still time to act on what the mocks reveal. Starting in the middle of DP2 works, but the goal narrows to exam technique and finishing coursework rather than rebuilding understanding. For MYP, the useful moment is usually right after a report shows criterion marks slipping while class participation looks fine.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the internal assessment without doing the work for the student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is clearer than parents expect. A tutor can question a research question until it becomes measurable, point out that a data set is too small to support a conclusion, explain what the evaluation criterion is really asking, and mark a draft against descriptors. A tutor cannot write sections, supply the analysis, or design the investigation. Your school also runs its own academic honesty checks and supervisor meetings, and any tutor working around those is putting the student at genuine risk.

faqs.question: Are online sessions good enough for Higher Level Physics or Mathematics?
faqs.answer: For most students they are better, not merely acceptable. Higher Level specialists are scarce, and restricting the search to people who can drive to South City 2 on a weekday evening shrinks the pool considerably. Online allows worked solutions on a shared screen, past papers annotated in real time, and shorter sessions placed close to a deadline. The requirement is a student who will write while the session runs rather than watch it. If that is in doubt, start with home sessions and move online later.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do IB students in South City 2 usually take?
faqs.answer: It varies with the load and the point in the year, so a fixed answer would be dishonest. A common pattern is one session a week per subject during settled teaching periods, rising to two or three in the fortnight before a draft deadline or mock exams, then dropping again. Two subjects at two sessions each every week for a whole year is more tuition than most students can absorb alongside school, and it tends to produce fatigue rather than better marks.

faqs.question: What does extended essay support actually involve?
faqs.answer: A small number of well-placed sessions rather than a standing weekly slot. The first cluster deals with choosing a subject and narrowing a question until it can be answered in four thousand words. The second deals with sources, method and structure before the first full draft. The third comes after supervisor feedback, when the argument usually needs tightening and the evaluation needs strengthening. Your school supervisor stays the formal authority throughout, and a tutor who contradicts that guidance is creating a problem rather than solving one.

faqs.question: Do tutors follow the school's teaching order or their own?
faqs.answer: The school's, in almost every case. Diploma subjects can be taught in several valid sequences, and a tutor running a different order forces the student to hold two versions of the course at once. The exception is deliberate and temporary: when a foundation topic from an earlier year is missing, that gap has to be filled before the current unit will make sense. A tutor should say when they are doing this and why, and it should be a detour rather than a new route.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum commitment, and can we pause during school exams?
faqs.answer: Terms vary by tutor, so agree them before the first paid session rather than after. Ask three things directly: whether there is a minimum number of sessions, how much notice a cancellation needs on either side, and what happens during school examination weeks and holidays. Most families need at least one planned pause each year. A tutor who is inflexible about a break during the school's own exam fortnight is not organising their work around the student's calendar.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP and the marks dropped without the understanding dropping. What is going on?
faqs.answer: This is the most common MYP complaint and it is usually an assessment problem rather than a knowledge problem. Criterion marks reward specific behaviours: analysing rather than describing, justifying a method, evaluating limitations, using subject terminology precisely. A student can know the material and still write an answer that satisfies none of those descriptors. The fix is short and targeted. Mark two or three past pieces against the actual criteria with the student watching, and the pattern usually becomes obvious within a session or two.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor start near Nirvana Country and South City 2?
faqs.answer: It depends on subject, level and the slot requested, so no fixed turnaround is promised. Common MYP subjects and Standard Level Diploma subjects at reasonable hours are usually the quickest to arrange. Higher Level Mathematics, Higher Level Physics and late evening slots take longer, and the wait grows sharply between December and February when mock preparation absorbs the available tutors. Accepting an online option, or a slightly different day, is normally what shortens the wait.

introSummary: IB tutors in Sushant Lok 1 Gurugram can be arranged as home sessions, online sessions or a mix of both, for students from Grade 1 to Grade 12 across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programme. IB Gram is an independent platform: it reviews a tutor's subject level, teaching history and availability, then puts two or three names in front of you with the trade-offs written down. What follows is a first session that diagnoses the gap and sets a short plan, rather than a term-long commitment signed on the strength of a phone call.

contentBlocks.heading: What the First Hour With a Sushant Lok 1 Tutor Should Produce
contentBlocks.body:
A first session should not feel like a sales call. It should feel like a diagnosis. Sixty to ninety minutes in, you want three things you can point at: where the gap actually sits, what the tutor intends to do about it over the next four sessions, and how that plan fits around the school deadlines already on the calendar.

Most parents searching for IB tutors in Sushant Lok 1 Gurugram arrive after a report or a mock that went differently than expected. The instinct is to book fast. The more useful move is to spend the first meeting getting the diagnosis right, because a tutor working on the wrong problem is expensive in a way that has nothing to do with fees.

Sushant Lok 1 sits in the older, lower-rise part of central Gurugram, next to South City 1 and within sight of DLF Hamilton Court. Families here can reach a fair number of schools inside twenty-odd minutes on a clear evening, which widens the pool of tutors who could realistically come home. It also means Golf Course Road traffic, not goodwill, decides whether a 6 pm slot is honest.

So treat the first session as a scheduling test too. A tutor who arrives late twice in the opening fortnight has told you the mode is wrong, not that the tutor is.
items: A written gap summary after the first sitting
A four-session plan, not a year-long promise
Timings tested against a real weekday evening
School deadlines listed before topics are chosen
Clear statement of what will not be covered

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Tutors Are Shortlisted for a Sushant Lok 1 Family
contentBlocks.body:
Matching begins with the syllabus document, not the subject name. An enquiry that reads 'Maths, Grade 11' is not yet a brief. Math AA HL and Math AI HL pull apart sharply after the first term, and a tutor fluent in one can be slow and unconvincing in the other.

The intake conversation therefore asks for the level, the school's assessment calendar, the last two or three pieces of written feedback, and whether an internal assessment is already underway. A student four weeks from an IA deadline needs a different tutor from a student eight months out with a shaky algebra base.

Then a shortlist is built. Two or three names, with the reasoning attached rather than hidden. This tutor has carried Physics HL groups through several May sessions. That one is stronger on MYP criterion writing and weaker on timed exam drilling. You get told the trade-off.

Availability is checked last, and checked plainly. A tutor who can only hold Saturday mornings is offered as a Saturday-morning option, subject to tutor availability, not dressed up as flexible.

Fees are raised before the trial rather than after it. They move with level, subject rarity and whether someone is travelling into Sushant Lok 1 or teaching from a screen. If nothing in the pool fits, saying so beats filling the slot.
items: Level confirmed before subject: AA HL, AI SL, MYP by year
Last written school feedback read, not summarised
Two or three names with stated strengths and gaps
Fee range given before a trial is booked
Availability described as it is, not as it could be

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP or DP: Naming the Stage Before Naming the Subject
contentBlocks.body:
Support runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12, which in practice is three quite different jobs wearing one label.

At the Primary Years end, ages three to twelve, the work is mostly about protecting inquiry while repairing mechanics. A seven-year-old who cannot decode fluently will struggle inside a unit of inquiry however well that unit is designed. Reading, number sense and confidence are the targets, and the tutor's discipline is to fix them without turning Saturday into a worksheet factory.

Middle Years students, roughly eleven to sixteen, bring a translation problem. The child understands the science. The criterion-related task is asking for something else: a hypothesis with justification, a reflection on method, a specific band descriptor evidenced in writing. Marks disappear in the space between knowing and showing.

The Diploma Programme, sixteen to nineteen, is a two-year calendar rather than a subject. Internal assessments, the extended essay, TOK and papers whose command terms carry exact meaning. 'Evaluate' and 'explain' are not swappable, and students who treat them as such lose marks they had genuinely earned elsewhere.

Naming the stage first is what stops a capable tutor being booked for the wrong problem. It is also the fastest way to shorten a shortlist honestly.
items: PYP: decoding, number sense, inquiry habits kept intact
MYP: criterion language, justification, reflection writing
DP: IA scaffolding, EE mentoring, TOK, command terms
Grade 1 to Grade 12 across all three programmes
May 2026 and November 2026 sessions planned backwards

contentBlocks.heading: Travelling to Your Door in Sushant Lok 1, or Meeting on Screen
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring may be available across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57 and Sohna Road, depending on tutor schedules. From Sushant Lok 1 the practical radius is generous, because the colony sits in the middle of most of it rather than at one end.

Home sessions work best between roughly 4 pm and 7 pm, and for subjects with wide tutor supply: MYP mathematics, sciences up to Grade 10, English A. Nobody is fighting the Golf Course Road crawl in both directions, and a younger child stays in a room where they already concentrate.

They work badly in two situations, and it is worth being blunt about them. A 9 pm Diploma slot after sport means a tutor travelling home close to midnight, and that arrangement quietly falls apart around week six. A rare requirement, say Math AI HL taught by someone who has actually marked it, may not exist within driving distance on the evening you need it.

Online tutoring stays available across Gurugram for every supported IB subject, and it fixes both problems. Past-paper work suits a shared screen unusually well, with the question, the markscheme and the student's attempt visible together. It suits a restless Grade 4 far less.

Hybrid is where most Diploma families land after a term of experimenting.
items: Home sessions strongest in the 4 pm to 7 pm window
Online for rare subject levels and late evening slots
Hybrid: weekly at home, extra revision online near exams
Screen sharing suits past papers and markscheme work
Younger students usually do better in person

contentBlocks.heading: Math AA HL, Physics and the Subjects That Need a Specialist
contentBlocks.body:
Six subjects account for most of what arrives from this part of the city, and they fail in different places.

Math AA HL leads by a distance. The usual break point is not calculus itself but the algebraic fluency underneath it: a student who is slow with rearrangement loses the time they needed for the actual question. An IB maths tutor in Sushant Lok 1 earns their fee by rebuilding that base while the syllabus keeps moving.

Math AI HL is the quieter difficulty. Fewer students sit it, so fewer tutors have taught it repeatedly, and the modelling-heavy questions reward an instinct that pure-maths teaching does not always build.

Physics separates students where algebra meets a diagram. Chemistry tends to come apart in organic mechanisms and in the calculation-heavy sections of the internal assessment rather than in the theory a student can recite.

Economics is the one parents underestimate. Diagram accuracy and the evaluation paragraph carry more weight than content recall, and students who write fluently but never evaluate stay stuck at the same band.

English A is hardest to shop for, because progress is slow and hard to see from week to week. Judge it on the quality of the annotation in a student's copy of the text, not on the mark after four sessions.
items: Math AA HL: algebraic fluency before calculus content
Math AI HL: modelling instinct, thinner tutor supply
Physics: translating a diagram into an equation
Chemistry: organic mechanisms and IA calculations
Economics: diagram accuracy plus evaluation writing
English A: annotation quality as the early signal

contentBlocks.heading: What Four Weeks of Honest Progress Looks Like
contentBlocks.body:
Marks are a lagging indicator. In four weeks a well-matched tutor rarely moves a grade, and any tutor who promises one is telling you something about their sales technique rather than their teaching.

Watch other things instead. Does your child start the homework without being asked three times? That single change usually arrives before any mark does, and it arrives because the work stopped feeling impossible. Look at the notebook: are there worked steps, or only final answers copied down? Ask the student to explain one topic aloud at dinner. Fluency in that explanation predicts more than a test score collected under different conditions.

By the fourth session you should also be able to name the plan. Not in detail, but in outline: we are fixing rearrangement and indices, then moving to differentiation, then past papers from November sessions.

If none of that has happened after a month, raise it directly. A tutor change is a normal event and not a failure of anybody's judgement. Matching involves people, and people occasionally do not suit each other. Say so early, while there is still room in the year to recover.

contentBlocks.heading: The Checks Run Before a Tutor Name Reaches You
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is a process, not a badge. What gets verified is documentary and specific.

Qualifications are checked against the level being taught, which matters more than a general degree. A master's in physics does not by itself mean someone has taught Physics HL to the current syllabus, so the question asked is which levels and which sessions. Teaching history is reviewed for continuity: how long with previous students, and whether those students stayed through a full year or left after a month.

Subject knowledge is checked at the assessment level. For Diploma subjects that means command terms, internal assessment criteria and the structure of the papers. For Middle Years it means the criterion descriptors a student is actually marked against. Identity documents are confirmed before any home visit is arranged in Sushant Lok 1 or anywhere else in Gurugram.

None of this predicts chemistry between a tutor and a fifteen-year-old, and nobody should claim it does. It filters out the clearly unsuitable and leaves you a smaller set of plausible people to judge for yourself. The judging is still your job, and the trial session exists so you can do it.
items: Qualifications matched to the exact level taught
Teaching history reviewed for student retention
Command terms and IA criteria checked, not just content
Identity confirmed before any home visit
Screening filters candidates; it cannot predict rapport

contentBlocks.heading: Starting in Gurugram Without Committing to a Full Term
contentBlocks.body:
The first step is a conversation, and it is short. You describe the student: grade, programme, subject level, the school, what the last piece of feedback said, and which evenings are genuinely free once school transport and activities are counted.

An advisor comes back with two or three tutors who fit, along with what each is stronger and weaker at, and a fee range for the level. Availability is confirmed at that point rather than assumed, because a name you cannot actually book is not a shortlist.

Then a first session, in your home in Sushant Lok 1 or online, whichever the timing supports. That session produces the gap summary and the short plan described above. If the fit is wrong, say so and a different name can be reviewed.

For students sitting May 2026 or November 2026 papers, starting earlier buys options that a late start simply does not. And if the student is already in the middle of an internal assessment, mention it in the first message. It changes who gets shortlisted more than anything else you could tell us.
