faqs.question: Can I get an IB home tutor in Sushant Lok 1, or will everything be pushed online?
faqs.answer: Home tutoring may be available in Sushant Lok 1 and across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sector 57 and Sohna Road, depending on tutor schedules. The colony's central position helps, because tutors can reach it from several directions. The honest limits are timing and subject rarity: a 9 pm Diploma slot or an unusual Higher Level subject may only be workable online. If a home tutor is offered for a slot needing an hour of peak-hour driving each way, ask how long that will realistically hold before you build a term around it.

faqs.question: How are fees decided for IB tuition near Sushant Lok 1?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the level, the subject, the tutor's experience with that exact syllabus and whether the session is at home or online. Diploma Higher Level subjects sit above Middle Years support, and rarer levels such as Math AI HL cost more because fewer tutors have taught them repeatedly. Home sessions carry travel time inside the rate. You are given a range before any trial is booked, not after it, and there is no obligation to continue if the first session shows the match is wrong.

faqs.question: My child starts DP next year at a school on Golf Course Road. When should we begin?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do. The useful window is the months before Grade 11 begins, when there is time to repair algebra, essay structure or lab writing without a live deadline in the way. Once the Diploma starts, internal assessments and the extended essay eat the calendar and tutoring turns reactive. Starting late is not fatal, and plenty of students recover ground, but the work is narrower and the choices fewer. Beginning before the first term removes that constraint entirely.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor and my child simply do not get along?
faqs.answer: Say so, and say so early. A mismatch found at week four costs a month; the same mismatch left until week twelve costs a term. Tell the advisor what specifically is not working, because 'it isn't clicking' is harder to act on than 'he explains too fast and never checks she has followed'. A different tutor can then be reviewed, subject to availability. No tutor suits every student, and treating a change as a normal adjustment rather than a complaint gets it done faster.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to Lancers, Scottish High or Pathways?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with any school, nor with the International Baccalaureate Organization. Those schools are named because families in Sushant Lok 1 and South City 1 attend them, and because a tutor who knows a school's assessment rhythm plans better. A tutor may have taught students from a school without representing it. If anyone claims insider knowledge of how a particular school marks internal assessments, treat that claim with suspicion.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring genuinely work for a subject like DP Chemistry?
faqs.answer: For most of it, yes, and for past-paper work it is arguably better. A shared screen puts the question, the markscheme and the student's own attempt side by side, which is awkward to arrange across a dining table. Mechanism drawing works well with a tablet and stylus. What online handles poorly is practical technique and the internal assessment stage where a student is fumbling with real apparatus at school. Many families run theory online and keep occasional home sessions for the practical write-up.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both regular subject teaching and IA support?
faqs.answer: Often, but confirm it at the start rather than assuming. Teaching a topic and mentoring an internal assessment are different skills: one is explanation, the other is asking questions until the student's own research question becomes answerable. Some tutors are strong at both. Others are excellent teachers who over-direct an IA, which is a real risk given academic honesty requirements. Ask directly how they handle an IA draft, and what they will refuse to do. A clear refusal is a good sign.

faqs.question: We live near DLF Hamilton Court. Which weekday slots are realistic?
faqs.answer: Between 4 pm and 7 pm is the sweet spot for home sessions, once school transport has come back and before the evening becomes a fight with homework. Sessions from 8 pm onwards suit older Diploma students but ask a lot of a travelling tutor, so those hold together better online. Weekend mornings are the quietest option and are usually easiest to book for students who need a longer, uninterrupted block for extended essay or internal assessment work.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a struggling Grade 10 student usually need?
faqs.answer: Two a week for one subject is a common starting point, with a third added only during a heavy assessment stretch. More than that tends to backfire, because a student needs unsupervised time to attempt problems badly before help is useful. If a student is behind in two subjects, it is usually better to run one properly than both thinly. The exact pattern depends on level, school workload and tutor availability, and it should be reviewed after the first month rather than fixed at the start.

contentBlocks.heading: The School Run From Sushant Lok 2 and What It Demands
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the timetable, because everything else follows from it. A child living in Sushant Lok 2 and studying at an international school on Golf Course Road or in Sector 57 leaves early, gets home somewhere between four and five, and then has music, swimming or a match on at least two evenings. That is the container any tutoring has to fit inside.

The schools around here also assess in bursts. Criterion-related tasks cluster before a break. Internal assessment drafts fall due within days of each other. Mocks arrive in a block. So a family that books a weekly slot in July and never revisits it will find the slot is wrong by October, not because the tutor changed but because the workload did.

Sushant Lok 2 sits against Golf Course Extension Road, with Ireo Skyon, M3M Merlin and DLF Park Place among the towers most enquiries come from. Access is easy in one direction and slow in the other, which quietly rules out some tutors and rules in others.

Parents comparing IB tutors in Sushant Lok 2 Gurugram tend to ask about subject expertise first. Ask about calendar awareness second, and the shortlist separates faster.

contentBlocks.heading: Where Sushant Lok 2 Students Lose Marks, Subject by Subject
contentBlocks.body:
The subject list from this pocket is narrow and it repeats: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A.

The first decision is which mathematics course a student sits, and it gets made at the start of Grade 11 with imperfect information. Analysis and Approaches rewards proof, algebraic manipulation and calculus fluency. Applications and Interpretation leans on modelling, statistics and using technology to reason about messy data. Students moved from one to the other mid-course lose ground, so an IB maths tutor in Sushant Lok 2 is often asked to advise on the choice before teaching a single topic.

In Physics, marks leak where a written scenario has to become a diagram, and the diagram an equation. Chemistry students frequently know their reactions and still lose internal assessment marks on uncertainty treatment and on the evaluation section.

Economics punishes students who describe rather than judge. Diagrams must be labelled precisely, and the higher bands reward a weighted judgement rather than a balanced list of two views.

English A is the slowest to shift. What improves first is the quality of the questions a student asks about a text, long before the essay mark moves.
items: AA versus AI: decided before Grade 11 settles it
Physics: scenario to diagram to equation
Chemistry IA: uncertainties and the evaluation section

contentBlocks.heading: From Enquiry to a Named IB Tutor in Sushant Lok 2
contentBlocks.body:
The sequence is deliberately short, and it runs in this order.

One: you send the specifics. Grade, programme, subject and level, the school, the tower or block in Sushant Lok 2, and the evenings that survive after activities. Two: an advisor reads the last piece of school feedback in its original wording rather than a summary, because a teacher's comment usually names the real problem better than a parent can.

Three: a shortlist of two or three tutors is put together, each with a note on what they handle well and where they are thinner. Four: availability is confirmed against your actual window, subject to tutor availability, and a fee range for that level is stated. Five: a first session is booked, at home or online.

What the process deliberately avoids is sending a long list of profiles and leaving you to guess. Ten names is not more choice. It is more work handed to a parent who has less information than the advisor does.

If the requirement is unusual and no strong match exists that week, you are told so. An empty answer given quickly is more useful than a weak match given confidently.

contentBlocks.heading: Three Programmes, Three Different Tutoring Jobs in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Parents usually name a subject. The programme is what decides the shape of the help.

In the Primary Years Programme, ages three to twelve, the tutoring worth paying for is quiet and structural: fluent reading, number relationships a child can see rather than recite, and enough writing stamina to take part in a unit of inquiry. Towards the top of the programme comes the exhibition, which asks a young child to sustain an independent piece of work for the first time.

The Middle Years Programme, eleven to sixteen, is graded against published criteria, and that is where families get caught out. A confident student can produce good science and still land in a middle band because the reflection was thin. The personal project in the final year rewards planning far more than talent.

The Diploma Programme, sixteen to nineteen, adds the core: theory of knowledge, the extended essay, and an internal assessment in every subject. Tutoring here is part teaching and part project management, because a student who misses a school draft deadline pays for it twice.

Support runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12, and the stage is confirmed before any tutor is proposed.

contentBlocks.heading: Documents, Levels and What Screening Cannot Tell You
contentBlocks.body:
Verification is worth describing plainly, because the word gets used loosely across the tutoring market.

Identity is confirmed with documents before a tutor is proposed for a home visit. Academic qualifications are checked, then checked again against the specific level requested, since a degree in economics is not evidence that somebody has taught the Higher Level paper structure. Teaching history is reviewed for how long tutors stayed with previous students, which is a duller signal than a list of qualifications and a more honest one.

For Diploma subjects the conversation covers assessment mechanics: command terms, the internal assessment criteria, the structure and timing of the papers. For Middle Years it covers the criterion descriptors themselves. A tutor who talks only about content and never about how that content is marked has told you something useful.

What none of this can establish is whether a particular adult will hold the attention of a particular teenager on a Wednesday evening. That is what a first session is for, and no amount of paperwork replaces it.

Screening is not a one-off event either. What families report after the first month feeds back into who gets suggested again, and that is a slower signal than a certificate but a more reliable one.

contentBlocks.heading: Signals a Parent Can Check Without Waiting for a Report Card
contentBlocks.body:
Waiting for the next report to judge a tutor wastes a term. Better evidence is available inside a month, and it is mostly behavioural.

Does the student bring a question to the session, or does the tutor arrive with everything already decided? A student who has started noticing what they do not understand is improving, whatever the marks say. Ask to see the working. Neat final answers with no method are a warning sign, particularly in mathematics, because they often mean the student is copying a pattern rather than following an argument.

Check whether the tutor references the school's own task sheet. Teaching that ignores the marking criteria produces students who understand the topic and still land two bands below where they should.

And look for one uncomfortable thing: a tutor willing to tell you something you did not want to hear. That the student is further behind than the school suggested, or that two sessions a week will not be enough this term. No one can promise a grade, and a tutor who avoids that conversation is managing you rather than teaching your child.

faqs.question: Are IB home tutors available inside the societies around Sushant Lok 2?
faqs.answer: Home tutoring may be arranged for addresses around Sushant Lok 2, including the towers along Golf Course Extension Road, depending on tutor schedules. Practical details decide it: visitor entry at the gate, whether the building allows a regular external visitor, and how the slot sits against the tutor's previous booking. IB Gram is not connected to any society or its management and arranges nothing on their behalf. Where timing or access does not work, the same tutor can usually teach the student online instead, at the same level and on the same plan.

faqs.question: My daughter has to choose between Math AA and Math AI. Can a tutor help decide?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the more useful early conversations. A tutor can look at her Grade 10 work, how she handles algebraic manipulation compared with data and modelling questions, and what she is likely to study after school. Analysis and Approaches suits students comfortable with proof and calculus. Applications and Interpretation suits students who reason well with statistics and technology. The school makes the final call with you, but walking into that meeting with an outside reading of her work helps a great deal.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting tuition in the middle of the school term?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, though what a mid-term start can achieve is narrower. The first few sessions get spent stabilising whatever is due immediately rather than repairing foundations, so progress feels slower before it feels faster. If the student is in the final months before an exam session, the plan becomes past papers and targeted gaps rather than a rebuild of the basics. Anyone promising a specific score from a late start is not being straight with you, and that is worth noticing early.

faqs.question: How do you handle a student who has two subjects going badly at once?
faqs.answer: Ordinarily by sequencing rather than doubling. Running two subjects with two tutors from the same week takes four or five hours out of an already full schedule, and the usual result is that neither improves. The better pattern is to fix the subject with the nearest deadline or the widest knock-on effect, often mathematics, then add the second once a routine holds. If both have imminent assessments, a lighter parallel plan is possible, but the trade-off should be named openly first.

faqs.question: Do tutors follow the school's marking criteria or their own approach?
faqs.answer: They should work from the school's task sheet and the published assessment criteria, and it is fair to ask for evidence of that in the first session. A student marked against Middle Years criteria needs teaching that names those criteria out loud. A Diploma student needs command terms treated precisely, because 'discuss' and 'outline' ask for different lengths and different structures. Teaching that ignores the marking scheme produces students who know the content and still miss the band they were aiming for.

faqs.question: What if we need to pause sessions during school holidays or travel?
faqs.answer: Pausing is normal and should be arranged directly with the tutor with reasonable notice. Many Sushant Lok 2 families travel in the summer and again in December, and a break of two or three weeks rarely undoes progress if the student keeps a small amount of work ticking over. Longer gaps do cost something, particularly in mathematics, where fluency fades faster than understanding. Restarting is subject to tutor availability, so share your dates early if you want the same slot back.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the MYP personal project?
faqs.answer: Support is possible, within limits that matter. A tutor can help a student narrow a topic, build a realistic timeline, structure the process journal and prepare for the report. What a tutor must not do is generate the content or make the decisions, because the personal project is assessed as the student's own work and academic honesty rules are taken seriously. A good mentor asks questions and refuses to supply answers, which students find frustrating and which is exactly the point of the exercise.

faqs.question: How quickly can sessions start after the first conversation?
faqs.answer: Often within a few days for common subjects and standard evening slots, and longer for rarer requirements such as Math AI HL or a specific Higher Level science at an awkward hour. Everything depends on tutor availability at that moment rather than on a fixed turnaround, and demand rises noticeably as the May and November sessions approach. If your window is narrow, say so at the start so that only genuinely available tutors reach your shortlist and no time is lost.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring cheaper than a tutor coming to Sushant Lok 2?
faqs.answer: Frequently, yes, because home sessions carry travel time that a tutor reasonably prices in, and Golf Course Extension Road takes what it takes. The gap is not enormous, and level matters more than mode: a Higher Level Diploma subject costs more than Middle Years support in either format. Some families use online purely to reach a specialist they could not otherwise book, which is a different reason from saving money and often the better one.

contentBlocks.heading: Sprint or Season: Two Reasons Sushant Lok 3 Parents Call
contentBlocks.body:
Almost every enquiry from this pocket falls into one of two shapes, and they should not be treated the same way.

The first is the sprint. A mock has come back badly, or a paper sits six to ten weeks out, and the family wants intensity. That work is real and it helps, but it has a ceiling. In eight weeks a good tutor can fix how a student reads a question, stop the errors that repeat across every script, drill the topics with the highest marks per hour, and get the timing under control. What eight weeks cannot do is rebuild two years of shaky algebra, and no tutor should pretend otherwise.

The second shape is the season. A parent calls in the first term, often before anything has gone wrong, because the subject choices look heavy or an older sibling struggled. This work is slower and quieter, and it compounds. Foundations get repaired while there is still slack in the calendar.

Parents searching for IB tutors in Sushant Lok 3 Gurugram should decide which of these they are buying before comparing anybody's fees. The two jobs need different tutors, different session lengths and different expectations.

Season: foundations, drafts, timetable management

The arrangement that fails is the one nobody stress-tested. A weekly home session at 7 pm is comfortable in September. In February, when a student wants three sessions in a week and two of them at short notice, a travelling tutor cannot always supply them, and the family discovers this at the worst possible moment.

So think about the exam term while choosing the mode. Online sessions scale up without a negotiation about traffic, which is why revision blocks so often move to screen even for families who prefer meeting in person.

The trade-off is genuine. Online loses something for younger children and for students who need somebody physically present to stay honest about the work.

A workable compromise: keep a fixed home session as the anchor, and add online sessions when the calendar tightens.

contentBlocks.heading: Six Weeks of Physics Revision Is Not Six Months of Physics
contentBlocks.body:
The subject mix here is predictable: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A. What changes with the calendar is what a tutor can usefully do in each.

Late in Math AA HL, the return comes from past papers sorted by topic, from a written list of the student's own recurring slips, and from timing drills. Early in the course, the same tutor would be repairing indices, surds and rearrangement, which pays far more but takes months to show.

Physics late means question-type recognition and method marks: writing the equation before the substitution, so that partial credit survives an arithmetic mistake. Physics early means the internal assessment, where a controllable variable and a large enough data set decide the mark before any analysis begins.

Chemistry follows the same split, with organic mechanisms and energetics dominating the revision weeks. Economics late is diagram discipline under a clock. English A resists sprinting more than any other subject, because argument quality is built slowly and cannot be drilled into place in a fortnight.

An IB maths tutor in Sushant Lok 3 asked for six weeks of help should tell you which of these two jobs they are doing.

contentBlocks.heading: What Late Help Can and Cannot Fix in PYP, MYP and DP
contentBlocks.body:
The programme decides how much a late start costs, and the difference is larger than most families expect.

Primary Years students, ages three to twelve, are the most forgiving. There is no external examination to miss, and a reading or number gap found in March can be worked on through the summer without consequence. The main risk at this stage is not the gap. It is a child quietly deciding they are bad at a subject.

Middle Years students, eleven to sixteen, sit in between. Criterion-related tasks recur, so a task lost in November can be answered better in February. What does not recover easily is a habit of writing reflections thinly, because that habit takes several assignments to change.

Diploma students carry the real cost. Internal assessments have school deadlines that do not move, the extended essay has a chain of drafts, and theory of knowledge sits on top of everything. A Grade 12 student calling in January can still improve technique substantially. They cannot recover an internal assessment already submitted.

Support runs from Grade 1 to Grade 12, with May 2026 and November 2026 as the fixed points a Diploma plan works backwards from.

contentBlocks.heading: Matching an IB Tutor When the Deadline Is Already Set
contentBlocks.body:
A late enquiry is matched differently from an early one, and it is worth knowing how.

With months in hand, the strongest teacher for the level is usually the right answer, even if their available slot is awkward. With weeks in hand, availability moves up the list, because a brilliant tutor who can start in three weeks is worth less than a good one who can start on Thursday.

The intake questions change too. For a sprint, an advisor asks for the mock paper itself, the mark breakdown and the exam date. For year-long support, the questions are about subject choices, the school's assessment pattern and what the student is like when work gets hard.

Either way you get two or three names rather than a long list, each with the reasoning stated, plus a fee range for the level and a plain note on what is realistic in the time available. Availability is confirmed with the tutor before the name reaches you, subject to tutor availability, so that nobody spends a week chasing a full calendar.

If the timeline genuinely does not allow what a parent is hoping for, that gets said at this stage rather than after four sessions.
items: Early enquiry: best teacher for the level wins
Late enquiry: availability rises up the ranking
Send the marked mock, not a description of it
Two or three names with a fee range attached
An honest note on what the remaining weeks allow

contentBlocks.heading: Judging Progress in a Sprint Versus Judging It Over a Year
contentBlocks.body:
The evidence you should look for depends on which job you bought, and using the wrong yardstick causes most of the unnecessary tutor changes.

In a short revision engagement, progress shows up as fewer repeated mistakes and better use of the clock. Ask to see two attempts at the same question type, two weeks apart. If the second one is faster and the method is written down before the numbers, the sessions are working, even if the raw mark has barely moved.

Over a longer engagement, the signals are slower and more structural. A student who used to wait for the tutor to start now arrives with a question. Homework gets attempted before it is understood, which sounds like a bad thing and is exactly the habit that produces independent learners.

In neither case should anybody be promising a grade. Predicted grades come from schools, final marks come from external moderation, and a tutor who talks about a guaranteed outcome is describing a sales position rather than a teaching one.

One more honest note: some students do not need a tutor at all. They need sleep, or fewer commitments, or a conversation with their school.
items: Sprint: same question type, two weeks apart, compared
Method written before the numbers appear
Season: student arrives with questions of their own
Attempting work before understanding it is a good sign
No guaranteed grades from any tutor, at any price

contentBlocks.heading: Gurugram Schools Around Sushant Lok 3 and Their Deadline Rhythm
contentBlocks.body:
Scottish High International School is the nearest of the well-known IB schools to Sushant Lok 3, sitting in Sector 57 itself. Lancers International School is over on Golf Course Road, Pathways World School draws from across the Gurugram region, and GD Goenka World School serves the Sohna Road side.

For a family weighing a sprint against year-long support, the school's own rhythm matters more than its reputation. A school that runs early mocks gives a Grade 12 student a real diagnostic in time to act on it. A school that sets internal assessment deadlines close together compresses the autumn and leaves the spring lighter. Knowing which pattern your child faces changes when tutoring is worth starting.

Ask the school for the assessment calendar and pass it on at the enquiry stage. Most parents do not, and it is the cheapest improvement available to a tutoring plan.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. Nothing here should be read as an endorsement by any of them, and a tutor who hints at influence over how a school marks its coursework has said something that should end the conversation. What a tutor can legitimately know is the published criteria and the dates you gave them.

Lancers International School, Golf Course Road
Pathways World School, Gurugram region
GD Goenka World School, Sohna Road side
Independent platform; no endorsement implied

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked, and Why It Matters More Under Time Pressure
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is ordinary administrative work, and describing it plainly is more useful than calling tutors verified and leaving it there.

Identity documents are confirmed before any home visit is arranged in Sushant Lok 3 or elsewhere in Gurugram. Qualifications are checked and then matched to the exact level requested, because teaching a subject and teaching its Higher Level paper structure are not the same claim. Teaching history is reviewed with attention to how long tutors held on to previous students.

For Diploma work, the interview covers command terms, internal assessment criteria and the shape of the papers. For Middle Years it covers the criterion descriptors a student is marked against.

This matters more, not less, when time is short. A family with eight months can absorb one wrong choice and correct it. A family with eight weeks cannot, because two wasted weeks is a quarter of what they have. So the shortlist for a late start is deliberately conservative: proven at the level, available now, and honest about what the remaining time allows.

None of it predicts rapport, which is what the first session is for.
items: Identity confirmed before a home visit is arranged
Qualifications matched to the exact level
Student retention treated as a signal
Command terms and criteria covered in the interview
Late starts get a deliberately conservative shortlist

contentBlocks.heading: Booking Sessions in Gurugram Before the Calendar Decides for You
contentBlocks.body:
Begin with a short message: the grade, the programme, the subject and level, the school, and whether you are after a revision push or ongoing support. If there is an exam or a draft deadline, give the date. If there is a marked mock, send it.

An advisor comes back with a small set of matched tutors, what each is strong at, a fee range for the level, and a realistic note on what the available weeks can achieve. Availability is confirmed before you see the names, subject to tutor availability.

Then a first session, at home in Sushant Lok 3 if the timing supports it or online if it does not. That session should end with the tutor telling you what they found and what they intend to do about it.

For students sitting May 2026 or November 2026 papers, the useful slots fill from the outside in: late evenings and weekend mornings go first. Asking early costs nothing and keeps the choice open.

And if you are unsure which of the two jobs you actually need, say that in the message. Working it out is part of the first conversation, and a family that has been told plainly they need six weeks rather than six months has been given something worth more than a tutor.
items: Say whether you want a sprint or ongoing support
Give the exam or draft deadline date
Send a marked mock paper if one exists
First session at home in Sushant Lok 3 or online
Weekend and late slots book out first

faqs.question: We are eight weeks from the mock. Is it too late to start tutoring in Sushant Lok 3?
faqs.answer: No, but be clear about what those weeks can deliver. A focused eight-week block can fix exam technique, cut down errors that repeat across every script, drill the highest-yield topics and get the timing under control. It will not rebuild foundations that took two years to weaken. The right plan starts from a marked script rather than the syllabus, and any tutor who promises a particular grade from an eight-week start is telling you what you want to hear.

faqs.question: Should we book a longer session or more frequent short ones?
faqs.answer: For revision, shorter and more frequent usually wins, because retrieval works better when it is spaced out than when it is stacked into one long sitting. Two sessions of an hour beat one of two hours for most students. Longer blocks make sense for internal assessment work or extended essay drafting, where a student needs time to get properly into the material before anything useful happens. The subject and the task should decide it, not habit or convenience.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor keep teaching once exams are over?
faqs.answer: Usually, and continuing with someone who already knows the student saves the two or three sessions a new tutor spends diagnosing. What often changes is the shape of the work. A revision tutor works from past papers and error lists; the same tutor supporting the next school year works from foundations and school deadlines. Talk about that shift explicitly, because a tutor who keeps drilling papers into a new academic year is solving a problem that has already gone away.

faqs.question: Do you offer group sessions, or is it always one to one?
faqs.answer: Matching is built around one-to-one work, since the whole value sits in teaching aimed at one student's specific gaps. Small groups can be arranged in some cases, most sensibly for two students at the same level in the same subject who study together anyway, and it depends entirely on tutor availability. Groups are cheaper per student and slower per student. For a Diploma student under deadline pressure, the trade-off rarely favours a group.

faqs.question: My son is in Grade 9 and doing fine. Is tutoring premature?
faqs.answer: Often it is, and saying so costs us a booking. A Grade 9 student who is coping does not need weekly sessions. What can be worth doing is a short diagnostic before subject choices are finalised, particularly in mathematics, where the gap between the two Diploma courses catches families out later. If that diagnostic shows nothing, stop. Adding a tutor to a student who is managing tends to reduce their independence rather than build it.

faqs.question: How does tutoring fit around the extended essay?
faqs.answer: A tutor can act as a sounding board while the student narrows a research question, discuss whether the sources will support the argument, and help build a drafting schedule that respects the school's internal deadlines. The supervisor at school remains the authority on the essay, and the writing must be the student's own under academic honesty rules. The most valuable contribution is usually early: a research question that is too broad wastes months that no amount of later editing recovers.

faqs.question: What if we start and the sessions turn out to be unnecessary?
faqs.answer: Then stop, and stop early. Some students settle after three or four sessions because the confidence problem was larger than the knowledge problem, and continuing out of caution wastes an evening a week. Tell the tutor and the advisor plainly. Arrangements are made between the family and the tutor, so ending or pausing is a conversation rather than a procedure. Restarting later is possible and depends on that tutor's availability at the time.

faqs.question: Are online sessions recorded, and can my child use the recordings?
faqs.answer: Recording depends on the individual tutor and on your agreement with them, so ask before the first session rather than after. Where recordings are available they help most with worked solutions in mathematics and the sciences, since a student can revisit a method at their own pace. They help far less with discussion-heavy subjects such as English A, where the value sits in the exchange itself and rewatching adds little.

faqs.question: Is a tutor near Sector 57 better than one further away in Gurugram?
faqs.answer: Only if the timing works out, and proximity is not evidence of teaching quality. A tutor in Sector 65 who has taught the exact Higher Level course you need is a better match than a neighbour in Sushant Lok 3 who has not, and the difference shows within a month. Distance matters for reliability, particularly for late slots, which is why families often keep a nearby tutor for the anchor session and go online for specialist subjects.

heroTitle: IB Tutors in Sushant Lok, Gurugram
heroSubtitle: Sushant Lok sits close to Golf Course Road and the central sectors, which makes home sessions easier to fill here than in most of the city. Online tutoring is available for every supported IB subject, Grade 1 through Grade 12, subject to tutor schedules.
introSummary: The short answer: IB tutors in Sushant Lok Gurugram can usually be arranged, from Grade 1 to Grade 12, at home or online, across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes. Home sessions here are among the easier ones to fill in the city, because most tutors working the Golf Course Road corridor pass through anyway. Online is available for every supported subject regardless of where the tutor lives. What decides whether the arrangement works is fit, not availability, and the sections below deal with that.

contentBlocks.heading: IB tutors in Sushant Lok, Gurugram: the short answer first
contentBlocks.body:
Yes, tutoring can be arranged here for all three IB programmes, at home or online, for children from Grade 1 through to the final Diploma year. Sushant Lok is central enough that a tutor living in the DLF phases, Sector 57 or the Sohna Road sectors can usually reach an address here without the journey eating half the session, so a fixed weekday slot is more achievable than it would be at the outer edges of the city.

That is the answer. The rest of this page is the part that decides whether the arrangement actually works.

Because what goes wrong is almost never availability. It is fit. A tutor who knows the subject but not the assessment. A slot booked at a time when the student is too tired to use it. A Higher Level requirement handed to somebody whose real experience stops at Standard Level. A plan that quietly ignores the school's own deadline calendar and then collides with it in week six.

So the sections below take those in order: how the match is made, which subjects need what, how the three programmes differ, where the area sits, which format to pick, and what screening covers before anyone is recommended.
items: All three programmes, Grade 1 to Grade 12
Home sessions realistic across most of Sushant Lok
Online available for every supported subject
Fit, not availability, is the usual failure point

contentBlocks.heading: How a Sushant Lok family goes from first call to first session
contentBlocks.body:
Six steps, and none of them take long.

One, a conversation about the student rather than the subject list: what the last set of results said, what the school has flagged, and where the student themselves thinks they are stuck. Two, the specifics: programme, year, subjects with Higher or Standard Level marked, and the deadlines that are near. Three, constraints, which for families here usually means a start time after the school bus gets back and before the evening runs out. Four, a shortlist of tutors matched on subject depth, level experience and familiarity with IB assessment. Five, a trial session. Six, a short written plan with a four-week review point.

The trial is the step worth protecting. It should not be a polished demonstration lesson. A useful trial has the tutor working through something the student has already got wrong, so you can watch how they handle confusion rather than how they perform when everything is going smoothly.

Availability depends on level and schedule. A tutor for MYP Mathematics on a Tuesday is straightforward. Higher Level Chemistry at half past eight in the evening in February is not.
items: Start with the student, not the subject list
Levels marked before any shortlist is drawn
Slot chosen around the school bus, not around the tutor
Trial built on a real error, not a set-piece topic
Written plan, four-week review point

contentBlocks.heading: Subjects most often requested by Sushant Lok students in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Math Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level generates the most requests, followed by Physics, Chemistry, Economics, English A, and Math Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level.

Worth knowing what each actually demands. In Math AA HL the difficulty is not the volume of content but Paper 3, which sets an extended problem the student has never seen and expects them to build towards a result across several linked parts. Math AI HL trades some of that abstraction for statistics, modelling and interpretation, so students who chose it hoping for an easier route are frequently surprised by how much writing it involves.

Physics and Chemistry each split into content teaching and internal assessment work, and those are sometimes two different tutors. An IA that is failing usually fails at the design stage: no genuine independent variable, or too few data points to say anything defensible.

Economics is mark-scheme sensitive. Diagrams have to be labelled and then referred to in the prose, and evaluation has to reach a judgement rather than list two views.

English A resists last-minute help more than any other subject. Paper 1 unseen commentary rewards a reading habit, and habits take months to build.
items: Math AA HL: Paper 3 extended problems, unfamiliar contexts
Math AI HL: statistics, modelling, written interpretation
Physics and Chemistry: content teaching versus IA design
Economics: labelled diagrams used inside the argument
English A: unseen commentary, individual oral, HL essay

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: three different jobs for a Sushant Lok tutor
contentBlocks.body:
A Primary Years Programme child, ages three to twelve, needs someone who can work inside inquiry rather than around it. The teaching is transdisciplinary and nothing is externally examined, so the job is confidence in reading, writing and number, delivered in short sessions connected to the unit the class is running now. A parent who wants an hour of drill worksheets is asking for something that will pull against the school.

A Middle Years Programme student, ages eleven to sixteen, needs someone fluent in criterion-related assessment. Four criteria per subject, published descriptors, marks awarded on best fit. Most MYP problems that look like subject weakness turn out to be a student answering a different question from the one the criterion asked.

A Diploma Programme student, ages sixteen to nineteen, needs a subject specialist and a calendar manager in the same person. Six subjects, three usually at Higher Level, an internal assessment in each, plus the extended essay, theory of knowledge and the creativity, activity, service commitment running alongside. Support for the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions is planned backwards from the paper dates, with earlier planning for younger cohorts who still have room to change direction.
items: PYP: inquiry-linked, no external examination
MYP: four criteria, descriptors, best-fit marking
DP: six subjects, IA in each, EE, TOK and CAS alongside
Planning runs backwards from May or November paper dates

contentBlocks.heading: Sushant Lok phases, Golf Course Road and the rest of central Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Sushant Lok runs in phases along the central spine of the city, with Phase 1 closest to the Galleria Market and Huda City Centre side, and Sushant Lok 3 sitting next to Sector 57 on the Golf Course Extension side. Golf Course Road, Sector 43, DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4 are all short distances away, and South City 1 and Sector 50 lie just to the south.

For tutoring this is close to the best position in the city. A tutor travelling from the DLF phases, Sector 57 or the Sohna Road sectors can reach most Sushant Lok addresses within about twenty minutes outside peak flow, which widens the pool of people able to offer a fixed weekday slot.

The metro matters more than parents expect. Tutors commuting from Delhi on the Yellow Line can reach Phase 1 addresses without a car, and that quietly adds specialists for the rarer Higher Level subjects who would otherwise be out of reach.

Home tutoring across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sector 57 and Sohna Road depends on tutor schedules. Online covers all of Gurugram without that constraint.
items: Phase 1 near Galleria Market and Huda City Centre
Sushant Lok 3 adjoining Sector 57
Short hops: Sector 43, DLF Phase 1, DLF Phase 4
Yellow Line access brings in Delhi-based specialists

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or a mix: what works in Sushant Lok, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Pick the format for the problem, not for the preference.

Home tutoring suits younger students, students who need supervision to begin work at all, and any situation where a parent wants to hear how the hour is going without asking afterwards. It also suits this area specifically, because travel is manageable from most directions.

Online tutoring suits Higher Level subjects, internal assessment sessions where both people need the same document open, revision blocks close to mocks, and any slot after eight in the evening. It also removes the commonest cause of a cancelled session, which is a tutor stuck somewhere on Golf Course Road.

Hybrid combines them, usually one of each per week.

The limitation nobody mentions: online exposes motivation. A student who is engaged will work well on a screen. A student who is being made to attend will find a screen far easier to hide behind than a person sitting beside them. If the honest problem is that your child does not want tuition at all, choose home sessions, keep them short, and expect the first month to be slow going.
items: Home: supervision, routine, younger learners
Online: HL specialists, IA drafts, post-eight slots
Hybrid: one of each per week is the common pattern
Reluctant student: home sessions, shorter, slower start

contentBlocks.heading: Schools Sushant Lok children commute to
contentBlocks.body:
Children living here attend several IB schools rather than one. Lancers International School on Golf Course Road is among the nearest. Scottish High International School in Sector 57 sits close to the Sushant Lok 3 end. Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School, further out in the Gurugram region and towards Sohna Road, mean longer bus journeys from this address.

Bus time changes what is realistic. A Diploma student spending ninety minutes a day on a school bus has fewer usable evening hours than a neighbour attending a school ten minutes away, and a tutoring plan that ignores this produces sessions where nothing is retained. The fix is usually a weekend morning for the heaviest subject and shorter weekday sessions for everything else.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. They are named because school-specific knowledge shortens the setup: internal deadline patterns, unit sequencing and mock timing all differ.

Ask any prospective tutor one simple question at the trial. What does the school calendar look like this term, and how will sessions sit around it. Vagueness there tends to predict how the next three months go.
items: Lancers International School, Golf Course Road
Scottish High International School, Sector 57
Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School, longer runs
Long bus days argue for weekend sessions on heavy subjects
Independent platform, no school endorsement implied

contentBlocks.heading: What screening covers before a Gurugram tutor is recommended
contentBlocks.body:
Screening answers four questions, and it helps to know which four.

Who are they. Identity and background verification, completed before any home session is arranged.

What have they taught. IB programmes, subjects, and crucially the levels, recorded separately. Higher Level experience is never inferred from Standard Level experience, because in Mathematics and the sciences those are different courses with different demands.

Do they know the assessment. A tutor is asked how they would take an internal assessment from research question through to evaluation, what a specific command term requires, and how criterion descriptors change what a strong answer looks like. This is where a lot of otherwise capable subject people come unstuck, and it is the check that matters most for IB work.

Can they teach a confused student. A short demonstration built on a genuine misconception rather than a clean topic they have prepared.

What screening cannot answer is whether this particular tutor will get on with your particular child. No process can. The trial session and the four-week review are how that gets tested, and both should be treated as real decision points rather than formalities.
items: Identity and background verified first
Subject and level recorded as separate facts
IA, command terms and descriptors probed directly
Demonstration on a misconception, not a prepared topic
Personal fit decided at the trial, not before it

contentBlocks.heading: Fees, cancellations and the questions Sushant Lok parents ask last
contentBlocks.body:
The questions that come at the end of a call are usually the ones that decide whether the arrangement survives past a term.

Fees vary by programme, level, subject and format. Higher Level Diploma subjects cost more than MYP support. Home sessions carry travel time inside the rate; online sessions do not. Ask for the per-session rate, the suggested weekly frequency and the resulting monthly commitment together, because a low hourly rate attached to four sessions a week is not the cheaper option.

Cancellation terms need to be stated before the first session and need to run in both directions. School trips, illness and internal examination weeks all create gaps, and a fair policy absorbs them without letting paid sessions quietly disappear.

Tutor changes should be possible without restarting the whole search, with the existing notes moving across to whoever comes next.

And the honest one. There is no guaranteed outcome on offer here. Grades are decided by external examiners on work produced under exam conditions. What tutoring changes is preparation, technique and the number of unforced errors. Anybody selling you a number in advance is selling something other than teaching.
items: Compare monthly totals, not hourly rates
Cancellation terms agreed in writing, both directions
Planned pauses for school exam weeks
Notes transfer if the tutor changes
No grade promises, from anyone

contentBlocks.heading: Arranging a first session in Sushant Lok
contentBlocks.body:
Arranging the first session takes one conversation. Have four things ready: the programme and year, the subjects with levels marked, the two evenings that are genuinely free, and the deadline that is worrying you most.

A shortlist can then be reviewed, subject to tutor availability, with home options checked against real travel into Sushant Lok at the hour you want rather than an average across the day. If a slot cannot be covered reliably, hearing that early is more useful than having it filled and then losing sessions to traffic in week four.

The trial follows. Watch for one thing above everything else: does the tutor find something specific the student was getting wrong, and can they say what they would do about it. General encouragement is easy to produce in an hour. A precise diagnosis is not, and it is the best early signal you will get.

After four weeks, ask for a short written update. If nothing has moved, ask why, and expect a straight answer about whether the issue is the match, the schedule, or something outside tutoring altogether.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor easy to arrange in Sushant Lok, or should we plan for online?
faqs.answer: Home tutoring is more achievable here than in most parts of the city, because the phases sit centrally and tutors working the Golf Course Road corridor already travel through. Even so, arrangement depends on the subject and the hour. Common subjects at reasonable times fill quickly. Rare Higher Level combinations, or slots after half past eight, are usually easier to cover online. Plan for home sessions as the first option and treat online as the widener rather than the fallback.

faqs.question: What should we ask a tutor during the trial session?
faqs.answer: Three questions, all after the session rather than before. What did you find that the student was getting wrong, stated specifically enough that you could repeat it back. What would the first month cover, and in what order. Is the deadline we are worried about realistic, and if not, what is the best achievable version of it. A tutor who answers all three concretely is showing you their diagnostic thinking. One who answers with reassurance is showing you something else.

faqs.question: Can tutoring start in the middle of DP2, close to final exams?
faqs.answer: It can, provided the objective shrinks to match the time left. In the last months before the papers, the gains available are in exam technique, timing, question interpretation, high-weight topics, and finishing whatever coursework is still open. Rebuilding a Higher Level course from its foundations is not available at that point, and a tutor who suggests otherwise is not being straight with you. Many families in this position get more from four intensive weeks than from a thin weekly slot stretched over three months.

faqs.question: Do you help with theory of knowledge and the extended essay?
faqs.answer: Both can be arranged, though neither runs like ordinary subject tuition. Theory of knowledge support clusters around the exhibition and later the prescribed title essay, where the usual problem is a student describing knowledge questions instead of arguing with them. Extended essay support works best as a few well-timed sessions: narrowing the question, sorting method and sources, then tightening the argument after supervisor feedback. Your school supervisor remains the formal authority on both, and a tutor should be working with that guidance.

faqs.question: Our child is in Grade 4 in PYP. Is a tutor even appropriate at that age?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the reason matters. A Grade 4 child who is behind on reading fluency, written expression or number confidence benefits from short, regular sessions with someone who works alongside the class inquiry. A child who is doing fine but whose parents want them ahead usually gains little and loses playing time. If a tutor proposes an hour of worksheets from another board's syllabus, that is the wrong help at this age, and it will pull against what the school is doing.

faqs.question: How do fees work for Higher Level subjects compared with MYP?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Diploma subjects generally carry higher rates, because the pool of tutors who have actually taught at that level is smaller and the preparation each session requires is greater. Internal assessment and extended essay mentoring are often priced separately from ordinary teaching, since they involve reading and annotating drafts between sessions. MYP support usually sits lower. Ask for the full picture before committing: rate, session length, weekly frequency, and how draft reading is charged.

faqs.question: What happens after four weeks if nothing has improved?
faqs.answer: Ask for it in writing before deciding anything. A tutor should be able to name what the blocker is: a foundation gap that is deeper than first thought, homework not being attempted between sessions, a slot too late in the evening to be useful, or a genuine mismatch of style. Each of those has a different remedy, and only one of them is a tutor change. Silence at week four is the real warning sign, more than slow progress itself.

faqs.question: Is IB tutoring different from CBSE or IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and this is where mismatches begin. IB assessment rewards concept-based understanding, criterion-related judgement and precise use of command terms, alongside coursework that carries real weight in the final grade. A tutor trained on a content-and-recall board can teach the topic accurately and still leave a student writing answers that score poorly against IB descriptors. Subject knowledge transfers between systems. Assessment literacy does not, which is why it is checked separately during screening.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two subjects, or do we need two people?
faqs.answer: It depends on the pairing and the level. Physics with Mathematics, or Economics with Business Management, are combinations plenty of tutors handle credibly. Two Higher Level sciences, or a science paired with English A, usually means one of the two gets a shallower service. There is also a practical benefit to splitting: two tutors give you two independent readings of how your child is working, and they rarely agree completely, which is often the most useful information you get.

contentBlocks.heading: Study Habits First: What Actually Moves Marks Near Udyog Vihar
contentBlocks.body:
Ask a DP student near Udyog Vihar how they revise and the honest answer is usually re-reading notes at 11 pm. That habit feels productive and is close to useless for an assessment model built on applying concepts to unseen material.

The habits that hold up are stage-specific. A PYP child needs twenty minutes of reading that is not homework, and a parent willing to ask one open question about it. An MYP student needs to open the criterion strands before starting an assignment, not after getting it back. A DP student needs a weekly plan with two fixed slots for the subject they avoid, because the avoided subject is where marks quietly leak away.

Study habits are also why tutor selection matters more than tutor credentials. A tutor who teaches beautifully but leaves no system behind produces good sessions and a flat report. The ones who help most spend the first few sessions building a routine the student can run alone, then start using session time for the harder teaching.

So when families around this corridor describe what they want, the useful brief is not someone strong in Physics. It is someone who will get a Grade 11 student to plan a week and hold to it, and who happens to be strong in Physics.

IB tutors in Udyog Vihar Gurugram are matched with that order of priorities in mind.

PYP: twenty minutes of reading that is not homework
MYP: read the strands before starting, not after
DP: fixed weekly slots for the avoided subject
Early sessions build the routine, later ones teach

contentBlocks.heading: Which IB Subjects Families Around Udyog Vihar Ask About
contentBlocks.body:
The enquiry mix along this corridor leans heavily towards DP mathematics and the sciences, with English A appearing later in DP1 once the first oral is announced.

Math AA HL requests usually arrive after the first calculus test. What the student needs is rarely more chapters; it is algebraic fluency that should have become automatic two years earlier, which is a slower fix than parents expect. Math AI HL requests look different. They tend to come from students who chose AI for sound reasons and then met the statistics and modelling papers, where the difficulty is reading a scenario and deciding which tool applies.

Physics and Chemistry enquiries split neatly by month. Before October the question is content. After October it is the internal assessment, and sessions become supervision of a method rather than teaching of a topic.

Economics comes up for the long evaluation question and for commentary selection, since a badly chosen news article limits the marks available before a word is written.

English A requests are the quietest and often the most useful, because reading speed and essay structure improve everything else on the timetable.

An IB maths tutor Udyog Vihar families can book on a weekday and an IB science tutor at higher level are usually two different people. Asking for one who covers both narrows the shortlist sharply.

Physics and Chemistry: content first, IA after October

contentBlocks.heading: PYP Curiosity, MYP Criteria, DP Deadlines
contentBlocks.body:
The three programmes look different from the dining table, which is where most parents form their view of how school is going.

In the Primary Years Programme, ages 3 to 12, there is very little to check. No marks to speak of, homework that looks like a project, and a child who either talks about the unit of inquiry or does not. Tutoring here is mostly reading fluency, number confidence and keeping the questioning alive. A tutor drilling worksheets on a PYP student is quietly undoing the programme.

In the Middle Years Programme, ages 11 to 16, reports start arriving with numbers out of eight against four criteria, and they confuse almost everyone the first time. A 5 in Criterion C is not sixty-two percent. Tutoring at this stage is largely about teaching a student to read the descriptor, plan against it, and self-assess before submitting anything.

In the Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19, everything becomes visible at once and usually all at the same time. Six subjects, three at higher level, TOK, CAS and the Extended Essay, on dates that do not move.

Families near Udyog Vihar with children at two of these stages often need two different kinds of tutor, and it saves a fortnight to say so at the enquiry stage.
items: PYP ages 3 to 12: little to measure, much to protect
MYP ages 11 to 16: four criteria, each out of eight
MYP marks are descriptive bands, not percentages
DP ages 16 to 19: six subjects plus TOK, CAS, EE
Two stages at home usually means two tutors

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid Around the NH-48 Corridor
contentBlocks.body:
Udyog Vihar is a work address. The students live around it, in Heritage City, the DLF Phase 3 residences, Ambience Caitriona and the sectors that back onto NH-48, which changes the tutoring arithmetic considerably.

IB home tuition in Udyog Vihar Gurugram is possible and can be arranged subject to tutor availability, but the honest constraint is the 6 pm to 8 pm window. That is when the office corridor empties towards Delhi and the service roads stop being a shortcut. A tutor who agrees to a 7 pm home slot in September is often the tutor who starts arriving at 7 25 by November, and that slow erosion is what ends arrangements.

Two workarounds hold up. The first is a later home slot, 8 pm onwards, which suits DP students and almost never suits a Grade 5. The second is online on weekdays with home visits on weekend mornings.

An IB online tutor in Udyog Vihar Gurugram removes the constraint entirely and widens the specialist pool to tutors sitting in Delhi or Noida. The cost is attention management for younger students, plus a dependence on the connection holding during a live drafting session.

Hybrid is what most families here settle into without ever planning to.

contentBlocks.heading: From Enquiry to First Session: The Steps IB Gram Follows
contentBlocks.body:
The sequence is short, and knowing it prevents the two-week wait that comes from an incomplete first message.

Day one is the enquiry. The details that speed everything up are grade, programme, subject and level, the school, the area you live in rather than the office you work near, and the evenings that are genuinely free. Day one or two is a call, mostly to find out what has already been tried, because a family on their third tutor needs a different shortlist from a family on their first.

Next comes the filter. Tutors are considered against the specific level rather than the subject label, and against the slot rather than the general week. A tutor free at 5 pm is no use to a student who reaches home at 6 30.

Then a shortlist, small and reasoned, usually with one home option and one online option so the trade-off is visible rather than assumed.

A first session follows, and it is meant to be judged. Ask the student one question afterwards: did the tutor explain, or did they solve? The answer predicts the next three months better than any qualification on the profile.

Fees, frequency and the review point are settled after that session, not before it.

Filtered on level and on the actual slot

contentBlocks.heading: What IB Gram Checks Before Sending You a Tutor Profile
contentBlocks.body:
Four questions decide whether a tutor reaches a shortlist at all.

Are they who they say they are? Identity and qualification documents are collected and matched against the profile. A certificate that does not match the claimed university is where most screening ends quietly.

Have they taught this programme, at this level? Teaching a subject and teaching it inside the Diploma Programme are different skills, and the second is what gets checked. For MYP, the question is whether they have marked against criteria rather than out of a hundred.

Can they mark? A short subject conversation built around a past paper answer usually settles it. A tutor who can say why an answer earned four marks instead of six understands the assessment model. One who says the answer looks fine does not.

Will they hold the academic honesty line? Every tutor is expected to coach through questioning and parallel examples, and to refuse when a student asks for an internal assessment to be rewritten. That refusal protects the diploma even when it makes the tutor briefly unpopular.

Parent feedback across the first month decides whether they keep getting recommended. Vague session summaries and repeated lateness end it faster than a weak subject answer would.
items: Documents matched against the profile shown to you
Programme and level history, not subject name
A marking discussion on a real past paper answer
Refusal to rewrite an internal assessment
First-month feedback decides continued recommendation

Lancers International School on Golf Course Road is the closest of the four schools families here mention most, and the run back from it is manageable on an ordinary evening. That last case is the clearest argument for online weekday sessions. A student who spends two hours a day on a bus has very little appetite for a tutor at the door at 7 pm, and the session that gets booked anyway is the one that gets cancelled in November.

contentBlocks.heading: Four Weeks In: The Signals Worth Watching
contentBlocks.body:
Judge the arrangement on behaviour before you judge it on marks. Behaviour changes first, and it changes in ways a parent can see without asking the tutor anything.

The student starts homework before being told twice. Questions get more specific, moving from I do not understand Physics to I do not understand why the uncertainty is added here. A draft exists a week before it is due rather than the night before. The student can explain, unprompted, what the last session covered.

The reverse signals are just as readable. Sessions that always run over suggest poor planning. A student who goes quiet after every session may be being lectured at rather than taught. Work completed suspiciously fast is worth opening and reading.

Marks are the slowest signal and the least reliable at four weeks, because school reporting cycles do not run at the speed of tutoring. No one can guarantee a grade in an externally assessed programme, and a tutor who offers one has told you something useful about themselves.

If nothing has shifted, ask for a diagnosis rather than more hours. Adding a fourth session to a week that cannot hold three is the most common wrong response, and it usually ends in cancelled slots.

Drafts appear days ahead of the deadline

contentBlocks.heading: Send One Subject and One Deadline to Start
contentBlocks.body:
A useful enquiry fits in four lines. The grade and programme. The subject and, for DP, the level. The nearest deadline, whether that is an internal assessment, a mock or a school assignment. And the residential area, because a tutor is matched to where the student sleeps rather than where a parent works.

From there the request is checked against tutors currently taking students near this corridor, with home, online and hybrid all considered rather than one assumed. Availability depends on level and schedule, and the late evening slots in DP subjects go earliest in the term, so an enquiry made a few weeks before a deadline gives a much wider choice than one made a few days before.

The shortlist that follows is small and comes with reasons attached. A first session confirms the fit, and fees and frequency are settled after that session rather than in advance of it.

If the match is wrong, say so early. The second shortlist is almost always better than the first, because it has more information to work with.

One more thing worth putting in the first message: whether anyone at home can sit in for the opening weeks. For a primary or early middle years student that single detail often decides whether an online slot is workable at all, and it changes the shortlist more than the subject does.

faqs.question: Is Udyog Vihar itself a residential area for IB students?
faqs.answer: Mostly not. Udyog Vihar is an office and industrial corridor along NH-48, so the students who search for tutors here generally live in the residential pockets around it: the DLF Phase 3 residences, Heritage City, Ambience Caitriona and the sectors nearby. This matters for tutoring because the home address decides travel time, not the landmark used in the search. When you enquire, give the residential area and the nearest main road. A tutor planning an evening route needs that far more than a locality name pulled from a map.

faqs.question: What is a realistic home tutoring slot near the Cyber City corridor?
faqs.answer: Anything before 6 pm is comfortable and rarely useful, since most students are not home yet. Between 6 and 8 the corridor is at its slowest, and a tutor coming from Delhi or from the Golf Course Road side may lose half an hour to it. After 8 pm the roads clear and the slot becomes practical, though it only suits older students. Weekend mornings are the easiest to hold consistently across a term. Availability can be reviewed for any of these, but a slot that is honest about traffic survives much longer.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come from Delhi or Noida for home sessions here?
faqs.answer: Some do, because the highway connection is genuinely good outside peak hours and this is one of the easier parts of Gurugram to reach from Delhi. The arrangement holds when the slot is late or on a weekend, and it breaks when the tutor is trying to arrive at 7 pm on a weekday. For a specialist subject where the right person happens to live across the border, online is usually the more durable answer. It removes the single point of failure that a long commute always represents.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP Grade 9 and the report has numbers out of eight. How should I read them?
faqs.answer: Each criterion is marked out of eight and the bands are descriptive rather than proportional. A 5 does not mean sixty-two percent; it means the work matched a particular descriptor band for that strand. Two subjects can both show a 5 and need completely different fixes. The practical step is to read the descriptor for the band above and identify the single thing missing, which is usually specificity, use of subject terminology, or evaluation where the student only described. A tutor should be able to point at that gap within one session.

faqs.question: Do you have tutors for both Math AA and Math AI at higher level?
faqs.answer: Both are supported, and they are matched separately because they are separate courses. AA at higher level needs someone comfortable with proof, calculus depth and algebraic manipulation. AI at higher level needs someone who works confidently with statistics, modelling and technology, and who can teach the interpretation the papers reward. A tutor genuinely strong in one is not automatically the right choice for the other. Tell us which course the school has assigned, since that alone removes half the guesswork from the shortlist.

faqs.question: How early before the May 2026 session should we start?
faqs.answer: For a DP2 student, the useful window opens around September of the preceding year, because that is when internal assessments are still movable. Starting in January is worth doing, but the plan narrows to exam technique and past papers rather than repairing coursework. For a DP1 student looking further ahead, the highest-value work now is subject fluency and habit building, which is unglamorous and pays more than early exam drilling. November 2026 candidates follow the same logic on a shifted calendar.

faqs.question: We tried a tutor last year and it did not help. What should we do differently?
faqs.answer: Say that at the enquiry stage, and say what specifically failed. Pace too fast, explanations that were really just solutions, unreliable timing, or a level mismatch are four different problems with four different fixes. A second shortlist built with that information is usually much better than the first. It also helps to change one variable rather than all of them. contentBlocks.heading: What Should Actually Happen in the First Session
contentBlocks.body: A first session with an IB tutor in Banjara Hills should feel more like a diagnosis than a demonstration. If a tutor spends the entire hour teaching a chapter without first asking what unit the school is on, what the last assessed piece looked like, or where the student got stuck, that is a signal to be cautious. What should come out of a proper first session is specific: which command terms the student consistently misreads, whether a Math AA problem falls apart at setup or at execution, whether an Economics paragraph has the right structure but weak evaluation, or, for a younger PYP learner, whether reading fluency or comprehension is the actual blocker. IB tutoring only works well when it respects concept-based learning and criterion-related assessment rather than treating every subject as content to memorise and repeat. Academic honesty matters here too, especially at MYP and DP level: a tutor should be building the student's own thinking, correcting method and explaining criteria, not producing assessed work on the student's behalf, since that only postpones a problem that resurfaces at the next paper or IA draft. By the end of a good first session, a parent should have three things in hand: a plain description of the actual gap, not a vague 'needs more practice'; a short list of what the next two or three sessions will target; and an honest read on whether home tutoring near Road No. 12 or Masab Tank, online sessions, or a hybrid mix makes more sense given the student's schedule.

Biology tutoring covers the same practical-plus-theory balance as the other sciences, and English A support ranges from literary analysis structure to the close reading skills a Paper 1 unseen text demands. contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP — Different Work Even Within the Same Family
contentBlocks.body: A single Banjara Hills household often has children spread across two different IB stages at once, and it helps to be clear about what actually changes between them. The Primary Years Programme, roughly ages 3 to 12, runs on units of inquiry and portfolio-based assessment, with no internal assessments or timed papers — tutoring here looks like reading support, number sense and help with a unit's central idea, and Banjara Hills specifically sees a steady stream of exactly this kind of request. The Middle Years Programme, ages 11 to 16, introduces criterion-related assessment: a student's work gets graded against specific criteria depending on the subject, and a tutor's job shifts toward helping a student understand what a criterion actually rewards, not just getting the content right. The Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19, adds internal assessments, an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, and the pressure of May and November exam sessions, with mock exams typically run some months before the real thing. A tutor working with a DP student in Banjara Hills is usually managing several of these at once — IA structure, EE mentoring, TOK support, and past-paper revision — while a younger sibling three rooms away needs something as simple as steadier reading practice. Treating both as 'IB tutoring' in the same breath undersells how different the actual work is.

contentBlocks.heading: Two Very Different Reasons Parents Search for an IB Tutor in HITEC City
contentBlocks.body:
Two kinds of parents land on this page, and they need different things. The first has a Diploma Programme student with a mock exam ten days away and a Math or Physics topic the student has quietly avoided for a month; the search is really about who can fix this by Friday. The second is looking further out, often at the start of a term or academic year, wanting a tutor who will sit with the student through an entire Primary Years, Middle Years or Diploma Programme cycle rather than parachute in for a crisis.

Both are legitimate reasons to look for an IB tutor near HITEC City, but they change what a first session should look like. Exam-season firefighting means triage: identify the two or three weakest topics, drill past papers, and accept that some gaps will not close in ten days. Year-long support means something slower: building a working relationship with the student's actual teacher-set assignments, tracking IA progress across months, and catching a struggling topic before it becomes a mock-week emergency.

HITEC City families near Madhapur and Cyber Towers ask for both kinds of support, often within the same household across different children or different years. IB Gram treats the two requests differently from the first message, because a tutor good at one is not automatically good at the other.

contentBlocks.body:
The matching process starts with the same handful of questions whether the request is urgent or long-term: the programme level, the specific subject or subjects, whether the need is a Higher Level gap or a broader review, and how many weeks are actually available before the next assessment. For an urgent HITEC City request, availability is checked first, since a mock exam ten days out narrows the realistic tutor pool quickly; a specialist who is excellent but only free on weekends is not a fit if sessions need to happen three evenings a week.

For a year-long request, the process slows down deliberately. A tutor's subject depth, prior experience with the specific programme level, and comfort with command-term marking are checked more carefully, because the relationship needs to hold up over months, not just get a student through one paper.

Either way, matches are suggested based on checked criteria and current availability, not guaranteed, since a particular subject-level-schedule combination may not have a free tutor in a given week. A first session is diagnostic in both cases: for the urgent request, it identifies which of the weak topics is actually fixable in the time left; for the year-long request, it sets a baseline the tutor and parent can return to later.

contentBlocks.heading: Subjects Families Near HITEC City Ask About Most
contentBlocks.body:
Math shows up first in most HITEC City requests, split fairly evenly between AA HL for students aiming at engineering or quantitative degrees and AI HL for students who prefer applied statistics and modelling over pure proof. Physics and Chemistry follow closely, often requested together by DP students keeping both sciences open for university applications, and Biology comes up for students who have not yet locked their final science combination.

Economics is common among HITEC City's technology and business-family households, particularly for essay technique and paper structure rather than content alone; a student can know the theory and still lose marks for a poorly structured extended-response answer. English A support tends to focus on written commentary and paper technique, a skill set closer to Economics essay marking than to Math, though families rarely think of it that way until a tutor points it out.

What matters for HITEC City specifically is depth at the HL level. A general subject tutor can usually manage SL content, but Higher Level Math, Physics or Economics needs someone who has actually taught that specific level before, not simply a strong graduate in the subject. IB Gram checks for that distinction rather than assuming a subject match is automatically a level match.

contentBlocks.heading: From PYP Reading Support to DP Exam Pressure
